## 8. Open questions / gaps

**Completeness caveat.**
- OSM is uneven. West of Pokrovsk almost no belts are mapped: they exist only as the gaps between farmland polygons, which the imagery shows follow the belts closely. In the best boxes about two-thirds of the belts visible in Sentinel-2 are mapped, so belt densities and OSM spacings are lower bounds and upper bounds respectively.
- OSM buildings are 1–18% complete, so building counts must come from Microsoft footprints, not OSM.
- The Sentinel-2 detector works only in clean grids. Crop stripes, tracks and (south of Chasiv Yar) wartime earthworks cause false detections.
- The imagery is from 2021 and so shows the pre-invasion landscape.
- Farmland polygons sometimes split one belt block into several fields, which biases field sizes low.

- **Sub-phases (IDs unchanged).** The e6 and e8 splits are supported and described in §3. For e9, a split at about Jun/Jul 2026 fits better than one at Vivaldi. Note the e5/e6 overlap in Oct–Nov 2023, and that e9 in practice starts on 29 Jan 2026, not 1 Feb.
- **Weapon dates still missing:**
  - NLAW's first delivery (UK, reportedly Jan 2022).
  - Abrams' and HIMARS' first combat-use dates.
  - Patriot's first intercept (the claimed Kinzhal kill of 4 May 2023). Ukrainska Pravda's 5 May item is an initial Air Force denial, and ISW's 6–7 May 2023 pages did not mention it.

  - Oryx per-country F-16 attribution is approximate.

  - Reuters' "600 km² by 8 Jun" figure (Syrskyi) could not be fetched (401) and is dropped.

- **US peace plan, Sep 2026.** CSMonitor says Zelensky rejected it. ISW says he agreed "fundamental principles" on 6 Sep. The plan's text has not been published.
- **Iran war and the negotiation calendar.** Reports that the war postponed an Abu Dhabi/US-hosted round in March 2026 could not be confirmed from a fetched source. The exact start date of the war is also not independently sourced here.

  - a Trump-announced version of the May truce (ISW reports it as agreed between Kyiv and Moscow);
  - the Mediazona excess-mortality estimate (~352k);
  - Vivaldi phase-3 claims (2,000 Russian losses, 250+ POWs).

  - the prelude, the Kharkiv 2022 and 2024 details, Kursk 2024, Avdiivka glide-bomb and shell ratios, North Korea, and Spiderweb's independent damage estimates;
  - the Sting production figures, the 2022 mobilization and 2026 conscription, and the Jan 2026 Abu Dhabi round.

- **Starlink cut-off (about 1 Feb 2026).** Russian units used Starlink to relay drone feeds (including strike drones reaching about 80 km) and Telegram to pass coordinates and coordinate air defence. Losing both makes their sensor-to-shooter chain less efficient but does not collapse C2 [src:carnegie-2026-kolomychenko-starlink-telegram]. This coincides with Ukraine's counteroffensive in the south.
- **Fires in the counteroffensive (from 29 Jan–9 Feb; see 00 §3 e9).** Ukraine's gains in the south rested less on tube artillery than on shaping fires. A SEAD/DEAD campaign opened Russian-held airspace. From spring 2026 an intermediate-range drone campaign hit fuel trucks, rail tankers and freight trains on the M-14, M-18 and T-0509 (H-20) highways and rail lines, 100–160+ km behind the front. Ukrainian armour could then be pushed 19 km past Russian lines near Oleksandrivka in March. FP-2 drones began firing unguided S-8 rockets at operational depth in May 2026, in effect drone-borne rocket artillery. The 7th Corps now tasks drone sorties specifically against Russian guns and drone launch sites. Russia's rate of advance fell to 2.9 km² a day in January–April 2026, excluding infiltrated areas, from 9.76 a year earlier [src:isw-2026-barros-intermediate-range-strikes]. ATACMS played almost no part: Ukraine's stock was "severely depleted" [src:kyivindependent-2026-farrell-atacms-iran].
- **Russian glide-bomb response.** KAB use rose throughout the counteroffensive. January is given as 5,171 (Air Force data via Kyiv Post) [src:kyivpost-2026-korshak-glide-bombs] or more than 5,700 (MoD), with a record 316 on 18 January [src:united24-2026-mykhailenko-january-kabs]. February was a record at the time, and March reached 7,987, more than 1,500 above it [src:ukrinform-2026-march-kabs]. April was nearly 7,000 and May about 7,500 [src:united24-2026-may-kabs]. June reached 8,266, with 391 bombs in 127 sorties (about 3 per sortie) on 13 June [src:kyivpost-2026-korshak-glide-bombs]. July brought 8,300+ [src:defenseexpress-2026-syngaivska-july-kabs] and August 8,766, or 283 a day. That is more than the 211–237 guided bombs a day the US dropped on Iran in Operation Epic Fury [src:militarnyi-2026-pryhodko-kabs-us-campaigns]. Kyiv Post projects about 100,000 more by mid-2027 [src:kyivpost-2026-korshak-glide-bombs]. Targets included bridges on the Pokrovsk–Kostyantynivka H-20 highway, hit with FAB-3000 and Kh-38 (February), and the Kramatorsk and Slovyansk agglomeration [src:isw-2026-02-12-assessment]. By late September, strikes in the Kramatorsk direction were intensifying, partly to leave ruins that Russian infiltrators use as cover [src:isw-2026-09-26-assessment].
- **Russian tube and rocket fire (Ukrainian counts of strike events, not rounds).** More than 113,000 attacks and 2,400 MLRS strikes in January 2026 [src:united24-2026-mykhailenko-january-kabs]. More than 115,000 artillery strikes, including 2,834 by MLRS, in March [src:ukrinform-2026-march-kabs]. Nearly 97,000 attacks and 1,300+ MLRS strikes in July [src:defenseexpress-2026-syngaivska-july-kabs]. Russian artillery brigades and regiments now field their own drone operators; ISW's order-of-battle notes name the 288th Artillery Brigade, for example [src:isw-2026-02-12-assessment].
- **Ukrainian glide bombs.** A domestic 250 kg glide bomb with a range of about 40 km, carried by the Su-24, was cleared in May 2026. Ukraine receives only "a few dozen" Western glide bombs a month [src:euromaidanpress-2026-axe-ukrainian-glide-bomb]. ISW links its use to the SEAD campaign, which lets Ukrainian jets fly closer and higher [src:isw-2026-barros-intermediate-range-strikes].
- **Ballistic pressure and the Patriot gap.**
  - Launches: 91 ballistic missiles in January 2026, in salvos of up to 30, with at least 2 Iskander-M built a day [src:euromaidanpress-2026-mukhina-ballistic-salvo]. A record 121 followed in February [src:frontliner-2026-zvirynskyi-strike-intensity], then 195 in July [src:united24-2026-mykhailenko-july-strikes]. Zelensky counts more than 2,100 missiles in 2026 to late September, over 950 of them ballistic [src:twz-2026-altman-vivaldi]. Ukrainian officials put Russian output at about 120 ballistic missiles a month, and the Atlantic Council expects more than 1,000 launches in 2026 [src:atlanticcouncil-2026-kuskevics-patriot].
  - Intercept rates depend on the counter and the salvo. CSIS's 10.2% is its 2026 dataset share (to mid-July) [src:csis-2026-jensen-two-strategic-attacks]. The MoD's monthly figures give about 40% in June, when 11 of 41 were downed on 2 June and about half on 15 June [src:euromaidanpress-2026-mukhina-ballistic-tripled], and 29 of 195 (15%) in July [src:united24-2026-mykhailenko-july-strikes]. In the first week of July only 4 of 49 were stopped [src:atlanticcouncil-2026-kuskevics-patriot], and none of 29 on the night of 6 July [src:euronews-2026-vakulina-zero-intercepts]. Air Force spokesman Ihnat: "We have enough systems, but what we need is a steady supply of missiles" [src:euronews-2026-vakulina-zero-intercepts]. Each ballistic missile typically takes 2–3 Patriot interceptors [src:euromaidanpress-2026-mukhina-ballistic-tripled].
  - **The US–Iran war**, from February 2026, reportedly consumed up to 1,430 Patriot rounds in 39 days [src:atlanticcouncil-2026-kuskevics-patriot]. Gulf states fired more than 1,100, and nearly a third of global Patriot stocks were used [src:euronews-2026-vakulina-zero-intercepts]. US ATACMS and PrSM stocks were also "badly depleted" (Reuters, which the White House denies) [src:kyivindependent-2026-farrell-atacms-iran]. Lockheed makes about 620–650 PAC-3 MSE a year, rising towards 2,000 under a January 2026 contract [src:twz-2026-altman-vivaldi] [src:atlanticcouncil-2026-kuskevics-patriot]. Ukraine bought 70 ATACMS from Turkey in August 2026 [src:kyivindependent-2026-rushton-ballistic-gap].
  - Oreshnik struck Lviv on 8 Jan 2026 and was used twice on 24 May 2026 [src:wikipedia-oreshnik].
- **Jet Gerans.** The Geran-5 debuted on 11 Jan 2026: about 1,000 km range, 90 kg warhead, air-launchable from the Su-25, with optional R-73 missiles [src:militarnyi-2026-pryhodko-geran-5]. Geran-3 and Geran-4, at about 500 km/h, are beyond current interceptor drones and complicate the work of mobile fire groups [src:frontliner-2026-zvirynskyi-strike-intensity]. Against the jets, Ihnat says, "mobile fire groups and anti-drone interceptors can no longer be relied upon" and scarce missiles must be used [src:pravda-2026-ihnat-jet-drones]. Gun defence is also fragile: on 1 Apr 2026 three of the eight guns in two Skynex batteries failed within minutes, and a Shahed got through [src:militarnyi-2026-khomenko-skynex-issues]. Zelensky counts 63,000 attack drones in January–August 2026, more than 7,700 of them jets [src:twz-2026-altman-vivaldi]. ISIS reconstructs jets at 57–62% of genuine Shahed/Geran use in August 2026 [src:isis-2026-anokhin-shahed-monthly-sep]. Zelensky, citing HUR, says North Korea has begun building Shahed-type drones with Russian help (claim) [src:euromaidanpress-2026-zoria-dprk-shaheds].
- **Shahed waves and who kills them.**
  - Volume and intercepts: a record 8,150 drones in May 2026, 35–40% of them decoys; the 2026 plan is about 60,000 attack UAVs plus 50,000 decoys [src:frontliner-2026-zvirynskyi-strike-intensity]. In July, 5,142 of 8,653 strike drones were downed (about 59%) [src:united24-2026-mykhailenko-july-strikes]. ISIS reconstructs a Shahed hit share of about 10–14% in July–August [src:isis-2026-anokhin-shahed-monthly-sep].
  - Intercept share: the MoD counted 7,476 of 8,150 Shahed-type launches intercepted in May 2026 (91.7%) [src:pravda-2026-sting-3000].
  - Who kills them, May 2026 (official claims): of more than 3,500 drones downed, Unmanned Systems Forces interceptors took more than 1,200 and army aviation helicopters more than 440 [src:kyivpost-2026-syrsky-may-interceptors]. The maker's claim for its Sting interceptor alone is more than 3,000 Shaheds and Gerberas in the same month [src:pravda-2026-sting-3000]. The counts cannot both be complete, so treat interceptor kill shares as a range. Beskrestnov ("Flash") says interceptors now kill about 50% of incoming Shahed-type drones, against about 10% in winter [src:kyivpost-2026-syrsky-may-interceptors]. Helicopters take up to 40% of drones in their designated zones, and one Navy Mi-8 crew downed 12 Shaheds in 3 h in March 2026 [src:pravda-2026-dotsenko-helicopters-drones].
  - Data caveat: from about 5 May 2026 the Air Force stopped consistently publishing Shahed counts, so monthly Shahed figures are reconstructions [src:isis-2026-anokhin-shahed-monthly-sep].
- **Ukrainian deep strike.** Flamingo hit the GRAU arsenal at Kotluban on 12 Feb 2026 [src:isw-2026-02-12-assessment]. On 20–21 Feb it holed a workshop roof at the Votkinsk missile plant, about 1,400 km away, about 20–25 m from the likely aimpoint [src:missilematters-2026-hoffmann-flamingo-votkinsk]. Cheboksary followed on 5 May and 10 Jun 2026 [src:rbc-2026-vialko-flamingo]. The maker claims 30 a month, with 210 planned. Independent counts find about 10 documented strikes since August 2025, salvos of 3–6 missiles every 3–8 weeks, and only a few that caused serious damage; the supply of AI-25 engines is the bottleneck [src:meduza-2026-flamingo-production] [src:rbc-2026-vialko-flamingo]. A Gripen deal was signed in May 2026 [src:wikipedia-ukrainian-air-force].
- **Operation Vivaldi** (Lyman, May–Sep 2026). This was a targeting operation more than an artillery one. According to the 3rd Corps, reconnaissance mapped Russian command nodes, which were then hit by kamikaze UGVs that heavy bomber drones dropped more than 10 km behind the line. Strikes on both ends of a diesel pipeline from Voronezh Oblast, which carried about half of the sector's fuel, forced 400 km truck runs. The repair base for the 20th Army was pushed back to Voronezh Oblast, and the Rubikon unit withdrew after losses (unit claims) [src:euromaidanpress-2026-zoria-vivaldi-targeting]. In the first phase, fires went into Russian ATV and motorcycle reinforcement runs and supply routes, stranding the infiltration groups, which were then cleared; EW and strikes on control posts degraded Russian C2 [src:isw-2026-09-26-assessment]. No source quantifies artillery, HIMARS or Ukrainian glide-bomb use in Vivaldi.

- **Radar-only diorama.** The map is the Azov basin at night, with track symbols and range rings. The player sees what Ukrainian radar and passive sensors see. The A-50 is itself a huge emitter, and passive cueing on its emissions is a sourced possibility [src:mwi-2024-mitchell-awacs-azov]. Each Ukrainian radar switch-on is a risk the player chooses.
- **Two different ambushes, two acts.**
  - **Act 1 (Patriot, January):** move a mobile battery to within about 15–25 km of the line [src:espreso-2024-defenseexpress-wandering-patriot], wait for the orbit, fire at the edge of the envelope and leave.
  - **Act 2 (S-200, February):** after Russia moves the orbit east [src:pravda-2024-ukdi-a50-redeploy], only a long-range, one-shot-and-hide weapon reaches it, and the crew must wait days [src:kyivpost-2024-tuzov-s200].
- **Win band.**
  - **Required:** both A-50 kills, on 14 Jan and 23 Feb.
  - **Bonus:** the Il-22M damaged.
  - **Debrief:** the contested fleet sizes (3/6 to 10) and the 160–300 km range claims.
  - **Fail states:** the battery found and struck, or the A-50 turning away as in autumn 2023 [src:babel-2024-perepechko-times-a50].
- **Pacing.** Long quiet waits (a week forward) are broken by a few minutes of engagement. Between the two kills, a glide-bomb pressure meter rises (Avdiivka falls on 17 Feb) [src:isw-2024-02-17-assessment], with the Su-34/Su-35 spree as interstitial targets [src:kyivpost-2024-orlova-six-aircraft-72h] [src:pravda-2024-february-13-aircraft].
- **Systemic payoff.** Killing or pushing back the A-50 should lower the effectiveness and boldness of Russian KAB carriers for a while [src:pravda-2024-romanenko-no-a50] [src:ukrinform-2024-ihnat-a50-sixth-day] and briefly reduce Azov tactical aviation [src:isw-2024-02-23-assessment]. Model this as a fading modifier, not a permanent one.
- **Russian AI levers.** Orbit distance versus coverage, which is the sourced trade-off [src:pravda-2024-ukdi-a50-redeploy]. Recalling strike packages when the AEW goes down [src:pravda-2024-petrenko-a50-five-aircraft]. Flares and evasive turns [src:twz-2024-newdick-second-a50].
- **The Kyiv vignette** plays as a short low-level dogfight-and-SAM tutorial with the "Ghost" debunk as its debrief [src:rusi-2022-bronk-russian-air-war] [src:kyivpost-2022-neplii-ghost-of-kyiv].
- **Coda.** The A-50s retreat to Ulyanovsk and Samara by 2026 [src:united24-2026-khomenko-a50u-patrols]. This links to Spiderweb (chapter 16), where an A-50 at Ivanovo is a target [src:kyivpost-2025-spiderweb-a50-ivanovo].

**Defining features.** A slow, artillery-heavy Russian advance city by city, with very heavy Ukrainian casualties. The original invasion force proved too small to cover the whole front, which set up e3 [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].

section: 4. Forces / Russia (Black Sea Fleet and supporting aviation)

markdown:
**Terrain and structures.**
- **Harbour defences.** Sevastopol was layered with nets, floating booms and a chain of barges. Other harbours were too, and so was the Kerch Bridge after Jul 2023 [src:navalnews-2023-sutton-russia-adapts].
- **Where to strike.** Budanov judged Sevastopol and Novorossiysk "comprehensive but [able to] be overcome" defences. He preferred to catch ships at sea, on duty or moving [src:pravda-2024-romaniuk-magura-target-eliminate].
- **The corridor** runs inside the territorial waters of Ukraine and its neighbours [src:hromadske-2024-ryzhenko-bsf]. The first ship hugged the coast toward Romania [src:maritimeexec-2023-joseph-schulte].
**The outcome the player must reproduce**
## 10. Game/sim relevance

**Ukraine (Air Force Command, HUR)**
- **Command.** Commander-in-Chief Gen. Valerii Zaluzhnyi; Air Force Commander Lt. Gen. Mykola Oleshchuk; spokesman Col. Yurii Ihnat; HUR chief Lt. Gen. Kyrylo Budanov, with spokesman Andrii Yusov [src:isw-2024-01-15-assessment] [src:pravda-2024-romanenko-second-a50].
- **Patriot.** The first batteries arrived in April 2023 [src:oryx-heavy-weaponry-supplied-ukraine], and Germany's second system had deployed by December 2023 [src:militarnyi-2023-kushnikov-three-su34]. By mid-2024 the US estimated "about a battalion" in Ukraine, some guarding static sites and some highly mobile. The German truck-mounted systems were the ones used to ambush the first A-50, after German–Ukrainian night mobility drills in Poland in April 2023 [src:twz-2024-newdick-patriot-a50-confirmed]. The same arm claimed the 13 May 2023 Bryansk kills [src:liga-2023-dzheripa-bryansk-patriot]. Patriot launchers can fire remotely, well forward of the radar and control station [src:mwi-2024-mitchell-awacs-azov].
- **S-200.** A Soviet 1960s long-range SAM, restored from May 2022 by recalled operators and engineers [src:babel-2024-perepechko-times-a50] and credited with the second A-50 and a Tu-22M3 at 308 km [src:kyivpost-2024-tuzov-s200]. A Russian court names the 138th Anti-Aircraft Missile Brigade and its commander, Col. Mykola Dzyaman [src:kyivpost-2024-dzyaman-court].
- **S-300.** The legacy force: in 2022, 35 S-300PS/PT divisions, 3 S-300V, 9 S-125 and 15 Buk-M1 [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons]. By The Times's account, S-300 radars were used as bait [src:babel-2024-perepechko-times-a50].
- **Fighters.** MiG-29 and Su-27 (the 40th Tactical Aviation Brigade over Kyiv in 2022) [src:kyivpost-2022-neplii-ghost-of-kyiv]. In 2024 they had no long-range air-to-air missile that could reach the A-50 [src:wikipedia-2024-a50-il22-shootdowns], and the F-16 arrived only in August 2024 [src:kyivindependent-2024-court-f16]. Su-24Ms struck Crimea and may have shaped the January geometry (Cooper's hypothesis) [src:nexta-2024-cooper-a50-trap].

Act 2 begins on 13 Apr. A Ukrainian Navy coastal battery in southern Odesa Oblast fired two R-360 Neptune missiles at the *Moskva*, the Black Sea Fleet flagship and its long-range air-defence umbrella, about 120 km offshore. Low cloud hid the ship from aircraft and satellites; the battery's ordinary radar reached it anyway, apparently ducted under that cloud [src:pravda-2022-romaniuk-moskva-neptune] [src:zavhorodnii-2025-battles-snake-island]. A satellite radar image at 18:52 caught the burning ship at 45°10′43″N 30°55′31″E, about 80 nmi south of Odesa [src:navalnews-2022-sutton-moskva-sar]. Russia blamed a fire and an ammunition explosion and said the ship sank under tow "in stormy sea" on 14 Apr [src:reuters-2022-moskva-sunk]. The US confirmed the two Neptunes [src:dod-2022-04-18-background-briefing] [src:nbc-2022-dilanian-us-intel-moskva].

## 2. Per-era notes

- **Air-bridge dates.** Only mission 1 (21 Mar), mission 3 (28 Mar) and the last flight (5 Apr, per Serbov) are dated. Missions 2, 4, 5 and 6 are not. TWZ's "around the middle of May" for the last sorties conflicts with the 5 Apr account and with GUR's figure of seven missions [src:twz-2022-altman-flint-helicopter-rescue] [src:rbc-2026-honcharova-serbov-interview].
- **Helicopter losses.**
  - Counts differ: 2 shot down plus a rescue helicopter (Budanov) [src:twz-2022-altman-mariupol-helicopter-missions]; 1 destroyed and 2 "missing" officially (Flint) [src:twz-2022-altman-flint-helicopter-rescue]. Time describes two Mi-8s damaged on mission 6 that crash-landed on friendly ground [src:time-2024-spencer-collins-mariupol-helicopters].
  - Crew deaths are unknown: Zelensky said 90% of the pilots did not return [src:pravda-2022-mazurenko-azovstal-weapons-delivery], while Time documents no crew deaths.
  - Wikipedia's "six helicopters shot down overall" is unsourced here [src:wikipedia-siege-of-mariupol].
- **Distance error.** Time's "82 km" from Dnipro to Mariupol is wrong; the straight-line distance is about 233 km [src:osm-nominatim-c03-places].
- **FAB-3000.** Use against Azovstal is reported but not confirmed by Ukrainian or Western sources fetched for this dossier.
- **Garrison numbers.** The strength at Azovstal by date, killed in action, and the size of each unit are not documented in Ukrainian primary sources reviewed here.
- **Civilians.** The number of civilians in the plant is uncertain ("hundreds" to about 1,000). The total civilians evacuated from Azovstal across both operations is unclear; the UP total of about 567 includes people from the wider city.
- **Russian losses** are only claimed (6,500 killed, per Ukraine).
- **Olenivka toll:** 50+ (UN, 2023), 51 (UN, Oct 2023), 54 (RFE/RL), 57 (Kyiv Independent) [src:un-news-2023-olenivka-justice] [src:kyivpost-2023-afp-olenivka-not-himars] [src:rferl-2025-peretiatko-azovstal-captivity] [src:kyivindependent-2024-shulzhenko-kozatskyi].
- **Drone footage.** Azov drone footage of the burning plant (early May) circulated widely, but no original upload or dated, stable URL was confirmed for this dossier.
- **Geography.** The helicopter landing spots, the bunker locations and the internal layout (which shops, which tunnels) are not mapped in public sources found.
- **Weather.** Values are reanalysis, not station records.
- **Not yet consulted.** Ukrainian parliamentary or journalistic investigations of why the city was encircled so fast (raised by Serbov) [src:rbc-2026-honcharova-serbov-interview].

- **Starlink cut-off.** SpaceX's whitelist cut Russian terminals in early February 2026. ISW dates the block to 1 Feb, and the Kyiv Independent reported the front-wide cut-off on 5 Feb [src:isw-2026-feb-26-assessment][src:kyivindependent-2026-starlink-catastrophe].
  - The larger Russian attack drones that struck 20–200 km deep via Starlink lost their link. FPVs on line-of-sight or mesh radio carried on [src:euromaidan-2026-axe-starlink-counterattacks].
  - Starlink was on Shaheds, Molniyas and the BM-35. One Ukrainian engineer estimates that only a "single-digit percentage" of Russian drones used it [src:euromaidan-2026-kossov-starlink-russian-drones].
  - The 3rd Army Corps commander Biletsky says the outage cut the effectiveness of Russia's drone campaign by roughly 20–40% in two weeks, with partial recovery expected in one to two months. ISW saw lower tempo and depth in Russian tactical and mid-range strikes, only partly offset by local SIM cards and relay drones [src:isw-2026-feb-26-assessment].
  - Ukrainian counterattacks began across nine vectors toward Huliaipole and in Zaporizhzhia and Dnipropetrovsk oblasts. One up-armoured M1A1 was still immobilised by FPVs [src:euromaidan-2026-axe-starlink-counterattacks].
  - Brigades gave mixed accounts of how much Russian assaults actually slowed [src:kyivindependent-2026-starlink-catastrophe]. The Kyiv Independent's front reporting noted that Russia's dispersed infantry assaults hardly needed Starlink. Russia also kept a "colossal" lead in fiber-optic drones reaching 50+ km [src:kyivindependent-2026-post-starlink-scramble].
- **Did the Russian kill zone shrink?** Only its deep layer did.
  - The satellite-linked strikes 20–200 km deep thinned [src:euromaidan-2026-axe-starlink-counterattacks][src:isw-2026-feb-26-assessment].
  - The fiber layer kept growing. A Russian fibre FPV reached Kharkiv's outskirts on 25 Feb [src:isw-2026-feb-26-assessment], and a ring-wing KVN variant (KVS) carries the same 3 kg payload up to 50 km [src:euromaidan-2026-axe-ring-fpv].
  - Frontelligence Insight's Tatarigami says about 60% of Russian FPVs in key sectors are fibre-optic. An OSINT tally cited by the same outlet puts Russian FPV use at about 10,000 a day [src:euromaidan-2026-axe-unjammable-russian-drones].
  - Ukraine is converging on fibre too: 70% of National Guard drones were fibre-optic by September 2026, up from about 20% [src:euromaidan-2026-vivdych-ng-fibre-70].
  - Fibre supply is a pressure point. ISW, relaying Russian industry sources, reports that Chinese suppliers raised the price for Russian buyers from 16 to 40 yuan per km between early 2025 and early 2026. The struck Saransk plant had made about 4m km a year [src:isw-2026-feb-26-assessment].
  - Russia's Rassvet satellite constellation (32 satellites by July 2026) went from 6–10 minute passes in March to windows of over an hour by late August. It has terminals small enough for Geran-type drones [src:euromaidan-2026-vivdych-rassvet-windows].
- **Kill-zone depth, 2026.** The 7th Air Assault Corps commander (Pokrovsk axis) described a kill zone of 20–25 km on both sides of the line in July 2026 and expects 30 km by the end of the year. In his sector drones cause 70–80% of damage [src:euromaidanpress-2026-vivdych-kill-zone-corps].
- **Drone Line results.** In March 2026, Fedorov claimed 1,000+ crews, 1 in 4 front-line kills and 10,500+ Russian troops struck, plus 33,000+ Russian UAVs destroyed by interceptors, and a 1.3:1 strike-drone advantage [src:rbc-2026-fedorov-drone-line]. In June Syrskyi claimed a 1.5:1 FPV advantage and 12.7% month-on-month output growth (April to May) [src:euromaidan-2026-mukhina-syrskyi-fpv-ratio].
- **USF claims.** Brovdi claimed 102,000 Russians killed or wounded in 12 months (to June 2026), with 360,000 targets hit in 1.7m sorties [src:euromaidan-2026-thomas-brovdi-102000]. That is about one hit per five sorties, a derived figure that mixes reconnaissance, bomber and strike sorties.
- **Leadership changes.** Fedorov was dismissed as defence minister on 14 July 2026, and Khmara was appointed on 19 August [src:euromaidan-2026-stanovych-fedorov-dismissal]. The scoring economy kept running: by September 2026 over 500 units were using DOT-Chain/Brave1 Market and the "Army of Drones Bonus", against 12 a year earlier [src:euromaidan-2026-mukhina-dot-chain-500-units].
- **Interceptors.**
  - Output reached up to 1,000 a day, and interceptors made about 70% of Shahed kills around Kyiv in February 2026 [src:justsecurity-2026-bidochko-drone-superpower].
  - Of 3,500+ drones downed in May 2026, USF interceptors claimed 1,200+ and helicopters 440+. Beskrestnov said interceptors now destroy about 50% of incoming Shahed-types, up from about 10% in winter. Syrskyi warned that Russia aims to raise the jet share to 50% [src:kyivpost-2026-syrsky-may-interceptors].
  - The ZIRKA interceptor (June 2026) flies at 340+ km/h, costs up to $2,000 and uses AI to detect and track its target automatically [src:militarnyi-2026-zirka].
- **Shahed volumes.** Monthly Shahed-type launches peaked at 8,161 in May 2026. The overall hit rate fell from about 16.5% (Aug 2025) to 6.7% (May 2026) [src:isis-2026-anokhin-shahed-monthly]. The Air Force reported 65,618 Shaheds and 10,604 Lancets destroyed from Feb 2022 to Aug 2026 [src:euromaidan-2026-murdoch-445000-intercepted]. From about 5 May 2026 the Air Force stopped consistently publishing Shahed counts, so later monthly figures are reconstructions. ISIS reconstructs August 2026 as 4,288 shot down or suppressed and about 716 hits (13.9%), with 57–62% of genuine Shahed/Geran use jet-powered [src:isis-2026-anokhin-shahed-monthly-sep].
- **Jet Gerans.**
  - Russia launched about 2,800 jet-powered drones in August 2026, up from about 350 in June. Only about 60% are intercepted, according to Air Force spokesman Ihnat [src:united24-2026-place-jet-gerans].
  - In September Ukraine downed 55% (more than 1,500 of over 2,730) [src:euromaidan-2026-zoria-jet-kill-rate-55].
  - HUR estimates Russia builds about 3,000 Geran-4/5 a month and has stopped making the Geran-3 [src:euromaidan-2026-thomas-hur-geran-production].
- **Autonomy.**
  - On 6 July 2026 a Molniya with an Nvidia Jetson Orin module picked its own target near a Zaporizhzhia gas station and killed three civilians. This is the first documented self-targeting Russian kill.
  - Jetson modules have turned up in the V2U, Lancet and Klin drones since June 2025 [src:euromaidan-2026-katola-molniya-self-targeting].
- **UGVs.** Monthly logistics and evacuation missions rose from 7,511 in January to 25,143 in August, and Ukraine plans 50,000+ UGVs in 2026 [src:united24-2026-ugv-missions].
- **Heavy bombers.** SkyFall says it makes 100,000 bombers a year at $8,500 each, about 16 times the cost of an FPV. A bomber drops three or four grenades a sortie and may fly a dozen sorties before it is lost, so it is cheaper per mission than a one-use FPV [src:euromaidan-2026-axe-bomber-drones].
- **Operation Vivaldi (Lyman, 3rd Army Corps).**
  - Heavy bombers air-dropped kamikaze UGVs more than 10 km behind Russian lines, and the corps claims 125+ km² cleared [src:euromaidan-2026-mukhina-vivaldi-ugv-drop].
  - The corps says Rubikon was pulled from the sector after losing operators, launch sites and logistics [src:kyivindependent-2026-farrell-rubicon-vivaldi].
- **Russian heavy bombers.** Russia is fielding a Baba Yaga equivalent called "Berdysh" and reportedly repairing captured Vampires [src:pravda-2026-berdysh-russian-heavy-drone].

## 8. Media

- **Modern RTS and tactical games** (Broken Arrow, WARNO, Regiments, Combat Mission: Black Sea) model massed combined arms between NATO-style and Russian forces. Broken Arrow's unit classes are infantry, recon, vehicles, support, helicopters and air, with no drone class [src:wikipedia-2025-broken-arrow]. Its drones are recon or strike aircraft inside the air-defence matrix [src:steam-2026-broken-arrow-anniversary-update], and loitering munitions were still only a roadmap item in 2026 [src:steam-2025-broken-arrow-roadmap]. WARNO and Regiments are set in 1989 [src:wikipedia-2024-warno][src:steam-2022-regiments]. CM: Black Sea is a *fictional 2017* Russia–Ukraine war. It has UAVs and EW, but it was designed in 2009–2013 and deliberately avoids the "frozen conflict" that followed 2014 [src:wikipedia-2014-combat-mission-black-sea]. It has had no official 2022-era content since [src:steam-2023-cmbs-update-2-18].
- **Operational and strategic sims** of the real war exist mostly as community scenarios or small indie titles. Examples are a TOAW IV "Ukraine 2022" scenario [src:matrixforums-2022-toaw-ukraine-2022] and Sand Table's *Ukraine War 2022* [src:steam-2024-ukraine-war-2022]. Command: Modern Operations' Ukraine-2022 scenarios are mostly *hypothetical NATO interventions* [src:matrixgames-2022-cmo-ukraine-scenarios]. The best commercial models of an operational layer are Cold War and WWII titles: Flashpoint Campaigns' WEGO orders and SOPs on 500 m hexes [src:steam-2023-flashpoint-southern-storm], and Steel Division 2's turn-based battalion campaign wrapped around real-time battles [src:steam-2019-steel-division-2]. The one large-audience RTS of the 2022 war, *Gostomel Heroes*, is told from the Russian side [src:steam-2026-gostomel-heroes-dlc].
- **Drone games and trainers**, many of them Ukrainian, are first-person and cover one drone at a time. Examples are UFDS [src:steam-2025-ufds], Obriy [src:ukrainesarmsmonitor-2026-obriy], *Remote Reaper* [src:steam-2025-remote-reaper] and the arcade *Death From Above* [src:steam-2024-death-from-above]. They model piloting, bombs and sometimes EW, but never the formation or operational picture. The first attempt to join the two, *Hell Of War* (early access, September 2026), puts the player in a command drone that can drop into an FPV [src:steam-2026-hell-of-war].
- **Board and professional wargames** are the most thoughtful about logistics, politics and attrition, but they cluster at the start of the war or at grand-strategic scale. GMT's *Defiance* covers Feb–Apr 2022 [src:gmt-2025-defiance], and Farren's *Glory to the Heroes* uses 150 km hexes [src:paxsims-2023-farren-glory-to-the-heroes]. Expert reviewers say that "relatively few of the existing commercial wargames" capture the dispersed, drone-saturated battlefield of 2025 [src:paxsims-2025-brynen-emergent-approaches].
- **Real-war gamification** may be the most important "prior art" of all. The Army of Drones Bonus (ADB) points economy is a live game system run by the Ukrainian state. Its prices have been rebalanced like a live game's: a killed soldier went from 2 to 6 to 12 points between early 2025 and early 2026 [src:united24-2025-khomenko-adb-launch][src:kyivpost-2026-korshak-epoints]. It is ethically contested [src:wotr-2026-almajdalani-gamified-war].
## 5. Systems and tactics in use

**Formations** (as credited by Putin on 17 Feb, plus units reported during the battle):
- **1st DNR Army Corps (8th CAA, SMD).** The 1st ("Slavic"), 9th, 110th, 114th and 132nd Motor Rifle Brigades, the 1454th and 1487th Regiments and the 10th Tank Regiment. Irregular units were attached: "Kluny", Pyatnashka, Dikaya Diviziya and Arbat (including ex-Wagner men) [src:isw-2024-02-17-assessment] [src:isw-2023-10-22-roca] [src:wikipedia-battle-of-avdiivka] [src:isw-2023-10-19-roca] [src:isw-2023-10-28-roca] [src:lwj-2024-hardie-avdiivka-analysis].
  - *The 114th* lost, per Kyiv Post, 190 dead and 160 wounded in October from 1,800–2,000 men [src:wikipedia-battle-of-avdiivka].
  - *The 1487th* was reduced to under 30% strength [src:isw-2024-02-21-roca].
- **41st CAA (CMD).** The 35th, 55th and 74th Motor Rifle Brigades, and the 90th Tank Division (6th, 80th and 239th Tank Regiments) [src:isw-2024-02-17-assessment]. Ukraine claimed the 90th lost 2,500–3,000 men and 250 armoured vehicles by 12 Nov [src:wikipedia-battle-of-avdiivka].
- **2nd CAA (CMD).** The 15th, 21st and 30th Motor Rifle Brigades, moved laterally from the Lyman direction [src:isw-2023-10-28-roca] [src:kyivindependent-2024-fornusek-3rd-assault-15000].
- **Volunteer Corps.** The 60th "Veterany" Reconnaissance-Assault Brigade, which led the pipe infiltration [src:lwj-2024-hardie-avdiivka-analysis]. HUR says the corps of about 18,000 includes ex-Wagner men and uses Wagner-style assaults [src:isw-2024-02-23-assessment].
- **Penal and special units.** Storm-Z units lost 40–70% [src:isw-2023-10-30-roca]. Storm-V units [src:ukrpravda-2024-isw-storm-v]. GRU spetsnaz and SSO ran night assaults and directed strikes [src:kyivindependent-2024-fornusek-3rd-assault-15000] [src:lwj-2024-hardie-avdiivka-analysis]. The 24th Spetsnaz Brigade reached the city administration [src:lwj-2024-hardie-avdiivka-analysis].
- **Air.** Su-25s close in; Su-34s and Su-35s with glide bombs from stand-off range [src:isw-2023-10-19-roca] [src:kyivpost-2024-orlova-six-aircraft-72h].

**Epilogue.** The withdrawal revealed the killings in Bucha [src:hrw-2022-trail-of-death-bucha] [src:bbc-2022-bucha-satellite-image].
## 3. The diorama: geography, terrain, weather

- **The defence.** Facing it was the 58th Combined Arms Army behind the best-prepared sector of the "Surovikin line": three belts about 30 km deep [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons]. ISW had the 42nd and 19th Motor Rifle Divisions heavily committed, with Spetsnaz brigades as the counterattack force; RUSI lists the 7th VDV and 42nd Divisions forward [src:isw-2023-06-08-roca] [src:isw-2023-07-13-roca] [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].
- **The first breach failed.** On 7–8 June the Western-equipped 47th Mechanised Brigade, with Leopard 2A6s of the 33rd, tried to breach south of Mala Tokmachka. Mines, artillery, ATGMs and Ka-52 helicopters stopped the columns. The photographs of abandoned Leopards and Bradleys became the offensive's emblem [src:guardian-2023-beaumont-wintour-mala-tokmachka] [src:popularmechanics-2023-roblin-minefield-losses] [src:isw-2023-06-08-roca].
- **The switch.** Within days Zaluzhnyi stopped frontal mechanized assaults. Ukraine turned to dismounted platoon and company assaults, counter-battery fire and deep strikes [src:euromaidan-2023-wp-analysis] [src:warontherocks-2023-kofman-lee-three-months] [src:kyivindependent-2023-farrell-counteroffensive-lurches].
- **The second push.** A renewed mechanized attack on 26 July broke into the first positions east of Robotyne but did not hold its furthest gains [src:isw-2023-07-26-roca] [src:isw-2023-07-27-roca]. Reserves, the 82nd Air Assault and 46th Airmobile Brigades, were committed in mid-August [src:warontherocks-2023-kofman-lee-three-months] [src:kyivpost-2023-york-82nd-in-action].
- **Robotyne.** The 47th entered Robotyne on 22 August and raised the flag on 23 August, and Deputy Defence Minister Maliar declared the village liberated on 28 August [src:isw-2023-08-22-roca] [src:euromaidan-2023-zoria-advance-from-robotyne] [src:kyivindependent-2023-khalilova-robotyne-liberated].
- **Verbove.** Ukrainian infantry then pushed east along the Russian trench belt to Verbove. ISW judged the field fortifications west of Verbove broken on 23 September. Al Jazeera reported Ukrainian and Western sources saying the "Surovikin Line" had been cut [src:isw-2023-08-30-roca] [src:isw-2023-09-23-roca] [src:aljazeera-2023-psaropoulos-surovikin-line].
- **No breakthrough.** Russia fed in VDV divisions and the 41st Army. The salient stopped short of Novoprokopivka and Verbove, and by November the front was positional. Zaluzhnyi called the war a "stalemate" [src:isw-2023-09-01-roca] [src:kyivindependent-2023-khalilova-vdv-robotyne] [src:isw-2023-11-06-roca] [src:abcnews-2023-burridge-stalemate].
- **Russian command.** Maj. Gen. Ivan Popov, the 58th Army commander who had celebrated the June minefield defence, was fired on about 11–12 July after complaining about counter-battery fire and the lack of rotation [src:isw-2023-07-13-roca] [src:politico-2023-camut-popov-fired].

- **Command.**
  - Adm. Viktor Sokolov led the fleet until Feb 2024. Vice Adm. Sergei Pinchuk was acting commander from Feb 2024 and is named BSF commander in Dec 2024 [src:pravda-2024-ukdi-sokolov][src:isw-2024-12-31-roca].
  - Navy C-in-C: Adm. Nikolai Yevmenov, then Adm. Aleksandr Moiseyev from Mar 2024 [src:hromadske-2024-ryzhenko-bsf].
  - Defence Minister Shoigu inspected the fleet on 17 Mar 2024. His successor Belousov inspected BSF naval-infantry training on 31 Dec 2024 [src:maritimeexec-2024-bsf-new-measures][src:isw-2024-12-31-roca].
- **Fleet size.**
  - Before the war: about 80 units (Pletenchuk) [src:pravda-2024-pletenchuk-third-of-fleet].
  - Left in Mar 2024 (Pletenchuk): 10 missile carriers, 3 submarines, 2 missile boats, several patrol ships, and 5 large landing ships, 4 of them under repair [src:pravda-2024-pletenchuk-third-of-fleet].
  - By Mar 2024 about 30 modern ships sat at Novorossiysk; Ochamchire (occupied Abkhazia) could hold no more than 5% of the fleet (Ryzhenko) [src:hromadske-2024-ryzhenko-bsf].

## 9. Russia's side as reported

The 47th Mechanised Brigade was moved from Zaporizhzhia to Avdiivka in October 2023, and its M2A2 ODS Bradleys anchored the northern flank around Stepove [src:euromaidan-2023-havrylets-avdiivka] [src:forbes-2023-axe-bradley-three-mtlb]. A Russian T-90M "Proryv", Russia's most capable frontline tank, attacked near Stepove, where Ukrainian troops held a trench under tank fire [src:twz-2024-altman-bradley-gunner] [src:twz-2024-altman-bradley-t90m-experts]. Two Bradleys took it on. The T-90M fired first and missed, and the first Bradley's run "didn't work out" [src:forbes-2024-axe-bradleys-t90] [src:twz-2024-altman-bradley-gunner]. The second Bradley's gunner-commander, "Serhiy", closed in with the M242 25 mm cannon and fired armour-piercing rounds into the rear of the tank. When those rounds gave trouble, he switched ammunition and shot out its optics [src:twz-2024-altman-bradley-gunner] [src:twz-2024-altman-bradley-t90m-experts]. Blinded, the T-90M popped smoke, backed away with its turret spinning and ran into a tree. Its crew bailed out, and an FPV drone finished the tank off [src:twz-2024-altman-bradley-t90m-experts].

The 2023 counteroffensive was planned around one main effort: a push south from Orikhiv to Tokmak and then Melitopol, to cut Russia's land bridge to Crimea [src:warontherocks-2023-kofman-lee-three-months] [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons]. The US–Ukrainian war games behind it imagined Ukraine reaching the Sea of Azov in 60–90 days [src:euromaidan-2023-wp-analysis].
**The crossings**

The trap was only partly closed, because many vehicles escaped down the four-lane road [src:nyt-2022-kramer-brovary-tanks] [src:mwi-2025-collins-spencer-battle-of-kyiv]. Ukrainian intelligence (HUR) claimed that the regiment's commander, Col. Andrei Zakharov, had been killed [src:interfax-2022-hur-brovary-zakharov]. ISW judged that the column had been "badly damaged", disrupting Russian efforts to encircle or assault Kyiv from the east [src:isw-2022-03-10-roca].

**Map box.** The map runs from Dvorichna (49.851, 37.683) in the north to Kupiansk-Vuzlovyi (49.660, 37.644) in the south, and from Sobolivka (49.705, 37.564) in the west to Lyman Pershyi (49.791, 37.706) in the east, about 20 × 13 km [src:osm-2026-kupiansk-pipeline-geodata]. Kupiansk is about 40 km from the Russian border [src:kyivindependent-2026-terajima-kupiansk-pipelines].

- **The 72nd Mechanised Brigade** held the town and its approaches. Its subunits included the 1st Mechanised Battalion, whose deputy commander was Lt. Vladislav Bayak. ## 9. Russia's side as reported

From July 2025 the battle became the war's defining drone fight. Russian FPV teams, Rubikon among them, put every road into Pokrovsk under fire control, and ISW judged that this had already denied Ukraine the city as a logistics hub [src:euromaidanpress-2025-tril-isw-21-months]. Russian infantry no longer stormed. It seeped through in groups of two to three and by the hundred a day, walking for days from Selydove [src:nv-2025-horova-deepstate-150-saboteurs] [src:cnn-2025-kottasova-pokrovsk-poised]. On 11 August such groups opened a 15 km wedge towards Dobropillia. The 1st Azov Corps and other reserves cut it off and cleared it by late October [src:euromaidanpress-2025-zoria-deepstate-wedge] [src:kyivindependent-2025-farrell-dobropillia-lessons]. Meanwhile infiltrators accumulated inside Pokrovsk itself: about 200–250 by late October, then more than 300 in the November fog [src:pravda-2025-kyrylenko-250-russians-pokrovsk] [src:euromaidan-2025-axe-foggy-advance]. The garrison was squeezed into the northern quarters and Myrnohrad onto a single drone-watched road [src:euromaidanpress-2025-axe-road-into-myrnohrad]. Russia announced the capture of Pokrovsk on 1 December and of Myrnohrad on 27 December. Ukraine held parts of both towns into late January 2026 [src:cnn-2025-stockwell-capture-claim] [src:isw-2025-12-28-roca] [src:isw-2026-02-25-roca].

## 2. Timeline

1. **Massed tube and rocket artillery (2022).** Russia fired about 20,000 rounds a day in Donbas, with peaks above 32,000. Ukraine rarely fired more than 6,000, and Russia held a 10–12:1 advantage by June 2022 [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons]. HIMARS/M270 GMLRS from late June 2022 broke the Russian model, which depended on railheads and big depots. RUSI calls their arrival "the point where the Russian offensive on Donbas ended" [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons].
2. **Precision and mass without air superiority (2023–24).** Russian shells ran short (about 12M rounds in 2022, trending to about 7M in 2023) [src:rusi-2023-watling-meatgrinder]. Russia moved to Krasnopol laser-guided shells, Lancet for counter-battery, and above all mass UMPK glide bombs. These let the VKS (Russian Aerospace Forces) strike the front from 30–90 km without entering Ukrainian SAM coverage [src:rusi-2025-watling-third-year]. Russian EW (electronic warfare) cut Ukraine's GPS-guided Excalibur hit rate from more than 50% to 6–7% [src:stripes-2024-khurshudyan-jamming]. Ukraine rationed shells: the ratio was 1:10 in February 2024 [src:liga-2025-shell-ratio].
3. **The drone-dominated kill zone and a deep-strike duel (2024–26).** Tactical UAVs now cause 60–70% of damaged and destroyed Russian systems [src:rusi-2025-watling-third-year], and Latvian intelligence puts drones at 70–80% of all killed and wounded on both sides by early 2026 [src:politico-2026-hartog-latvian-drones]. Artillery survives by dispersing and digging in, and it works as a partner to drones rather than the main killer. The Ukrainian shell ratio recovered to about 1:1.8 by July 2025 [src:liga-2025-shell-ratio], helped by the Czech initiative [src:kyivindependent-2025-czech-initiative]. Russian KAB use climbed from about 5,000 to almost 8,800 a month during 2026 [src:kyivpost-2026-korshak-glide-bombs] [src:militarnyi-2026-pryhodko-kabs-us-campaigns], and Iskander-M output to 60–70 a month [src:kyivindependent-2025-post-ballistic-production]. Russia launched 100–200 ballistic missiles and up to about 8,000 Shahed/Geran drones a month [src:frontliner-2026-zvirynskyi-strike-intensity] [src:united24-2026-mykhailenko-july-strikes]. As PAC-3 ran short, partly because of the 2026 US–Iran war, Ukraine's ballistic-missile intercept rate collapsed to 10–15% [src:csis-2026-jensen-two-strategic-attacks] [src:atlanticcouncil-2026-kuskevics-patriot]. Ukraine answered with its own long-range weapons, above all mass mid-range and long-range drones, plus a small number of Flamingo and Neptune missiles.

- **Ukrainian ISR at night:** Aerorozvidka, then a volunteer IT-born drone unit, worked with about 30 special-forces troops on quad bikes. They had thermal drones and night-vision goggles and ambushed the Russian column north of Kyiv at night. Their first targets were the column's forward supply depot and its lead vehicles [src:defenseexpress-2022-aerorozvidka-convoy]. The unit's own claims were only partly verified.
- **Russian C2 failed badly:**
  - There was no time to exchange radio encryption keys, and troops were poorly trained on their radios. Many fell back on stolen civilian phones.
  - Ukraine was therefore able to monitor much of Russian tactical traffic. Only 10–20% of brigade/BTG radio traffic was about combat management; most of it was units reporting their own locations.
  - Units reused the same routes and staging areas and relied on a few main supply routes [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons].
- **Deception:** Ukraine photographed bomb damage at its airfields, printed the pattern onto covers, and brought aircraft back to "destroyed" sites. Dummy air-defence sites soaked up Russian munitions. Russian satellite intelligence missed 3–4 Ukrainian military trains a day in March 2022 [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons].
- **Starlink:** First shipments arrived on 28 February 2022, and 5,000 terminals had been delivered by 6 April [src:wikipedia-starlink-russo-ukrainian-war].

**The Ukrainian adaptation (July – November).**
- **Dismounted assault groups.** Platoons and companies of 10–15-man squads moved along tree lines, mostly on foot [src:cnn-2023-cotovio-pleitgen-verbove] [src:warontherocks-2023-kofman-lee-three-months].
  - The pace was 700–1,200 m every five days [src:rusi-2023-watling-stormbreak].
  - Each battalion yielded only about two platoons of assault-capable troops [src:rusi-2023-watling-stormbreak].
  - Engineers cleared mines by hand at night [src:isw-2023-09-03-roca].
- **Bradleys as "taxis".** They delivered and recovered assault groups and survived mines and a near-direct 120 mm mortar hit [src:kyivindependent-2023-farrell-47th-surovikin-line].
- **Tank raids.** Leopard 2A6s fired HE into tree lines and pulled back at the first Russian round. Tanks ran along tree lines to set off anti-personnel mines for the infantry [src:euromaidan-2023-rfu-tank-raids].
- **The counter-battery war.** It used GMLRS and FPVs [src:kyivindependent-2023-farrell-counteroffensive-lurches], radar-hunting [src:warontherocks-2023-kofman-lee-three-months], and night bombing with converted agricultural drones [src:rusi-2023-watling-stormbreak]. Popov's complaint is the Russian side of this [src:isw-2023-07-13-roca].
- **Deep strikes.** Storm Shadow hit HQs and generals [src:warontherocks-2023-kofman-lee-three-months] [src:cnn-2023-lister-popov-dismissed].
- **What countered Ukraine.** Russian FPVs took the edge at small-unit level by September. A 47th sergeant: "Our enemy has learned and adapted" [src:kyivindependent-2023-farrell-47th-surovikin-line]. Air cover was missing against glide bombs and helicopters [src:kyivindependent-2023-kossov-out-of-steam].

- **Operator:** DeepState UA (ДіпСтейт), a Ukrainian NGO co-founded by childhood friends **Roman Pohorilyi** (law background) and **Ruslan Mykula** (marketing) [src:wikipedia-deepstatemap-live] [src:kyivpost-2025-ashcroft-inside-deepstate].
- **Origins:** It began in February 2020 as a Telegram channel on world news and politics. The team experimented with an updatable conflict map during the 2021 Taliban offensive, and before the full-scale invasion it switched to tracking Russian forces on Ukraine's borders [src:wikipedia-deepstatemap-live].
- **Launch:** The map went live on **24 February 2022** (e1-invasion). It first ran on Google Maps. Google blocked the account in late March 2022, so DeepState built its own platform, and data from before 3 April 2022 was lost [src:wikipedia-deepstatemap-live]. The site's own version history starts on 2022-04-03, which matches this [src:deepstate-api-history].
- **Team and security:** 100+ paid staff and volunteers work from an undisclosed location in Kyiv. Staff are vetted, including with polygraphs, and access is tiered so that the most sensitive material stays with the co-founders [src:kyivpost-2025-ashcroft-inside-deepstate]. About 60 people work on verification [src:wikipedia-deepstatemap-live].
- **Reach:**
  - Its busiest days came during the September 2022 Izium/Lyman liberation (e3) [src:wikipedia-deepstatemap-live].
  - It passed 1 billion total views, announced in February 2024 [src:wikipedia-deepstatemap-live].
  - The Telegram channel had 800k+ subscribers in 2025. The audience is about 70% Ukrainian and 30% international [src:kyivpost-2025-ashcroft-inside-deepstate].
- **Funding:** Mostly donations, plus Telegram ads and merchandise [src:kyivpost-2025-ashcroft-inside-deepstate]. Wikipedia also records partial government funding [src:wikipedia-deepstatemap-live].
- **Apps:**
  - Android (March 2023) and iOS (April 2023, after Apple initially resisted) [src:wikipedia-deepstatemap-live].
  - "DeepStateMap 2.0" (2 July 2024) overhauled the graphics and added offline mode, drawing tools, keyboard shortcuts, expanded weapon-range overlays and coordinate copying [src:wikipedia-deepstatemap-live].
- **Tech stack (from the live page source):** Leaflet with a PixiJS WebGL overlay, Highcharts for statistics charts, fabric.js for the drawing tools, and leaflet.pattern for patterned fills [src:deepstate-map-live].

markdown:
- **Old meaning:** grey meant "territory where the situation requires clarification," in practice the thin no-man's-land between the two sides' first lines [src:onlineua-2026-deepstate-legend] [src:kyivindependent-2025-farrell-front-line-mapping].
- **2025 shift:** Ukraine had too few troops to man positions densely, and Russia attacked with small infiltration squads instead of mechanised assaults. The result on DeepState was "increasingly jagged and unusual formations," with grey now depicting a wide contact zone of overlapping positions [src:kyivindependent-2025-farrell-front-line-mapping].
- **2026 redefinition:** DeepState explained that grey now represents **areas where Russian forces have infiltrated**. Positions "may effectively overlap or intermix," and grey should not be read as no-man's-land, as either side's control, or as a precise front [src:onlineua-2026-deepstate-legend]. Internally the polygons are still coded `geoJSON.status.unknown` [src:deepstate-api-history].
- **How deep the zone is:** one analyst describes the contested zone near Kotlyne growing from about 1 km deep (Jan 2025) to "five to eight times wider." He argues that a front "thickened into a depth of 12 kilometers" can no longer be the thing being fought over [src:warontherocks-2026-maurin-front-line].
- **Beyond grey:** the only other uncertainty device is time. The two-week blue "recently liberated" state and the dated "Liberated dd.mm" labels encode how old a change is [src:wikipedia-deepstatemap-live] [src:deepstate-api-history].

The brief dated the Avdiivka infiltration to February 2024. The sources put the main Tsarska Okhota breach in mid-to-late January and its reuse on about 15 February [src:lwj-2024-hardie-avdiivka-analysis] [src:kyivpost-2024-korshak-avdiivka-pipe]. United24 says Ukrainian forces reported it in February [src:united24-2026-kabachynskyi-pipelines]. ## 10. Open questions / gaps

1. **Ukraine restores the S-200 (May 2022).** Ukraine chose to revive a retired 1960s system, find its old operators and rebuild launchers and missiles [src:babel-2024-perepechko-times-a50]. The payoff came nearly two years later, at ranges Patriot could not reach [src:kyivpost-2024-tuzov-s200].
2. **Russia flies the A-50 closer (late 2023 – Jan 2024).** In November 2023 the UK MoD warned that Russia might accept more risk with the Mainstay [src:theaviationist-2024-cenciotti-a50-il22]. Constant sorties began in early January over the Crimea threat [src:isw-2024-01-15-assessment]. MWI reads the forward orbit as urgent need and risk acceptance [src:mwi-2024-mitchell-awacs-azov].
3. **Ukraine pushes Patriot to the front (Jan 2024).** Using a scarce strategic SAM as a forward ambush weapon, rather than for city defence, was what the US officer called "stretching the very, very edges" of its envelope [src:twz-2024-newdick-patriot-a50-confirmed]. The precedent was Bryansk in May 2023 [src:liga-2023-dzheripa-bryansk-patriot].
4. **The target order on 14 Jan.** Ihnat says the A-50 was the priority target and the Il-22M was hit in the same engagement ("caught in crossfire") [src:isw-2024-01-15-assessment] [src:wikipedia-2024-a50-il22-shootdowns]. Sources say nothing of an alternative plan.
5. **Russia's response: move the orbit east (from 17 Jan).** Russia traded coverage for survival, "at the expense of their overall efficacy in Ukraine" (UK DI) [src:pravda-2024-ukdi-a50-redeploy].
6. **Ukraine answers with range and patience (Feb 2024).** Rather than chase the new orbit with Patriot, HUR and the Air Force set an S-200 ambush and waited a week [src:kyivpost-2024-tuzov-s200]. They struck on 23 February, Russia's Defender of the Fatherland Day, a date HUR made a point of [src:pravda-2024-romanenko-second-a50].
7. **Russia grounds or withholds the A-50 (late Feb – Mar 2024).** It recalled strike sorties on 23–24 February [src:pravda-2024-petrenko-a50-five-aircraft] and flew no A-50s near the front for over a week. Oleshchuk reported pilots' "discussions" about being sent "one way" [src:pravda-2024-romanenko-no-a50].
8. **Ukraine goes after the repair base (Mar 2024 onward).** Ukraine struck Taganrog, the only A-50 repair plant, in March 2024 [src:pravda-2024-ivashkiv-taganrog], December 2024 [src:armada-2025-oliver-berievs] and November 2025 [src:euromaidanpress-2025-mukhina-taganrog-a50]. In June 2025 Spiderweb reached the home base at Ivanovo [src:kyivpost-2025-spiderweb-a50-ivanovo].
9. **Kyiv 2022 (vignette).**
   - Ukraine switched deconfliction from time to area after friendly fire [src:rusi-2022-bronk-russian-air-war].
   - Russian pilots went low, then refused missions beyond the lines, and the VKS switched to night attacks from 9 March [src:rusi-2022-bronk-russian-air-war].
   - On 30 April the Air Force chose to debunk its own myth after The Times misidentified the Ghost [src:kyivpost-2022-neplii-ghost-of-kyiv].

**Roads and supply.**
- **The O0542 (H0542).** This was the main supply route and the only paved road in. It ran from the west through Lastochkyne, past the famous city sign, into Industrialnyi Avenue [src:lwj-2024-hardie-avdiivka-analysis] [src:euromaidan-2023-havrylets-avdiivka] [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-last-days-avdiivka].
- **The Avdiivka–Sieverne road.** The secondary route, running past the 9th quarter [src:lwj-2024-hardie-avdiivka-analysis].
- **Dirt tracks to Lastochkyne and Sieverne.** These were the last routes in February [src:isw-2024-02-15-roca].
- **The O0562.** A GLOC 3.3 km from the southern Russian line on 12 Oct [src:isw-2023-10-12-roca].
- **The N20.** The Donetsk–Kostiantynivka highway, partly Russian-held from the start [src:isw-2023-10-11-roca].
- **Rail.** The Avdiivka–Pokrovsk railway runs past Stepove and the plant [src:osw-2023-ber-battle-avdiivka-day-596].

The Crimean Bridge is two parallel structures, a four-lane road bridge and a double-track rail bridge, about 19 km long. Russia built it after occupying Crimea in 2014, and it opened to cars in May 2018 and to trains in December 2019 [src:wikipedia-crimean-bridge]. Ukraine hit it three times, each time by a different route: "The first time we approached it from land, the second time – from the water. In 2025, we approached it from underneath the water" [src:ssu-2025-maliuk-hallmark].
