## 2. Per-era notes
## 10. Game/sim relevance

**The air war stayed contested.** Since early March 2022, Ukrainian ground-based air defence has kept Russian crewed aircraft out of Ukrainian-held airspace except at very low altitude [src:rusi-2022-bronk-russian-air-war]. Russia's layered IADS (integrated air defence system) keeps Ukraine's small air force (MiG-29, Su-27, Su-24M, Su-25, and from 2024–25 F-16 and Mirage 2000) to stand-off strikes and anti-missile and anti-drone patrols. Neither side has air superiority. Glide bombs are Russia's workaround: "Glide bombs gave the VKS teeth without the need to first achieve air superiority" [src:rusi-2025-watling-third-year].

**The outcome the player must reproduce (chapter window, to 31 Mar 2023):**
- **Vuhledar stays Ukrainian.** Russia never holds positions inside the town.
- **Russian gains are a few kilometres at most.** They take Pavlivka (claimed on 14 Nov 2022, contested until at least 23 Nov), Mykilske (about 27 Jan 2023) and parts of the dacha areas south and southeast of the town [src:isw-2022-11-14-roca] [src:isw-2022-11-23-roca] [src:isw-2023-01-27-roca] [src:isw-2023-02-14-roca].
  - ISW: Russia "failed to advance four kilometers from Mykilske and Pavlivka to Vuhledar" in three weeks [src:isw-2023-03-05-roca].
  - DeepState (relayed by Novaya Gazeta Europe): Russia advanced about 2 km near Mykilske between April 2022 and March 2023 [src:novayagazeta-2023-ukmod-raam].
- **Russian armoured losses fall in a contested band:**
  - **About 25–30 vehicles in a single engagement.** This is visually documented. ISW counted 13 tanks and 12 BMPs in one filmed engagement [src:isw-2023-02-09-roca]. The UK MoD said at least 30 "mostly intact" armoured vehicles were abandoned in one incident [src:reuters-2023-ukmod-vuhledar-dozens]. Girkin said more than 30 [src:politico-2023-melkozerova-155th-brigade].
  - **About 103 vehicles, including 36 tanks, on 8–10 Feb.** This is Oryx's count for Avdiivka and Vuhledar together [src:insider-2023-oryx-103-vehicles]. The Moscow Times attributes the whole figure to Muradov's units [src:moscowtimes-2023-muradov-dismissed].
  - **About 130 vehicles, including 36 tanks.** This is the Ukrainian military's claim: "over the past week", per spokesman Dmytrashkivskyi on 12 Feb [src:politico-2023-melkozerova-155th-brigade], and "at least 130 tanks and APCs" over three weeks, per the NYT [src:nyt-2023-kramer-epic-tank-battle].
  - Unnamed observers quoted by RFE/RL put it at 20–40 tanks and vehicles [src:rferl-2023-eckel-what-happened-vuhledar].
- **Ukrainian equipment losses are small.** Oryx counted 20 Ukrainian vehicles, including 2 tanks, against the 103 above [src:insider-2023-oryx-103-vehicles].
- **The 155th Brigade ends the window combat-ineffective.** The UK MoD called its losses "extremely high", and from 23 Feb Ukraine reported elements refusing to attack [src:nv-2023-ukmod-155th-satellite] [src:isw-2023-02-23-roca].
  - Personnel claims range widely. Ukraine said "almost the entire brigade" of about 5,000 men, at 150–300 marines a day [src:politico-2023-melkozerova-155th-brigade]. The UK defence secretary said 1,000 killed on 14–15 Feb [src:taskandpurpose-2023-slayton-vuhledar-mines].
  - The floor is BBC Russian's names-only count for the whole 2022–24 battle: 211 dead and 42 missing from the 155th, and 72 dead from the 40th [src:kyivindependent-2024-hodunova-bbc-marines].
- **Command consequence.** Muradov is reported relieved [src:moscowtimes-2023-muradov-dismissed].

Inside, the defenders used the plant's Soviet-era tunnels and shelters: about 11 km² of plant above 24 km of tunnels [src:abc-2022-ozdemir-inside-azovstal]. Seven Ukrainian Mi-8 missions (16 helicopters) flew in ammunition, Stingers, NLAWs, Starlink terminals and 72 Azov volunteers, and brought out wounded. Three helicopters were lost [src:twz-2022-altman-mariupol-helicopter-missions] [src:time-2024-spencer-collins-mariupol-helicopters] [src:militarnyi-2022-sapwood-helicopters-seven-times]. UN/ICRC convoys took civilians out between 30 April and 7 May [src:un-ukraine-2022-05-03-lubrani-azovstal] [src:isw-2022-05-07-roca]. Russian troops broke into the plant on 4 May [src:isw-2022-05-04-roca]. On 16 May the General Staff declared that the garrison had "fulfilled its combat mission" and ordered the commanders to save their men's lives [src:defenceua-2022-mariupol-garrison-mission]. By 20 May Russia claimed 2,439 had left the plant and surrendered [src:pravda-2022-mazurenko-2439-shoigu]. At least 50 prisoners, many of them from Azovstal, were killed in the Olenivka barracks explosion of 28–29 July 2022 [src:un-news-2023-olenivka-justice].

**Roads and bridges.** The road refs are as ISW uses them [src:isw-2023-03-07-roca] [src:isw-2023-04-21-roca].
- **T0504 Kostiantynivka–Chasiv Yar–Bakhmut.** The southern road of life, via Ivanivske. ISW called it "Ukrainian forces' last remaining GLOC into Bakhmut that Russian forces are not fully interdicting" [src:isw-2023-03-07-roca]. The 3rd Assault Brigade calls the T0504 through Khromove "the last paved route" [src:youtube-2023-3oshbr-road-of-life-trench-battle].
- **O0506 Chasiv Yar–Khromove–Bakhmut.** The northern road, entering the city as Yuvileina St [src:isw-2023-04-26-roca]. The Kyiv Independent counts two roads of life: "one to the north, through … Khromove, and the T0504 further south through Ivanivske". Both were within 1 km of Russian positions in April, and the Khromove road had been out of active use for weeks by 21 April [src:kyivindependent-2023-farrell-bakhmut-flanks-hold].
- **Which road is "the road of life".** Sources disagree [src:businessinsider-2023-baker-jankowicz-unyielding-city] [src:kyivindependent-2023-farrell-ukraine-strikes-back-last-streets]. Treat both as supply routes.
- **M03 (E40) Sloviansk–Bakhmut.** The northern supply road. Russia came within 2.5 km of it by 8 February 2023 [src:isw-2023-02-08-roca].
- **T0513 Siversk–Bakhmut.** Cutting it would require advances west of Soledar [src:isw-2023-01-07-roca].
- **T1302.** Runs north-east via Bakhmutske [src:isw-2022-11-15-roca].
- **Bridges.**
  - **22 Sep 2022:** the central Bakhmutka bridge was destroyed, cutting off the east bank [src:pravda-2022-kyrylenko-bridge-bisects-bakhmut].
  - **3 Mar 2023:** two bridges went, one over the Bakhmutka in the north-east and one on the Khromove road [src:isw-2023-03-03-roca]. Cherevatyi blamed Russia for the Khromove bridge; ISW could not tell who blew it [src:isw-2023-03-04-roca].
  - **4 May 2023:** a bridge over the canal west of the city was down [src:isw-2023-05-05-roca].
- **Fire control.**
  - RUSI puts Russian artillery control of the supply roads from February 2023 [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].
  - The Kyiv Independent says Russia had "fire control over all the remaining roads" by early March [src:kyivindependent-2023-farrell-russia-takes-bakhmut].
  - ISW judged Russian interdiction claims exaggerated throughout [src:isw-2023-04-08-roca].
## 2. Timeline

**The land alternative.**
- The bridge is one of two southern ground lines of communication. The other runs through occupied Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson oblasts [src:isw-2023-07-17-roca].
- After Act 1, columns moved Mariupol–Berdiansk–Melitopol [src:isw-2022-10-10-roca]. After Act 2, tourist traffic was rerouted through Dzhankoi and Armiansk toward Melitopol [src:isw-2023-07-17-roca].
- Russia built a rail line through the occupied coast [src:euromaidan-2024-rail-uk-mod; molfar-2024-bridge-satellite]. By 2026 that corridor was itself under drone attack: M-14 freight was down about 71%, and the Chonhar and North Crimean Canal crossings were cut [src:euromaidanpress-2026-crimea-island; kyivindependent-2026-moroziuk-crimea-rail-bridge; maritimeexecutive-2026-rail-ferries].
**Weather and light.** These are modelled reanalysis values (Open-Meteo), not station readings [src:openmeteo-2026-krynky-weather].
## 5. Systems and tactics in use

- **Starlink cutoff.** From 4 February 2026 Starlink whitelisted terminals, so Russia's smuggled units went dark. This "grounded many Russian drones and blinded headquarters" [src:euromaidan-2026-zoria-air-assault-south]. Russians tried to re-register terminals through Ukrainian proxies [src:osw-2026-wilk-zaporizhzhia].
- **Southern counteroffensive.** Led by the Air Assault Forces, with the 425th Assault Regiment (Abrams) and the 37th Marines. By 22 February it had retaken 300+ km² and 8 settlements, amid up to 50 engagements a day [src:euromaidan-2026-zoria-air-assault-south]. Possibly two brigades crossed the Vovcha [src:osw-2026-wilk-zaporizhzhia].
- **Operation Vivaldi (Lyman, from about late May or early June 2026).** Run by the 3rd Army Corps under "maximum information silence":
  - Assault teams and drones conducted "strike-search" actions against infiltration groups. The corps reported 75 km² cleared and 10 km² liberated, including Serednie; OSINT estimates exceed 200 km² [src:kyivindependent-2026-farrell-vivaldi].
  - The deeper logic was to cut off infiltrators rather than hunt them. A "middle-strike" campaign at 30–200 km plus local drone dominance hit Russian logistics, depots and launch sites [src:mwi-2026-rose-vivaldi]. ISW says the first phase defeated infiltration groups by destroying the ATV and motorcycle assaults sent to reinforce them. Strikes on supply routes left the stranded groups demoralized and short of supplies, and only then were they cleared. By late September Ukraine was applying the same "target the reinforcement" pattern in other sectors [src:isw-2026-09-26-assessment].
  - Assaults go in behind robots. 3rd Corps UGVs cleared 30 km of routes in two nights on the Shandryholove axis and now lift about 60% of the anti-personnel mines in its zone. One crew can also remotely mine up to 200 m of Russian routes a day. The corps claims 125 km² retaken over two phases [src:euromaidan-2026-vivdych-robot-demining]. Outside mappers put it higher, at 200–240 km²; that range is an estimate by mappers, not ISW's [src:kyivindependent-2026-york-vivaldi-gains].
  - The 60th Mechanized Brigade struck Russian drone launch sites at set times before infantry advanced. Russia responded by shifting south to infiltrate Mykolaivka toward Sloviansk [src:euromaidan-2026-thomas-vivaldi-shift].
- **Fortress belt.** Kostiantynivka's population is down from 67,000 to about 2,500. Russian small groups infiltrate its streets, and ground robots haul most supplies [src:euromaidan-2026-tril-fortress-belt].
- **Russian infiltration in 2026.** Russia has made near-zero net gains since March 2026 [src:isw-2026-09-26-assessment]. Radio Svoboda, citing DeepState, says Russian gains fell from 450–550 km² a month at the 2025 peak to 160 km² in April 2026 [src:euromaidan-2026-tril-cost-per-km]. Its figure of 27 km² for July is too low: DeepState itself reported 36 km² [src:kyivpost-2026-zavadska-deepstate-july], and the full monthly series is in file 07 §2.7. Infiltration groups of two to six walk 15–20 km to reach positions [src:euromaidan-2026-tril-cost-per-km]. At Kupiansk, Russian troops walked about 10 km through a disused gas pipeline to enter the city [src:euromaidan-2026-zoria-kupiansk-pipeline]. In northern Kharkiv Oblast they bypass Ukrainian positions in a "chessboard" pattern. Glide bombs turn near-rear settlements into ruins that later infiltrators use for cover, and in the south the dried Kakhovka reservoir bed is an infiltration route [src:isw-2026-09-26-assessment].
- **Protected armour.** A Russian T-72B3A fitted with an FPV-adapted Arena-M active protection system (July 2026) took seven drones to exhaust its countermeasures and 15–20 FPVs in all to kill [src:militarnyi-2026-pryhodko-aps-80].
- **Anti-drone works.** 1,066 km of roads netted in 2026, with 4,000 km planned by year's end. The kill zone is 15–30 km deep. Ground robots flew 66,000 logistics and evacuation missions in the first half of 2026 [src:euromaidan-2026-mukhina-anti-drone-nets].
- **Remote mining.** Drones lay mines, and Ukraine claims 678 Russians killed by engineering obstacles in February 2026 [src:euromaidan-2026-mukhina-drone-mines]. Russian remote mining and drones have made supply routes near Novopavlivka too dangerous to drive, and a Zemledeliye launcher was destroyed by FPVs on the Zaporizhzhia front in July [src:euromaidan-2026-mukhina-zemledeliye]. Drone-dropped anti-tank mines also hit evacuation vehicles [src:euromaidan-2026-mukhina-chornovol-evacuation].
- **Mined land.** The war has affected about 133,300 km², including 57,900 km² of farmland, according to Deputy Minister Ihor Bezkaravainyi. He says the 20 km zone along the front "is not described in any international standard" [src:euromaidan-2026-helme-bezkaravainyi-demining]. A far smaller area, about 460,000 ha (4,600 km²), has been identified as requiring clearance [src:euromaidan-2026-mukhina-460k-hectares].
- **Rotation and evacuation.** After cases of soldiers held on position for 502 days, Syrskyi capped deployments at two months [src:euromaidan-2026-mukhina-502-days]. His July review restated it as rotation at least every 60 days "whenever operationally possible". No fetched source measures compliance [src:euromaidan-2026-murdoch-syrskyi-h1]. Wounded can still wait "days, weeks, and sometimes months" [src:euromaidan-2026-kossov-evacuation].
  - Robotic casevac is expensive. One early operation used about four UGVs to bring out a single wounded soldier, and one robot drew about 15 FPVs plus artillery. UGVs cannot cross rivers and get stuck in mud and glide-bomb craters [src:euromaidan-2026-murdoch-robotic-medevac].
  - Most units still lack dedicated evacuation groups or light armoured evacuation vehicles. In one 2025 case a single evacuation cost seven casualties after two vehicles hit drone-dropped AT mines [src:euromaidan-2026-mukhina-chornovol-evacuation].
  - More than 44,000 people have received prosthetics under the state programme since 2022, military and civilian combined [src:euromaidan-2026-mukhina-prosthetics].
- **Ukrainian manpower reform.** Fixed-term contracts opened on 15 June 2026. They run 10–14 months in infantry and assault roles and 24 months elsewhere, followed by a guaranteed deferral from mobilization. About 2,000 soldiers signed in the first month [src:euromaidan-2026-helme-syrskyi-silence]. Soldiers read the scheme as restarting the clock rather than offering a way home [src:euromaidan-2026-helme-draft-crisis].
  - Defence Minister Fedorov was dismissed in July amid street protests, and Mykhailo Drapatyi replaced Syrskyi as Commander-in-Chief [src:euromaidan-2026-helme-syrskyi-silence] [src:euromaidan-2026-mukhina-awol-return].
  - Drapatyi ordered a force-wide manning audit. An AWOL return scheme let those absent by 12 June report back by 20 September and choose among more than 70 units [src:euromaidan-2026-mukhina-awol-return].
  - Syrskyi's own H1 2026 review said Russia still held almost a 2:1 edge in personnel and equipment, while Ukraine carried out 40% of all assault actions [src:euromaidan-2026-murdoch-syrskyi-h1].
- **Casualty claims (September 2026).**
  - *Russian dead, counted by name.* Mediazona/BBC confirmed 248,844 to 10 September [src:kyivindependent-2026-hyatt-mediazona] and about 259,000 to 21 September [src:mediazona-2026-casualties-count]. Their estimated true toll is about 438–535k killed [src:wikipedia-casualties].
  - *Russian dead, official estimates.* The UK intelligence chief said in May 2026 that 500,000 Russians had been killed [src:euromaidan-2026-tril-cost-per-km].
  - *Russian killed and wounded.* Ukraine's General Staff claims 1,531,060 by 28 September [src:ukrpravda-2026-genstaff-losses]. Syrskyi puts the H1 2026 rate at about 32,000 a month [src:euromaidan-2026-murdoch-syrskyi-h1].
  - *Russian cost per km².* Radio Svoboda, from General Staff and DeepState data, puts Russian losses per km² gained at 85 in 2025 and 290 in 2026, against ISW's 53 for autumn 2024 [src:euromaidan-2026-tril-cost-per-km].
  - *Ukrainian dead.* Zelensky said in February 2026 that 55,000 had been killed, up from 31,000 (Feb 2024) and 46,000 (Feb 2025), with a "large number" missing [src:euromaidan-2026-thomas-zelensky-55k]. UALosses has named 96,821 Ukrainian dead and 97,938 missing to 21 June 2026 [src:ualosses-2026-soldiers].
  - *North Koreans.* HUR claims over 7,000 casualties, against about 6,000 per NIS and British estimates [src:kyivindependent-2026-terajima-nk-hur].
- **North Koreans in 2026.** In January the troops in Kursk were firing tube artillery and MLRS at Ukrainian border areas and running reconnaissance, rotating under a bilateral agreement; about 3,000 had gone home (HUR via Yonhap) [src:koreatimes-2026-yonhap-nk-kursk]. On 28 September Zelensky said more than 8,000 were in Russia and another 10,000 were being prepared [src:kyivindependent-2026-hyatt-nk-mobilization].
- **Russian manpower.** Q1 2026 recruitment was 71,216 (about 800 a day), a three-year low; it recovered to about 1,000 a day in April [src:kluge-2026-recruitment]. Regional sign-up bonuses reached a mean of 1.47M RUB [src:united24-2026-litnarovych-bonuses]. Russia missed its 30,000-a-month target in 2026 [src:kyivindependent-2026-hyatt-mediazona].
  - Syrskyi says Russian losses exceeded recruitment for the first time in H1 2026 [src:euromaidan-2026-midttun-losses-recruits]. Ukrainian intelligence gives about 232,000 recruited against about 240,000 lost from January to July. It also describes a Russian General Staff contingency to mobilize 300,000 a year in 2026–27, which Putin publicly denied [src:euromaidan-2026-thomas-mobilization-600k].
  - After the September Duma elections Zelensky said "additional mobilization" had begun. A 28 September decree raised active strength to 1,550,500 [src:kyivindependent-2026-hyatt-nk-mobilization].
## 3. Weapon catalog

- **HUR (Defence Intelligence).** Chief: Lt. Gen. Kyrylo Budanov. Spokesman: Andrii Yusov.
  - The head of the unmanned-systems department is a general with the alias "Borets" [src:pravda-2024-romaniuk-magura-target-eliminate].
  - **Group 13** is the special unit that ran every Magura sinking and air kill. Its commander's call sign is "Thirteenth" [src:ukrinform-2025-magura-v7][src:euromaidan-2024-zoria-ivanovets-sunk].
  - Operators sit at a "remote bridge" in Kyiv, over 1,000 km from the targets, for a day or two per mission: two computers and a control panel [src:pravda-2024-romaniuk-magura-target-eliminate].
  - Funding and support come through United24 and the Ministry of Digital Transformation [src:pravda-2024-hur-ivanovets].
- **SBU.** Head: Vasyl Malyuk. Brig. Gen. "Hunter" leads the Sea Baby programme.
  - The SBU ran the Sea Baby (Kerch Bridge, Novorossiysk, *Sig*, *Samum*, *Derzhavin*, *Kozitsky*, the Dec 2024 machine-gun raid) [src:wikipedia-sea-baby][src:pravda-2024-sea-baby-avdiivka].
  - Wikipedia names Brig. Gen. Ivan Lukashevych as the man who proposed SBU USVs [src:wikipedia-sea-baby]. That he is "Hunter" is **not** established.
  - HUR says the SBU's **Mamai** long-range drone made the Novorossiysk hits [src:pravda-2024-romaniuk-magura-target-eliminate].
- **Navy and the 385th Brigade.**
  - The Navy co-planned the Novorossiysk, *Sig* and *Kotov* operations. Its spokesman is Capt. 3rd rank Dmytro Pletenchuk [src:pravda-2023-novorossiysk-olenegorsky-gornyak][src:ukrinform-2024-kotov].
  - The **385th Separate Brigade of Special-Purpose Naval Unmanned Systems** was formed in Aug 2023 in the Navy, staffed mostly by HUR and SBU operators. It later came under the Unmanned Systems Forces [src:navalnews-2023-sutton-385th-brigade][src:wikipedia-385th-usv-brigade].
- **Equipment and numbers.**
  - Magura V5: at least 16 seen at one base in Dec 2023 [src:navalnews-2023-sutton-russia-adapts]. Production of up to 50 a month is claimed by a low-reliability source [src:gssr-2026-swarm-at-sea].
  - Sea Baby: 35 crowdfunded in Feb 2024 at about UAH 8.5m each [src:pravda-2024-sea-baby-fundraiser].
  - Mamai: numbers unknown [src:pravda-2024-romaniuk-magura-target-eliminate].
  - Missiles for the drones: R-73 "SeeDragon" from 2024; AIM-9M from Jan 2025 [src:gur-2024-mi8][src:twz-2025-altman-su30-aim9].
- **Context fires** (not playable here, but they shape the map): Neptune, Harpoon and Storm Shadow strikes on ships and the BSF HQ [src:euromaidan-2024-zoria-kotov-sunk][src:wikipedia-storm-shadow].
### Ukraine (Mariupol garrison)

- **Denial, then "halted".**
  - On 6 Aug the MoD and FSB claimed that raids by about a battalion of armour had been repelled. Milbloggers mocked it as a "media stunt" [src:isw-2024-08-06-roca; src:wikipedia-2024-kursk-offensive].
  - On 7 Aug Gerasimov told Putin about 1,000 attackers had been stopped. Putin called it a "large-scale provocation" [src:isw-2024-08-07-roca].
  - Milbloggers raged that the build-up had been seen for months [src:isw-2024-08-07-roca]. They called the column move to Oktyabrskoye "criminal incompetence" [src:kyivpost-2024-oktyabrskoye-himars].
- **Framing.**
  - A "counterterrorism operation", not war, to avoid panic [src:isw-2024-08-10-roca].
  - Putin publicly chastised officials and shifted the blame [src:isw-2024-08-12-roca].
  - Zakharova blamed US HIMARS for the Glushkovo bridge and for killing evacuation volunteers [src:aljazeera-2024-seym-bridge-western-weapons].
- **Silence about North Koreans.** Russian officials did not acknowledge them until Gerasimov thanked them on 26 Apr 2025 [src:isw-2024-12-17-roca; src:isw-2025-04-26-roca]. Pyongyang confirmed the next day [src:euromaidan-2025-tril-nk-acknowledges].
- **Encirclement claims.**
  - Putin claimed 2,000 Ukrainians were "encircled" in October; ISW never saw evidence [src:isw-2025-03-14-roca; src:kyivindependent-2024-denisova-17800-casualties].
  - In March 2025 he claimed Ukrainians were "blocked" and offered surrender terms in reply to Trump. Milbloggers' own maps showed exits into Sumy Oblast [src:isw-2025-03-14-roca].
  - Medvedev: "The lid of the smoking cauldron is practically closed" [src:cnn-2025-edwards-russia-advancing-kursk].
- **Victory narrative.**
  - Gerasimov: Gornal "liberated" and 76,000 Ukrainian casualties. Putin: "The Kyiv regime's adventure has completely failed" [src:bbc-2025-somerville-russia-claims-kursk].
  - Russia accused Ukraine of shelling the Sudzha gas station on 21 Mar [src:euromaidan-2025-tril-sudzha-gas-station].
  - A section of the pipe went on show in a 2025 exhibition celebrating the operation [src:ukrpravda-2026-kyrylenko-kupiansk-is-yours].
- **Internal strain.**
  - Conscripts were captured in large numbers [src:wikipedia-2024-kursk-offensive].
  - Captured papers show suicides and morale orders in the 488th Regiment [src:guardian-2024-walker-seized-papers].
  - Alaudinov called for conscripts to fight and dismissed their families' concerns [src:isw-2024-08-19-roca].
The fires war went through three overlapping regimes.

**Caveats.**
- **Publication dates, not event dates.** Versions lag events by 2–3 days, and Ukrainian gains are sometimes released weeks later: DeepState's July 2026 report added 25 and 27 km² reclaimed in earlier months [src:kyivpost-2026-zavadska-deepstate-july], and AMK Mapping described a September 2026 DeepState release near Lyman as "OPSEC release part 3", covering advances "primarily... during May and June" [src:amk-mapping-control-map]. So e9 recaptures are pushed into Aug–Sep, and Ukrainian gains in May–July are understated.
- **April 2022 is unusable.** DeepState rebuilt the map after Google blocked it, and the 3 April version is incomplete (computed April "gain" of 15,376 km² is an artefact). Crimea and ORDLO were not drawn as polygons until mid-2022, hence the fixed pre-2022 mask.
- **Grey zone.** Red to grey counts as a Ukrainian recapture and grey to red as a Russian gain. Grey tripled from about 400 km² (2023) to 1,600–1,800 km² (mid-2026), so in e9 part of the "recapture" is reclassification. Counting red plus grey as Russian gives August 2026 a net Ukrainian gain of about 103 km².
- **Gross vs net.** Monthly gross sums exceed year-on-year differencing because of back-and-forth churn. For 2023, differencing gives 699 km² gained and 539 recaptured; DeepState's rounded 2023 figures were about 540 and 430 [src:euromaidan-2025-hrudka-2024-3600].
- **Other trackers differ by method.** ISW counted +104 km² of assessed Russian control plus 628 km² of infiltration zone for Jan–May 2026 [src:euromaidan-2026-zoria-may-14]. The Russian project Slivochny Kapriz, which credits any area where Russian troops were seen, gives 550–600 km² a month for 2025 [src:euromaidan-2026-tril-cost-per-km]. Ukrainian-held ground inside Russia (Kursk, 2024–25) is outside this metric.
- **Totals.** Coastline generalisation makes totals about 0.7% lower than DeepState's. Changes are unaffected.
- **Western comparison.** ISW put Russia's 2025 gains at about 4,700 km² against Russia's claimed 6,000 km² [src:bbc-2022-ukraine-in-maps]. The gap between claimed and assessed numbers is itself a UI motif.

## 11. Open questions/gaps

Accessed 2026-09-28. Sources are in `sources/03-fires-air.yaml`, cited inline as `[src:<id>]`. The player side is Ukraine. Russian capabilities are described as reported by Ukrainian and Western sources.

- **Soviet belt design norms.** Spacing as multiples of tree height and the official cross-belt rules were still not found. The measured grid (§2.7) and Parfonov now replace the search-only Oleshky figure as the basis. The forestry-journal site refused connections again, the MDPI Ukraine shelterbelt papers (Land 2025, Resources 2025) returned 403, and Ukrainian-language norms were out of scope.
- **Measurement coverage.** Five boxes is a small sample, and OSM completeness varies. The next step is to run the same method over the NASA Harvest field polygons offline (NC-ND, statistics only) or over a belt layer derived from WorldCover or Dynamic World.
- **Balka dimensions.** No source gives typical balka widths, depths or slope angles. Measure them from Copernicus GLO-30 along the sample boxes. Chalk hills beyond the Sviati Hory area are unsourced.
- **Weather effects.** Rain, fog and icing are now sourced qualitatively. Wind limits, summer dust and any *quantified* foliage-versus-detection relationship were not found. Parfonov says only that canopy "substantially" degrades FPV effectiveness, and a Resources 2025 paper mentions rising dust storms without figures.
- **Crater density 2023–26.** No crater-density study for Donbas or Zaporizhzhia after 2022 was found. The Kyinska hromada count (e1) lacks an area, so it gives no density. UNOSAT's product pages render by JavaScript and could not be listed.
- **Village destruction over time.** Beyond the Marinka narrative there is no settlement-level damage time series. Sentinel-1 coherence methods exist but were not applied.
- **Dataset corrections to the brief.** No EuroCrops Ukraine subset exists. FTW and AI4Boundaries exclude Ukraine. The Microsoft footprint licence is inconsistent (CDLA-P 2.0 in the repo vs ODbL at Overture).
- **Process note.** The web-search quota ran out, so later research used OpenAlex, publisher site searches, the DeepState endpoints, Overpass, Microsoft footprints and EOX tiles. ISW pages returned 403. The procgen literature on field patterns and hedgerows is still thin.
## 4. Forces

- **Jammers in every trench.** The FPV boom brought mass trench and backpack jammers. Kvertus went from dozens a month (2022) to thousands (2024) [src:euromaidan-2024-martyniuk-ew-backpacks]. In December 2023, commanders who had refused EW kit that September began signing for it "without even reading" the forms [src:euromaidan-2025-zoria-jamming-fails].
- **Frequency moves began.** Russian FPVs moved from 850–930 MHz to 720–1020 MHz, although 65–70% still used standard bands [src:euromaidan-2024-martyniuk-ew-backpacks]. Vehicle jammers went from one module in spring 2024 to seven by autumn, which strained power supply and weight [src:euromaidan-2025-zoria-jamming-fails].
- **Industry scaled.** EW output grew 340-fold in 2024 over 2023, and the number of makers went from about 10 to more than 140 [src:militarnyi-2025-pryhodko-ew-340x].
- **Russia fielded vehicle "domes".** The Volnorez cone jammer appeared in autumn 2023 [src:militarnyi-2024-kushnikov-volnorez].
- **Western framing.** CNAS called EW "the most effective way to stop drones" and noted operators being hunted with drone-tracking software [src:cnas-2024-pettyjohn-evolution].
- **Russian Starlink use confirmed.** GUR called it "systemic" in February 2024 [src:aljazeera-2024-gur-starlink].
- **Turtle tanks.** Russian "turtle tanks" with onboard jammers appeared in April 2024 [src:kyivpost-2024-turtle-tanks].
- **Pokrova went live in early 2024**, and its Lima component deployed from July 2024 [src:militarnyi-2026-khomenko-pokrova-lima; src:kyivpost-2026-lima].
- **Russian firmware logistics became a target.** Russian units reflash thousands of DJIs every month from central servers. The IT Army claims it disrupted those servers in February 2024 [src:euromaidan-2025-martyniuk-drone-firmware].
**Fields.** East of Kupiansk the shelterbelt grid runs WNW–ESE and NNE–SSW: 0.62 km of belt per km², with main belts about 1.1 km apart (measured from OSM) [src:osm-overpass-2026-landscape-sample].

**Strength.**
- *Defenders.* About 10,000 (Forbes) [src:forbes-2024-axe-bradleys-t90].
- *Men at risk in the north.* "Potentially 2,000-4,000 men" of three brigades (Kyiv Post, 16 Feb) [src:kyivpost-2024-korshak-zenit-withdrawal].

- **Tech tree with obsolescence timers.** Each item has an effectiveness curve that decays once the enemy fields a counter. The lags from section 2 give plausible decay times:
  - Frequency moves: weeks. A band change can be a firmware push, so model it as a software event that needs no factory time [src:pravda-2025-fpv-ew-shield].
  - Cages and antennas: 3–9 months.
  - Systemic counters (Starlink, GPS weapons, mesh, satellite constellations): 6–24 months.
  - Excalibur's fall from 55% to 6% is a ready-made decay curve.
- **EW bubbles as map layers.** Model GNSS-denial fields (Pole-21, Zhitel, Lima/Pokrova) separately from control- and video-link jamming domes (trench, vehicle and backpack jammers). Each field has a band set. A drone with a matching band, or a fibre, autonomy, mesh or CRPA upgrade, ignores the corresponding bubble. Dome radius is about 200–300 m for omni jammers and several km for directional ones [src:pravda-2025-fpv-ew-shield].
- **Friendly-fire toggle.** Friendly jamming also blocks your own drones, so let players schedule "EW pauses" to launch strikes [src:rusi-2025-watling-third-year]. Lima-Quant's makers say brigade commanders switch it off because it blinds their own Mavics, a direct trade-off between strategic protection and tactical ISR [src:forbes-2026-hambling-lima-quant].
- **CRPA arms race as a ladder.** Each Russian CRPA tier (4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24) needs more jammers or a new Ukrainian technique. The late tiers break the "one jammer per element" rule [src:forbes-2026-hambling-lima-quant; src:euromaidan-2026-mukhina-crpa-20]. The end state is optical terrain matching, which ignores GNSS jamming altogether [src:militarnyi-2026-leonov-geran-5-optical].
- **Emission signatures.** Every emitter (jammer, drone ground station, Starlink dish, Volna uplink jammer) adds to a detectable signature. Direction finding and EW-hunting FPVs let the enemy strike emitters, so "emit and die" is a trade-off rather than a free buff [src:militarnyi-2025-kushnikov-ew-hunter-fpv; src:rusi-2023-watling-stormbreak]. Big emitters are rare and valuable: 24 Zhitels confirmed hit in four years, some 55 km deep [src:militarnyi-2026-pryhodko-lasars-zhitel; src:euromaidan-2026-mukhina-zhitel-55km].
- **Comms backbone as a strategic toggle.** Starlink access is an event-driven, side-specific modifier. Its removal in February 2026 should cut enemy drone effectiveness by roughly 20–40% for weeks, with partial recovery over one to two months as workarounds come online [src:isw-2026-feb-26-assessment]. The recovery paths are separate techs:
  - Terrestrial mesh: 150–175 km range, but needs relay towers you can strike [src:militarnyi-2026-khomenko-mesh-175km].
  - Fibre.
  - Rassvet: model it as scheduled satellite windows that lengthen with each launch [src:euromaidan-2026-thomas-isw-rassvet].
- **Satcom jamming is partial.** Model anti-Starlink jammers as packet loss (0–35%) in a cell about 17 km across rather than as a blackout. Unhardened drone video fails; hardened C2 degrades [src:militarnyi-2026-stepanets-ew-vs-starlink].
- **Detector blindness.** Analogue-video detectors (Chuika) warn infantry only while the enemy uses analogue video in covered bands. Digital video removes the warning until a bearing-only detector is researched [src:euromaidan-2026-mukhina-molniya-digital; src:militarnyi-2026-khomenko-chuika-4].
- **Fibre vs nets vs autonomy** are three counters to EW, each with its own cost:
  - **Fibre:** limited range, snag risk, visible cable. Adoption can reach 70% of a force's drones [src:euromaidan-2026-vivdych-ng-fibre-70].
  - **Nets:** fixed infrastructure, which burns and can be bypassed.
  - **Autonomy:** needs machine-vision research, and the unit costs 10–20% more.
- **Active protection as ammunition.** APS should hold a finite load that saturation attacks deplete: 7 FPVs emptied an Arena-M, and the kill took 15–20 [src:militarnyi-2026-pryhodko-aps-80].
- **Gun air defence has a reliability roll.** Guns are cheap per kill and good for point defence (about 4 km), but can fail mid-engagement [src:militarnyi-2025-shumlianskyi-skynex-shaheds; src:militarnyi-2026-khomenko-skynex-issues].
- **Strike-war economics.** Interceptor effectiveness against piston Shaheds should drop sharply when jet Gerans enter the enemy mix. Mobile fire groups and propeller interceptors should become near-useless against jets until a jet-interceptor tech with machine-vision lock is researched [src:euromaidan-2026-mukhina-jet-interceptors; src:pravda-2026-ihnat-jet-drones].
- **Thermal masking is partial.** Anti-thermal ponchos should reduce detection probability at range, not grant invisibility, and moving cancels most of the benefit [src:militarnyi-2025-yan-russian-thermal-ponchos].

From 16 to 19 August air strikes and HIMARS dropped the three Seim road bridges in Glushkovo Raion. That isolated the Russian troops between the river and the border [src:isw-2024-08-16-roca; src:isw-2024-08-19-roca; src:militarnyi-2024-kursk-crossings-osa]. The advance peaked in late August at a claimed 1,250–1,300 km², then turned into a positional defence [src:kyivindependent-2024-denisova-92-settlements; src:isw-2024-08-28-roca].

  - Massed fires from two artillery brigades blunted the drive on Kyiv [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons].
  - The 72nd's 2S3 batteries rotated between four positions each [src:mwi-2025-collins-spencer-battle-of-kyiv].
  - Artillery fired on the runway at Hostomel [src:bar-2024-sladden-collins-connable-irpin-river] and on pontoon sites plotted in advance [src:nyt-2022-kramer-demydiv-flood].
  - Fire was called in over WhatsApp [src:swj-2022-rice-untold-story-battle-kyiv] or from civilian phone calls: an artillery strike destroyed a refuelling point after a woman phoned it in [src:mwi-2025-collins-spencer-battle-of-kyiv].
- **Demolition and water.** Bridges were blown on 25–27 Feb, though few on day one [src:mwi-2025-collins-spencer-battle-of-kyiv]. Two dam and sluice breaches flooded the floodplain [src:mwi-2025-collins-spencer-battle-of-kyiv] [src:wapo-2022-sonne-battle-for-kyiv]. Russian intelligence "did not foresee the use of hydrotechnical structures" [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons]. The Russians made "a dozen or more wet gap crossings" with pontoons, and most were destroyed by fire [src:mwi-2025-collins-spencer-battle-of-kyiv]. RFE/RL says three pontoons at Moshchun, two of them destroyed [src:rferl-2023-dzhulay-furlong-moshchun-dam].
- **Head-and-tail ambushes.**
  - Vokzalna: an ATGM on the lead vehicle, an RPG on the trail vehicle, then artillery for 10–20 minutes on a column in "parade formation" [src:mwi-2025-collins-spencer-battle-of-kyiv].
  - Irpin: NLAWs on the lead and trail vehicles [src:swj-2022-rice-untold-story-battle-kyiv].
  - Brovary (v01) [src:nyt-2022-kramer-brovary-tanks].
  - Javelins at the convoy's head made "a roadblock", according to a US official [src:abc-au-2022-convoy-dispersed].
- **Drones.** Aerorozvidka's night teams carried thermal drones, 1.5 kg bomblets, night-vision goggles, sniper rifles and remote mines [src:guardian-2022-borger-aerorozvidka-convoy]. They launched when Russian jamming was off, ran after launch, prioritised EW vehicles and fed Delta and Starlink to the artillery [src:guardian-2022-borger-aerorozvidka-convoy]. A Furia UAV cued fire on the Rakivka pontoon [src:mwi-2025-collins-spencer-battle-of-kyiv]. Russian jamming at Moshchun "made Ukrainian drones inoperable" [src:wapo-2022-sonne-battle-for-kyiv]. TB2s hit SAMs, guns and trucks early on, but their emissions made them trackable [src:thenational-2022-harding-drone-strikes].
- **Air defence and the air war (the vignette).**
  - *Opening:* jamming and decoys hit S-300 and Buk hardest "to the north of Kyiv along the Hostomel/Irpin and Chernihiv axes". Fighters carried the air defence for the first days [src:rusi-2022-bronk-russian-air-war]. Two SAM sites screening the Dnipro were destroyed, which opened the helicopter route [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons].
  - *Russian SAM chaos:* Russian SAMs assumed "anything flying was Russian" [src:rusi-2022-bronk-russian-air-war].
  - *Ukrainian SAMs recover:* lone Buk TELARs and surviving S-300s acted as "pop-up" threats and made medium altitude "prohibitively dangerous" from 3 Mar [src:rusi-2022-bronk-russian-air-war].
  - *MANPADS:* the VKS flew at 500 ft or below and lost at least eight jets in a week [src:rusi-2022-bronk-russian-air-war]. Stinger and Igla were "a major factor" [src:twz-2022-trevithick-terrible-day].
  - *Russian counters:* Su-35S CAPs with R-77-1s outranged Ukraine's R-27s, at "up to 15:2" odds (6:2 per Zabrodskyi) [src:rusi-2022-bronk-russian-air-war] [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons]. S-400s and a Podlet-K1 radar in Belarus forced Ukrainian jets below 100 ft [src:rusi-2022-bronk-russian-air-war]. From 9 Mar the VKS switched to night Su-34 sorties, because MANPADS crews lacked night-vision goggles [src:rusi-2022-bronk-russian-air-war].
  - *Deconfliction:* time slots until 3 Mar, then areas after friendly fire [src:rusi-2022-bronk-russian-air-war].
- **Russian helicopters.** Ka-52s led the gunships and suffered disproportionately. They often failed to dispense flares when engaged by MANPADS [src:rusi-2022-bronk-russian-air-war].
- **Russian logistics.** Columns carried 3–4 days of supply [src:mwi-2025-collins-spencer-battle-of-kyiv] and used Belarusian railways [src:isw-2022-02-27-roca]. They were short of fuel, food and spare parts [src:defenseone-2022-copp-convoy-stalled]. The BBC adds tyres, the mud and C2 failures [src:bbc-2022-why-convoy-stopped]. By 22 Mar some troops had frostbite for lack of winter gear [src:kyivindependent-2022-pentagon-short-food-fuel].
- **Withdrawal technique.** Russia covered the withdrawal with heavy artillery, mined the routes and blew bridges Ukraine had failed to destroy on day one [src:mwi-2025-collins-spencer-battle-of-kyiv] [src:euromaidan-2022-day-38-kyiv-recaptured].
Boats moved mainly at night [src:kyivpost-2024-korshak-krynky-drones], and evacuation boats were called "at night" [src:slidstvo-2024-stanko-krynky-hell].

Across all eras, the aid picture shifts from US-led gifting (2022–2024), through the US drawdown and the two brief 2025 pauses, to European-financed support and European purchases of US weapons via PURL (2025–2026) [src:kiel-2026-trebesch-four-years] [src:kiel-2026-nishikawa-h1-2026] [src:crs-2026-if12040-us-security-assistance]. From March 2026 the US–Iran war competes for the same Patriot and ATACMS stocks (e9) [src:cnn-2026-cohen-interceptors-depleted]. As of late Sep 2026 there is no durable ceasefire. Russia still demands all of Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson oblasts, neutrality and demilitarization, and Ukraine refuses [src:csmonitor-2026-weir-peace-talks] [src:isw-2026-09-06-roca].

**Strength, as claimed.**
- *Ukrainian estimates of the Russian force.* About 40,000 (Shtupun, 29 Oct, and again in January) [src:isw-2023-10-29-roca] [src:isw-2024-01-21-roca]. About 50,000 (Lykhovii, Feb) [src:isw-2024-02-15-roca]. About 15,000 assault troops in the 3rd Assault's sector [src:kyivindependent-2024-fornusek-3rd-assault-15000].
- *Ratios in the final weeks.* Foka of the 3rd Assault: four Russian brigades rotating with two in reserve, and odds of 1:12 in infantry and 1:10 in artillery and ammunition [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-last-days-avdiivka]. 3rd Assault statements: 7:1 [src:kyivpost-2024-korshak-zenit-withdrawal].
- *Forbes.* Two field armies of about 40,000 against about 10,000 defenders [src:forbes-2024-axe-bradleys-t90].
- *Equipment.* The vehicle fleet was mostly Soviet-era. Only about 22% of tank losses were modern T-72B3, T-80BVM or T-90 types; 65 T-80BVs were lost; and 77 of 173 lost IFVs were BMP-1s [src:theinsider-2024-meat-grinder-avdiivka].

**Hostomel.** On 24 February about 34 helicopters landed 200–300 VDV at Hostomel. Fewer than 200 National Guard conscripts held them for more than an hour before withdrawing. The follow-on Il-76 airlift was aborted in mid-air [src:wotr-2023-collins-kofman-spencer-hostomel] [src:bar-2024-sladden-collins-connable-irpin-river]. A Ukrainian counterattack at sunset retook the field by 21:00 and cratered the runway. The Russians had the airport back on 25 February, but only when the mechanised column from Belarus arrived [src:wotr-2023-collins-kofman-spencer-hostomel] [src:isw-2022-02-25-roca].

## 9. Terms

At the materiel level (cages, antennas, fibre spools, interceptors), the lag is typically 3–9 months. At the systemic level (Starlink, US GPS weapons, mesh networks, satellite constellations), it is 6–24 months. KSE describes Ukraine's "development – combat testing – modification" loop as running in months, with innovation cycles "measured in weeks" [src:kse-2025-drone-innovations]. RUSI's lesson for everyone is that holding a technological edge "requires the ability to rapidly update systems in the field" [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].

**The east and the turn.** East of the Dnipro the Russian columns were stopped at Chernihiv and at Brovary [src:wapo-2022-sonne-battle-for-kyiv] [src:mwi-2025-collins-spencer-battle-of-kyiv]. ISW judged on 19 March that the campaign to seize the capital had failed [src:isw-2022-03-19-roca]. On 29 March Russia announced in Istanbul that it would "drastically reduce" activity around Kyiv and Chernihiv [src:euromaidan-2022-day-35-kyiv-attacks]. On 2 April Deputy Defence Minister Maliar declared the whole Kyiv region liberated [src:aljazeera-2022-kyiv-region-retaken] [src:cnn-2022-murphy-antonov-withdrawal-maxar].
## 10. Game/sim relevance

- **The convict army.** Wagner began recruiting in Russian prisons on 1 July 2022 and enlisted at least 48,000 convicts before the scheme ended in February 2023 [src:mediazona-2024-price-of-bakhmut]. It threw them at the city's eastern and southern edges from August in small assault groups, with executions for retreat [src:isw-2022-08-01-roca] [src:cnn-2023-lister-wagner-tactics-report].
- **The autumn grind.** Through the autumn the front barely moved: Prigozhin's own figure was 100–200 m a day [src:isw-2023-01-03-roca]. The city became a symbol. Zelensky visited on 20 December and took the defenders' flag to the US Congress the next day [src:president-2022-zelensky-bakhmut-visit-awards] [src:pbs-2022-freking-zelensky-dc-visit].
- **The winter pincers.** In January Wagner, joined by VDV and other regular troops, took Soledar to the north-east (12–16 Jan). It then swung round the city's north (Krasna Hora, Paraskoviivka, Berkhivka, Yahidne) and south (Klishchiivka, Ivanivske) [src:isw-2023-01-13-roca] [src:isw-2023-01-31-roca] [src:isw-2023-02-27-roca].
- **The decision to hold.** Ukraine debated withdrawing, and the US advised it [src:wapo-2023-khurshudyan-short-of-skilled-troops]. In early March Ukraine gave up the east bank of the Bakhmutka but chose to reinforce the rest [src:isw-2023-03-07-roca] [src:isw-2023-03-06-roca].
- **The fall of the city.** Wagner took the city block by block: the AZOM plant about 28 March, the city hall on 2 April, about 76% of the city by 11 April [src:isw-2023-03-29-roca] [src:isw-2023-04-03-roca] [src:isw-2023-04-11-roca].
- **The feud.** Prigozhin fought the MoD in public over shells, and on 5 May threatened to leave [src:isw-2023-05-05-roca].
- **The end.** From 9 May Ukrainian brigades counterattacked the weak Russian regulars on the flanks [src:isw-2023-05-10-roca]. Wagner took the last western blocks anyway, and on 20 May Prigozhin declared the city captured [src:isw-2023-05-20-roca]. Wagner handed over to the army from 25 May and mutinied a month later [src:isw-2023-05-25-roca] [src:meduza-2023-prigozhin-aborted-rebellion].
## 10. Game/sim relevance

**How forces changed over the window.**
- Feb–Apr: the *Moskva* knits island, rigs and fleet into one air-defence system [src:pravda-2022-romaniuk-zmiinyi-battle].
- After 14 Apr: the big ships pull back out of Neptune range [src:dod-2022-04-18-background-briefing] [src:navalnews-2022-sutton-curse-snake-island]. The island holds on with point defence brought in by small craft that TB2s hunt [src:navalnews-2022-sutton-tb2-ghost-snake-island].
- June: Harpoons and coastal guns make resupply impossible [src:zavhorodnii-2025-battles-snake-island].

**Terrain.**
- **Uphill all the way.** The ground climbs from the Kinska valley at Orikhiv (about 51–53 m) and Mala Tokmachka (about 68 m) to about 120–140 m on the Robotyne–Kopani ridge, peaking at about 152 m just south of Robotyne [src:opentopodata-srtm30m]. The attackers advanced up a long, open slope under observation.
- **Open steppe.** The Zaporizhzhia steppe is flat to gently rolling, which makes for long sight lines [src:cepa-2023-kallberg-treelines].
- **A grid of shelterbelts.** In the OSM and Sentinel-2 sample box around Robotyne, tree lines run roughly E–W and N–S. Main belts are about 0.5–0.6 km apart and cross-belts about 1.0–1.2 km apart, at 1.34 km of mapped belt per km² [src:osm-overpass-2026-landscape-sample] [src:eox-2021-s2cloudless]. Kofman and Lee: "a war of tree lines, with shifts in the line often counted in hundreds of meters" [src:warontherocks-2023-kofman-lee-three-months].
- **Ravines.** Balkas separate the "platforms", as described at Rivnopil on the neighbouring axis [src:euromaidan-2023-rivnopil-heights]. The Balka Uspenivka southeast of Orikhiv was a named fighting area [src:isw-2023-08-22-roca].
- **Dams.** A Ukrainian mine-action officer reported that Russia was regularly blowing up small dams in the south to disrupt Ukrainian operations [src:isw-2023-06-13-roca].
## 8. Media
## 7. Data access and licensing

**Rail.**
- Kupiansk-Vuzlovyi is the junction. It has lines to Kharkiv, Sviatohirsk and Sievierodonetsk, and via Kupiansk to Stary Oskol in Russia; the Belgorod–Vovchansk–Kupiansk line dates from 1901 [src:wikipedia-kupiansk-vuzlovyi].
- Novaya Gazeta Europe names two lines from Kupiansk into Russia, via Vovchansk to Belgorod and via Valuyki. They fed Russian forces at Kharkiv, Sloviansk, Bakhmut and Donetsk [src:novayagazeta-2022-fedorov-dual-pushback].
- After Kupiansk fell, Russia had to route logistics through the Valuyki line [src:isw-2022-09-16-roca]. Syniehubov called Kupiansk-Vuzlovyi "one of the biggest logistical railway routes" in the oblast [src:pravda-2022-roshchina-kupiansk-vuzlovyi].
- Lyman is a rail hub carrying up to 30% of Donetsk railway cargo [src:wikipedia-lyman-ukraine]. Wikipedia lists Balakliia, Shevchenkove, Kupiansk and Izium as the key logistics nodes Russia had held since the spring [src:wikipedia-2022-kharkiv-counteroffensive].
- Russian Railway Troops rebuild bridges, for example a pontoon rail bridge at Kupiansk [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons].
## 7. Terms
## 4. Forces

**Adaptations Russia led:**
- **Fibre-optic FPVs.** KVN, developed through the Ushkuinik accelerator, and the Rubicon unit [src:kyivindependent-2025-farrell-fiber-optic].
- **Multi-element CRPA (Kometa-M)** on Shaheds, UMPK glide-bomb kits and Iskander-K [src:defenseexpress-2025-kometa-m-16]. It then moved to a new CRPA series that beats jammer-count arithmetic [src:forbes-2026-hambling-lima-quant].
- **Mesh radio control** of Gerans and Gerbera via Chinese COFDM modems and relay towers [src:euromaidan-2026-vivdych-xk-f358; src:militarnyi-2026-khomenko-mesh-175km].
- **Vehicle cages and "turtles"** [src:kyivpost-2024-turtle-tanks].
- **Road nets** [src:defenseexpress-2025-russian-net-tunnels].
- **Kh-101 improvements** for EW-resistant terminal navigation [src:rusi-2025-watling-third-year].
- **Frequency hopping on Molniya** [src:euromaidan-2026-mukhina-molniya], then digital video [src:euromaidan-2026-mukhina-molniya-digital].
- **Jet Gerans** [src:united24-2026-place-jet-gerans].
## 10. Game/sim relevance

- **Where to strike (summer 2022).**
  - The General Staff asked for diversions to support Kherson. Syrskyi chose the seam between the Izium stronghold and the Belgorod bases, because the Russians thought "you'd have to be crazy" to strike there [src:wapo-2022-khurshudyan-inside-counteroffensive].
  - RUSI judges the choice by three factors: Russian weakness, Izium's role as a springboard for attacks on Donbas, and Russian artillery in range of Kharkiv [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].
  - Zelensky approved the plan in mid-August as "a large swath of territory with minimal resources and losses" [src:wapo-2022-khurshudyan-inside-counteroffensive].
- **How to fight: bypass and speed over reduction.** Syrskyi: "Everything depended on the first day — how far we could break through." The stated risk was Russian reserves arriving from across the border and cutting off Ukrainians behind the lines [src:wapo-2022-khurshudyan-inside-counteroffensive].
- **Stripping other sectors.** Ukraine took M777s and drones from hotter sectors to give each attacking brigade at least eight howitzers, with tens of thousands of rounds against a feared need of over 100,000 [src:wapo-2022-khurshudyan-inside-counteroffensive].
- **Was it a surprise? (debated).**
  - RUSI: Russia saw the build-up but had no forces to respond. Ukraine surprised it on timing, not intent [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].
  - The Balakliia papers show Russian officers expected an attack "to take control of Balakliia" from late July [src:reuters-2022-saito-balakliia-base]. Milbloggers had warned for days [src:isw-2022-09-08-roca].
  - Syrskyi says the information "didn't reach anyone or it wasn't taken into account" [src:wapo-2022-khurshudyan-inside-counteroffensive].
- **Exploit into Izium early (about 9–10 Sep).** At battalion level the plan was changed from halting on a ridge north of Izium to entering the city, once intelligence showed "half the units in Izium… are simply fleeing" [src:wapo-2022-khurshudyan-inside-counteroffensive].
- **Russia: stand or run (9–11 Sep).** Moscow first sent convoys and helicopters [src:isw-2022-09-09-roca], then ordered withdrawal behind the Oskil and called it a regrouping [src:isw-2022-09-10-roca].
  - ISW judged that Russia lacked the reserves to build an Oskil line, and that prudence demanded pulling forces from other sectors to a line further east [src:isw-2022-09-11-roca]. Instead, Lapin kept attacking at Bakhmut [src:isw-2022-09-12-roca].
  - Posen argues the opposite: Russia had deliberately economised in Kharkiv, may have "chosen to accept the loss", and saved most of its units [src:foreignpolicy-2023-posen-breakthrough].
- **When to stop: the Oskil (11–13 Sep).**
  - Ukraine halted the main advance at the Oskil around 11 Sep [src:isw-2022-09-16-roca]. ISW repeatedly said Ukraine could cross "if they choose", because Russia was too weak to hold the whole river [src:isw-2022-09-10-roca; src:isw-2022-09-13-roca].
  - Defence Minister Reznikov stressed the need to secure the retaken ground against a counterattack on stretched supply lines [src:aljazeera-2022-ganchev-eight-times].
  - The chosen course was local bridgeheads (Borova, Kupiansk, Dvorichna) rather than a second leap [src:isw-2022-09-13-roca; src:isw-2022-09-19-roca]. The sources found give no fuller account of the Ukrainian reasoning.
- **Next objective: Lyman.** After a week in Izium, the 25th was redirected south-east to Lyman [src:wapo-2022-khurshudyan-inside-counteroffensive]. The pincer came from Sviatohirsk and the Oskil, and cut the Drobysheve–Torske road rather than storming the town [src:wikipedia-2022-lyman-front; src:isw-2022-09-30-roca].
- **Russia: reinforce Lyman or the south?** ISW assessed that the decision not to reinforce Kupiansk and Lyman was almost certainly Putin's, prioritising Kherson and Zaporizhzhia [src:isw-2022-10-01-roca].
- **Russia: mobilise.** The breakthrough exposed how stretched Russia was, and mobilisation followed on 21 Sep [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons; src:wikipedia-2022-russian-mobilization].
- **The lesson that misled 2023.** RUSI says 2023 planners believed Russia's Kharkiv collapse came from poor morale, when it really came from a shortage of troops [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].

**Map.** The core map is Kyiv city astride the Dnipro, with a ring of approach about 50 km deep. The outer ring shows the corridors from the launch areas.
- **The two banks.** The Dnipro splits the city. The right (west) bank holds the historic centre, the government quarter and the Shevchenkivskyi, Pecherskyi, Holosiivskyi, Solomianskyi, Sviatoshynskyi, Obolonskyi and Podilskyi districts. The left (east) bank holds Darnytskyi, Dniprovskyi and Desnianskyi. This is our reading of the OSM district positions [src:osm-photon-c18].
- **The hardest-hit district.** Darnytskyi, the left-bank south-east [src:bbc-2026-rainsford-most-massive-kyiv].

### Ukraine
## 11. Open questions/gaps

- **Exact withdrawal date.** "Several weeks" before 16 Jul 2024 (Suspilne). The last reported ground combat was on 11 Jul. Wikipedia uses 17 Jul. No official date exists [src:euromaidan-2024-tril-krynky-withdraw] [src:kyivpost-2024-korshak-krynky-retreat].
- **Ukrainian losses.** Official figures are a state secret. There is no breakdown of losses on the river versus in the village, or by brigade beyond "about 700" for one. The UALosses captured count is 54 or 64 [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-krynky-untold] [src:wikipedia-battle-of-krynky].
- **Russian losses after November 2023.** Only Lykhovii's ratio and Naalsio's equipment count exist. The November claim is variously printed as 1,216 or 1,126 KIA, and as 14 "watercraft", "boats" or "aircraft" [src:euromaidan-2023-zoria-marines-bridgeheads] [src:isw-2023-11-17-roca] [src:isw-2023-12-16-roca] [src:kyivindependent-2024-ostiller-krynky-lost]. The boats reading fits the Marine Corps release.
- **The Antonivskyi footholds.** Mashovets's 9 Nov claim of continuous control from the rail bridge to the road bridge conflicts with UP's account that both western footholds were abandoned by early November. A March 2024 return to the road bridge is reported only by Russian bloggers and Saldo [src:isw-2023-11-09-roca] [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-krynky-untold] [src:kyivpost-2024-korshak-krynky-drones].
- **Boat types and counts.** No full inventory: hulls, motors and losses per month. "US boats with pontoons" is not identified by model.
- **Russian strength figures** (64k → 120k) are expert estimates with no stated method.
- **Weather.** Fog days and river state (current, ice) were not sourced. The temperatures are modelled.
- **Timing of the raids before Krynky.** The Feb–Jun 2023 island raids and the unit roles in the summer raids are thinly documented. The best sources are UP and KI soldier testimony.
- **The parliamentary follow-up.** It is not known whether the defence committee ever held the hearing Bobrovska proposed.
- **Chemical weapons.** Testimony only, with no OPCW finding sourced here.

## 10. Game/sim relevance

Accessed 2026-10-01. English-language sources, with Ukrainian outlets paired with Western analysis and OSINT. Russian statements appear only as Ukrainian, Western or independent Russian outlets report them. Loss figures are **claims**, and the claimant is always named.

**The night of 26–27 July: "cheese".** At about 22:55, eight rockets hit the Antonivskyi road bridge and two hit the rail bridge 6 km upstream [src:wikipedia-antonivka-road-bridge] [src:isw-2022-07-27-roca]. Russian air defence lights up only after the impacts. The next morning the deck is holed across its full width, and the occupation administration closes the bridge to all traffic [src:isw-2022-07-27-roca]. A Ukrainian newspaper calls it "cheese" [src:wavellroom-2022-miller-river-too-far]. The weather is clear and the night warm [src:openmeteo-era5-kherson-2022]. A diorama can show the queue of trucks at the Oleshky end.

   - What followed: Pavlivka was taken, the brigade gutted, and the same command repeated the plan in January [src:isw-2023-02-10-roca].
2. **Russia: the purpose of the January 2023 attack.** The sources disagree.
   - ISW first read it as an information operation or spoiling attack to distract from Bakhmut [src:isw-2023-01-24-roca] [src:isw-2023-01-25-roca].
   - The UK MoD saw a "concerted offensive assault" to open a new axis [src:isw-2023-01-31-roca].
   - Kyiv Post's sources later said the aim was to cut off the whole Ukrainian Donbas grouping and break through here rather than at Bakhmut [src:kyivpost-2024-kostezh-why-lost].
   - The UK MoD also suggested the MoD wanted a success of its own to rival Wagner [src:novayagazeta-2023-ukmod-raam].
3. **Ukraine: rapid reinforcement in late January.** A Kremlin-affiliated milblogger judged that the Russians lost the initiative by the end of January "due to Ukrainian forces' rapid transfer of reserves" [src:isw-2023-02-11-roca]. Pushilin likewise blamed reserves "in large quantities" [src:cnn-2023-lister-vuhledar-turkeys]. Which reserves came from where is not public.
4. **Ukraine: the kill-zone design.** Leaving the roads clear and mining the shoulders, rather than blocking the roads, was a deliberate choice to draw columns in [src:nyt-2023-kramer-epic-tank-battle]. Firing RAAM into freshly cleared lanes broke with the Soviet practice of laying narrow belts just before an attack [src:forbes-2023-axe-minefield-raam].
5. **Russia: columns on the same routes.**
   - The repeated choice to send columns down the same narrow approaches drew fire from milbloggers, who wanted Muradov tried [src:isw-2023-02-10-roca].
   - Some argued the units had no alternative: no communications, no situational awareness, "blind, deaf tanks" [src:cnn-2023-lister-vuhledar-turkeys], or a lack of demining equipment [src:moscowtimes-2023-muradov-dismissed].
   - ISW put the cause in training [src:isw-2023-02-10-roca].
6. **Ukraine: spending HIMARS on tactical targets.** Commanders called in HIMARS against a stalled column, though it was normally reserved for depots and barracks [src:nyt-2023-kramer-epic-tank-battle].
7. **Russia: switching to infantry (late February).** After losing "so many machines", Russia attacked only with infantry [src:nyt-2023-kramer-epic-tank-battle], at the cost the notebook records [src:forbes-2023-axe-diary-1100].
8. **Russia: "at any cost" (4–5 March).** Ukraine's General Staff reported that Shoigu ordered Muradov to take Vuhledar at any cost amid a dispute between them. ISW judged a renewed offensive impossible without new reserves [src:isw-2023-03-05-roca]. Muradov's reported dismissal followed on 3 April [src:moscowtimes-2023-muradov-dismissed].
9. **Epilogue, Ukraine: when to leave (Sep – Oct 2024).**
   - The Khortytsia group says higher command authorised the withdrawal [src:kyivindependent-2024-denisova-withdraw-vuhledar].
   - A 72nd soldier told Kyiv Post that "the order to withdraw was never given", and analyst Kuzan said rotating the brigade was discussed but no reserves existed [src:kyivpost-2024-kostezh-why-lost].
   - The new brigade commander called the town untenable with the forces available [src:hromadske-2024-okhrimenko-withdrawal].

## 8. Open questions and gaps

- **Russia refined its "reconnaissance-strike complex"** [src:rusi-2023-watling-meatgrinder]:
  - Kill chain: 3–5 minutes from drone detection to fires, 20–30 minutes from an electronic-warfare (EW) detection.
  - Strelets (a reconnaissance/fire-control data system) was widely used by VDV (airborne), Wagner and recon specialists.
  - EW: about one major system per 10 km of front, sited about 7 km behind the line. Ukrainian drone losses were about **10,000 per month**.
  - Russian EW reportedly decrypted Ukrainian Motorola traffic in near real time.
- **Russian C2 hardened:**
  - HQs dispersed and were wired to forward command posts (CPs), often through the captured Ukrainian civilian telecoms network.
  - Brigade CPs sat about 20 km back, underground.
  - Below battalion level, much traffic was still sent in the clear on analogue radios [src:rusi-2023-watling-meatgrinder].

1. **Manoeuvre and shock, 2022 (e1–e3).** Russia's plan for a quick decapitation fails near Kyiv. Russian massed artillery grinds forward in Donbas in summer. Ukraine then exploits an overstretched Russian force in Kharkiv Oblast and levers Russia out of right-bank Kherson. Russia answers with mobilization, annexation claims and a long-range strike campaign using Iranian-designed Shaheds [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons] [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons] [src:wikipedia-russo-ukrainian-war].
2. **Attrition and the failed breakthrough, 2023 to mid-2024 (e4–e6).** Wagner and convict "meat assaults" take Bakhmut. Ukraine's Western-equipped 2023 offensive stalls in about 30 km of prepared Russian defences. Then, while US aid is stalled, Russia uses its shell and glide-bomb superiority to take Avdiivka [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons] [src:euromaidanpress-2024-tril-avdiivka].
3. **The drone-dominated war, mid-2024 to 2026 (e7–e9).** Tactical UAVs become the main killer, and the "kill zone" makes manoeuvre very costly [src:rusi-2025-watling-third-year]. Russia buys slow gains at huge cost: about 3,600 km² in 2024 and about 4,300–4,800 km² in 2025, depending on the tracker [src:csis-2026-jones-10-charts] [src:kyivindependent-2026-basmat-deepstate-2025]. Ukraine raids Kursk, strikes deep (Spiderweb), and scales interceptor drones against about 50,000 Shaheds a year. From late January 2026 it turns local counterattacks into real gains, helped by Russia's loss of Starlink, and by September ISW assesses that Russia has made "near-zero net gains since March 2026" [src:pravda-2026-romanenko-dshv-745] [src:isw-2026-02-12-assessment] [src:isw-2026-09-26-assessment].

**Underwater charges (Act 3).**
- Charges were placed at the supports over several months and fired starting at 04:44 [src:pravda-2025-prots-third-strike].
- The method is undisclosed. Russian milbloggers guessed a sea drone [src:reuters-2025-polityuk-underwater], and Euromaidan inferred underwater drones [src:euromaidan-2025-third-strike].
- The barrier system above was built against surface and underwater *drones*. It did not stop charges laid by agents.

**Map frame.** The playable box is the city and coast (about 47.03–47.23 N, 37.47–37.76 E, the OSM city bounds) [src:osm-nominatim-c03-places]. Off-map are the air-corridor route to Dnipro and the epilogue sites (Olenivka, Novoazovsk).

**The island as terrain.**
- Bare rock with steep shores and no trees [src:wikipedia-snake-island-campaign] [src:pravda-2022-romaniuk-zmiinyi-battle].
- Hard to dig into, so shelters protect against splinters, not bombs [src:pravda-2022-romaniuk-zmiinyi-battle].
- Features to model:
  - A lighthouse on the southern point, used by the Su-27s as their aiming mark [src:twz-2022-payne-su27-snake-island].
  - A pier and the island's "only operable boat ramp" on the north side, where the Serna wreck blocked landings [src:navalnews-2022-sutton-tb2-ghost-snake-island] [src:spacecom-2022-wall-maxar-snake-island].
  - The main building complex above the pier, and the east point (ammunition and fuel) [src:twz-2022-payne-su27-snake-island].
  - Radars, towers and antennas, destroyed on 24 Feb [src:ukrinform-2022-zmiinyi-defenders-alive].

**Strength.**
- **On the axis (RUSI).** Up to 105,000 troops, about 470 tanks, up to 1,410 AFVs, 720+ guns, up to 230 MLRS and 12 operational-tactical missile complexes. Each 10 km of front was held by a motor-rifle regiment plus an airborne regiment. There were 35 days of ammunition at the guns and about 60 attack helicopters [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].
- **On 8 Jun (Forbes, via Wikipedia).** "Perhaps 10,000 or more" in the 42nd Division's regiments near Tokmak [src:wikipedia-battle-of-mala-tokmachka].
- **Aviation.** 27 helicopters at Berdiansk by 13 Jun, including 5 Ka-52 [src:isw-2023-06-14-roca].
