Links only; nothing downloaded. The licence of embedded footage is generally unstated, so treat it as all rights reserved by the publisher or original poster.
The five "unit leaders of the defence of Azovstal" freed on 21 Sep 2022 were Prokopenko, Volynskyi, Palamar, Denys Shleha and Oleh Khomenko [src:pravda-2022-swap-215-medvedchuk].

- **Snake Island, 24–25 Feb.** As reported by Western and Ukrainian outlets:
  - The MoD (Konashenkov) said 82 Ukrainian servicemen surrendered voluntarily, signed pledges and would be released [src:wikipedia-snake-island-campaign].
  - Russia claimed it sank 6 of 16 Ukrainian boats that attacked on 25 Feb, and accused the US of helping. The US denied it [src:wikipedia-snake-island-campaign].
- ***Moskva*, 14 Apr.**
  - The MoD said a fire detonated ammunition, the fire was contained, and the crew was evacuated. Later that day: the ship "lost stability … in the stormy sea conditions" under tow and sank. It made no mention of a strike [src:reuters-2022-moskva-sunk] [src:isw-2022-04-14-assessment].
  - On 16 Apr the MoD showed Adm. Yevmenov meeting about 100 crew [src:meduza-2022-moskva-37-dead].
  - On 22 Apr it gave 1 dead, 27 missing and 396 rescued [src:wikipedia-sinking-of-the-moskva].
  - A Sevastopol court declared 17 dead in Nov 2022 [src:meduza-2022-moskva-17-declared-dead].
  - In Jan 2026 a Moscow court acknowledged the Ukrainian missile, named Shubin, found 20 dead, 24 injured and 8 missing, and claimed 2.2 bn roubles [src:rbcukraine-2026-court-moskva].
  - State-TV figures criticised the navy, and some blamed Norwegian missiles or US electronics. Russia sent the 1915 salvage ship *Kommuna* to the wreck [src:wikipedia-sinking-of-the-moskva].
- **May–June.**
  - The MoD claimed to have repelled the May assault and killed "more than 50" paratroopers [src:pravda-2022-romaniuk-zmiinyi-battle].
  - It claimed every Ukrainian drone and missile attack in June was defeated. ISW: "despite considerable evidence to the contrary" [src:isw-2022-06-30-assessment].
  - Russian media gave 10 missing and 23 injured on the *Vasily Bekh* [src:twz-2022-newdick-harpoon-bekh].
- **30 Jun.** The MoD said the tasks were "completed", and that the withdrawal was a "goodwill gesture" so as not to obstruct UN grain-corridor efforts [src:zavhorodnii-2025-battles-snake-island] [src:pravda-2022-balachuk-zaluzhnyi-bohdana].
  - Milbloggers followed the line and ignored the strikes [src:isw-2022-06-30-assessment].
  - The DoD saw "no credence" in the goodwill claim [src:dod-2022-vergun-snake-island-retreat].
- **7 Jul.** The MoD said a 05:00 flag landing was hit by missiles, "killing some of the Ukrainian troops". Ukraine denied any deaths [src:twz-2022-altman-flag-snake-island].
Snow depth stayed at 0–3 cm through the window [src:open-meteo-2026-era5-c01-hostomel].

- **Starlink whitelist.** It was ordered on 2 February and Russian terminals were blocked by 5 February [src:kyivindependent-2026-myronyshena-starlink-whitelist; src:ukrinform-2026-liskovych-starlink-c2]. ISW dates the block to 1 February [src:isw-2026-feb-26-assessment].
  - Beskrestnov: Russia's "entire C2 system has collapsed".
  - ISW, 8 Feb: Russian milbloggers say units need radio and satellite donations and run communications "on the ground". A Ukrainian brigade reports degraded Russian C2 and drone operations, but small-group assaults continue. ISW expects Russia to struggle to sustain its battlefield air interdiction (BAI) campaign [src:isw-2026-feb-08-assessment].
  - ISW, 26 Feb: Biletsky says Russian drone effectiveness fell by roughly 20–40% in two weeks. He expects partial recovery through other satcom within one to two months, but not Starlink-level efficiency for three to five years. ISW has observed reduced tempo and depth of Russian tactical and mid-range strikes [src:isw-2026-feb-26-assessment].
  - More than 200 km² retaken within 5 days, per the Atlantic Council [src:atlanticcouncil-2026-spencer-starlink-crisis].
  - Wikipedia's figure for the southern front is much smaller, "ten to twelve kilometers" [src:wikipedia-starlink-war], and ties it to an April start, so treat the gains as contested.
- **Russian recovery, Feb–Sep 2026.** It is partial and uneven, and it is moving to terrestrial mesh first and satellites second:
  - **Terrestrial links.** Ubiquiti radios already made up about 80% of Russian frontline links before the cut [src:militarnyi-2026-ubiquiti-80].
  - **Mesh.** Unsanctioned Chinese XK-F358 mesh modems (about $7,000–9,000) fly on Geran-5 and Gerbera [src:euromaidan-2026-vivdych-xk-f358]. Relay chains reach 150–175 km, about twice the 2025 range [src:militarnyi-2026-khomenko-mesh-175km]. Beskrestnov says nobody in the armed forces worked systematically on countering this mesh for a year [src:euromaidan-2026-mukhina-geran-mesh].
  - **Fibre.** Russian fibre FPVs reached Kharkiv's outskirts on 25 February, about 21 km from the border. Chinese optical fibre for Russian buyers rose from 16 to 40 yuan/km after Ukraine struck the Saransk fibre plant [src:isw-2026-feb-26-assessment].
  - **Rassvet.** 16 satellites were launched in March and 16 more in July. Only the 12 good first-batch satellites are at about 550 km, giving two daily windows over Ukraine totalling up to 90 minutes (ISW, 31 Aug) [src:euromaidan-2026-thomas-isw-rassvet]. Coverage grew from 6–10 minute passes in March to two windows of more than an hour each by late August [src:euromaidan-2026-vivdych-rassvet-windows]. Russia needs 200–300 satellites for 24/7 cover, and Soyuz-2.1b cadence caps it at about 128 in four years (ISW) [src:euromaidan-2026-thomas-isw-rassvet].
  - **"Kupol".** The reported "Kupol" system is the Volna Kupol Garant jammer. It is a counter to *Ukrainian* Starlink, not a replacement for Russia's (see below) [src:militarnyi-2026-shumlianskyi-volna-mass-production].
  - **Yamal/Express GEO terminals.** No fetched source was found.
- **Russia jams Ukraine's Starlink.** Volna Kupol Garant jams the 14–14.5 GHz uplink over about 20 km² per unit. It was reported deployed in June and announced as in serial production in August, with the Russian claim that Starlink is "shut down everywhere we need" [src:militarnyi-2026-pryhodko-volna-kupol-garant; src:militarnyi-2026-shumlianskyi-volna-mass-production].
  - A Ukrainian satcom engineer measures the effect of such systems as 0–35% packet loss inside a cell about 17 km across. That breaks unhardened drone video, but it is not a blackout [src:militarnyi-2026-stepanets-ew-vs-starlink].
  - Russian authors concede that the strategic Tobol and Tirada-2 satellite jammers have not been seen working against Starlink in combat [src:militarnyi-2026-glazyev-starlink-scenarios].
- **GNSS war at the top end.**
  - **Lima-Quant (April 2026).** Its developers claim KABs "dropped to zero" effectiveness on about 700 km of front, with 869 KABs in a month causing minor injuries to 8 soldiers, and 41 of 42 Kinzhals neutralised [src:forbes-2026-hambling-lima-quant].
  - **Night Watch (July 2026).** It claims 61 Kinzhals countered and says EW accounts for about half of all "intercepted" Shaheds and missiles [src:militarnyi-2026-kozatskyi-lima-half].
  - **Russia keeps climbing.** A 32-element CRPA (16 L1 plus 16 L2 elements) was recovered [src:militarnyi-2026-khomenko-crpa-32]. 20-element arrays were expected in September 2026 and 24-element ones in 2027 [src:euromaidan-2026-mukhina-crpa-20]. A Geran-5 with optical terrain matching is reported but unconfirmed [src:militarnyi-2026-leonov-geran-5-optical].
- **Interceptors took over the Shahed fight.** In February 2026 they flew about 6,300 sorties and made more than 1,500 kills; near Kyiv more than 70% of Shaheds fell to interceptors [src:isis-2026-anokhin-shahed-monthly].
  - Sting alone claimed more than 3,000 Shahed and Gerbera kills in May. The MoD counted 7,476 of 8,150 launches intercepted that month (91.7%) [src:pravda-2026-sting-3000].
  - They took more than 40% of Shahed kills on 24 May 2026 [src:militarnyi-2026-pryhodko-interceptors].
  - The Shahed hit rate fell to about 6.7% in May 2026 [src:isis-2026-anokhin-shahed-monthly]. Beskrestnov says 92–96% of piston Shaheds on deep-rear raids are stopped, which pushes Russia to jets for those raids [src:isis-2026-anokhin-shahed-monthly].
- **Guns: useful but fragile.** One Skynex battery claims about 35 Shaheds and 2 cruise missiles, 12 targets in a single engagement [src:militarnyi-2026-kozatskyi-skynex-12]. An internal report says two Skynex lost three of eight guns to faults within minutes on 1 April 2026 and let a Shahed through [src:militarnyi-2026-khomenko-skynex-issues].
- **Russia's answer was jet Gerans** [src:united24-2026-place-jet-gerans; src:euromaidan-2026-mukhina-jet-interceptors]:
  - About 3,000 Geran-4/5 a month, per HUR.
  - Interception rate against jets about 60%.
  - The first "ready" jet interceptors failed in combat.
  - Ihnat: at up to 500 km/h the jets outrun 300 km/h interceptors, so mobile fire groups and interceptors "can no longer be relied upon" against them and missiles must be used [src:pravda-2026-ihnat-jet-drones].
- **Radio-frequency adaptation is continuous.**
  - Molniya uses frequency hopping [src:euromaidan-2026-mukhina-molniya], and detectors need monthly updates [src:united24-2026-brizard-detectors].
  - Chuika 4.0 was widened to 4.5 GHz for Molniya video [src:militarnyi-2026-khomenko-chuika-4].
  - Molniyas are now switching to digital video, which the analogue detectors cannot see [src:euromaidan-2026-mukhina-molniya-digital].
  - Russia's "Shtora" spoofs video feeds [src:militarnyi-2026-khomenko-t200-shtora].
- **Ukraine moved to cable.** The National Guard now flies 70% of its drones on fibre, up from about 20% [src:euromaidan-2026-vivdych-ng-fibre-70].
- **Active protection returned to armour.** Russia's FPV-adapted Arena-M was first used in July 2026. It stopped several FPVs: 7 drones emptied it, and killing the tank took 15–20 FPVs. Ukrainian APS stop 60–80% of FPVs in tests [src:militarnyi-2026-pryhodko-aps-80].
- **Emitter hunting went deep.** Only 24 Zhitels have been visually confirmed destroyed or damaged in the whole war [src:militarnyi-2026-pryhodko-lasars-zhitel]. One National Guard unit killed two in 2026, the second 55 km behind the front [src:euromaidan-2026-mukhina-zhitel-55km].
- **Operation Vivaldi near Lyman** began with nine months of EW preparation to blind Russian drones. It then struck the Rubicon unit and Russian logistics 50 km and then 120 km deep, and then used UGVs [src:euobserver-2026-vasilko-vivaldi; src:mwi-2026-rose-vivaldi; src:kyivindependent-2026-farrell-vivaldi].

One Ukrainian tank crew stopped about three miles short of its ambush site, out of range of return fire, and shot at targets it could not see, with a drone pilot calling coordinates over the radio [src:nyt-2023-kramer-epic-tank-battle].

1. **The first wave (10–12 Oct).** Dawn fire preparation, then columns of 20–40 vehicles roll across flat fields at the salient's shoulders. A 53rd Brigade video shows one column losing two vehicles and 100 men in ten minutes [src:kyivpost-2023-korshak-worst-defeat-avdiivka]. An AFV is filmed falling into water [src:isw-2023-10-12-roca]. The scale: 70 vehicles in one day [src:wikipedia-battle-of-avdiivka].
2. **Storming the terrikon (~16 Oct).** Tanks line up at the foot of a 40 m wall of spoil while infantry try to climb it under machine guns and drone drops. One soldier gets three quarters of the way to the first terrace [src:euromaidan-2023-avdiivka-spoil-tip]. By late October the heap is Russian, but Ukrainian fire stops them massing on it [src:euromaidan-2023-havrylets-avdiivka].
3. **The coke plant under bombs.** The anchor, bombed to ruins but never taken. "The Russians were just banging their heads against the plant" (Samurai) [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-last-days-avdiivka]. A Presidential Brigade soldier: they "kept throwing themselves at the coke plant, leaving piles of their corpses there" [src:wikipedia-battle-of-avdiivka].
4. **The promka falls (Nov).** A fortified hill of factories held since 2014 is ground away building by building near Yasynuvata-2, while Russian armour moves "freely" in its northern part [src:kyivpost-2023-korshak-factory-district] [src:isw-2023-11-26-roca].
5. **The pipe (mid-Jan).** Men with oxygen cylinders and torches cut exits every 100 m under a mortar barrage, then emerge behind Tsarska Okhota [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-last-days-avdiivka] [src:kyivpost-2024-york-graveyard-armour]. Ukrainian counterattacks retake some ground [src:isw-2024-01-25-roca]. See c17 for the mechanic.
6. **The Bradley duels (Nov–Jan).** See vignette v02. A T-90M is blinded by 25 mm fire at Stepove, and one Bradley kills three MT-LBs in about 30 seconds [src:twz-2024-altman-bradley-t90m-experts] [src:forbes-2023-axe-bradley-three-mtlb].
7. **Cutting the neck (12–15 Feb).** Infiltration through the dachas in fog, the jump across the railway, then Industrialnyi Avenue and the "Brevno" restaurant at the O0542 junction [src:lwj-2024-hardie-avdiivka-analysis] [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-last-days-avdiivka].
8. **The 3rd Assault's counterattack.** The brigade pushes back to the railway but cannot hold under artillery. "F**k Avdiivka, we'd rather fight in Mariupol again" [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-last-days-avdiivka].
9. **Leaving Zenit (13–15 Feb).** The order comes at 21:00. Men walk 1–2.5 km by night through a 120 m gap, following the sound of a drone. Six wounded and a Russian POW stay in the bunker, and the evacuation vehicle never comes [src:kyivindependent-2024-terajima-avdiivka-wounded-on-foot] [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-last-days-avdiivka]. For the debrief: the later execution video [src:kyivpost-2024-zenit-pows-executed].
10. **The last night (16–17 Feb).** Syrskyi's announcement at about 01:00. The plant is emptied by 05:00, with maps and documents destroyed. The 9th quarter is held until dawn. A convoy is hit on the "road of death" [src:lwj-2024-hardie-avdiivka-analysis] [src:wikipedia-battle-of-avdiivka].
11. **Bombers falling (17–29 Feb).** Two Su-34s and a Su-35 on day one, then more Su-34s on 18, 19, 27 and 29 Feb, an A-50 on 23 Feb, and Cospas-Sarsat beacons in the Sea of Azov [src:kyivpost-2024-orlova-six-aircraft-72h] [src:pravda-2024-romanenko-su34-beacon] [src:pravda-2024-february-13-aircraft].

Ukraine first confirmed a "foothold" through Andriy Yermak on 13 November [src:isw-2023-11-14-roca]. The Marine Corps and the General Staff announced "several bridgeheads" on 17 November [src:isw-2023-11-17-roca]. The best depth reached was about 2.5 km from the river, in December [src:kyivindependent-2024-york-krynky-ongoing].

On 5–6 March 2025, as the US paused intelligence sharing (5 March), Russian forces broke through south of Sudzha. On 8 March about a hundred of them came out of a disused gas pipeline inside the town [src:pravda-2025-kyrylenko-breach-south-sudzha; src:isw-2025-03-09-roca; src:twz-2025-newdick-kursk-pipeline]. Ukraine withdrew from Sudzha on 10–12 March, and Russian troops raised flags in the town on 12 March. On 16 March the Ukrainian General Staff's maps confirmed the loss [src:isw-2025-03-12-roca; src:wikipedia-2024-kursk-offensive; src:kyivindependent-2025-sudzha-withdrawal-confirmed].
10 Oct 2023 – 17 Feb 2024 (aftermath to 1 Mar 2024), Avdiivka and its flanks, Pokrovsk raion, Donetsk Oblast, at the northern edge of occupied Donetsk.

**Where each act hit.**
- **Act 1.** "Midway between the main arch span … and Tuzla Island" [src:wikipedia-2022-crimean-bridge-explosion]. Naval News puts it "south of the main bridge span" [src:navalnews-2024-sutton-kerch-defenses]. Meduza's reading of the CCTV has the truck "beginning to ascend" toward the shipping arch [src:meduza-2022-what-we-know-bridge]. The case file names supports 235–236 [src:pravda-2024-kommersant-rocket-fuel].
- **Act 2.** Support 145 "from the Krasnodar Territory" (Aksyonov) [src:twz-2023-altman-kerch-closed]. A source close to Ukrainian intelligence told Meduza it lies on the Ukrainian side of the border [src:wikipedia-2023-crimean-bridge-explosion].
- **Act 3.** "Key supports" [src:liga-2025-malyuk-two-tons]; "the key and most complex" part of the bridge [src:kyivindependent-2025-fornusek-underwater]. No published pier number.

**The Russian shift to infantry.** After the armour was spent, Russian infantry advanced in waves and dug in behind burned-out vehicles. A 72nd soldier: "They'd come in groups of five. We'd kill four, one would stay and dig in" [src:kyivpost-2024-kostezh-why-lost].

**Ukraine.**
- **Strength (contested).** Formal units numbered 3,000–5,000, and the whole force up to 18,000, mostly Territorial Defence (TDF) and volunteers [src:mwi-2025-collins-spencer-battle-of-kyiv]. Wikipedia's infobox gives 20,000 soldiers and 18,000 irregulars [src:wikipedia-2026-northern-front].
- **The pre-war appreciation.** More than 10 brigades, about half the manoeuvre force, were in Donbas, and Kyiv held one manoeuvre brigade and two artillery brigades [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons].
- **Command.** Col. Gen. Oleksandr Syrskyi commanded the defence of Kyiv. The Kyiv Defence Council (Syrskyi, Mayor Klitschko, Lt. Gen. Pavliuk) formed on 24 Feb [src:mwi-2025-collins-spencer-battle-of-kyiv]. Syrskyi set up two defensive rings, suburbs and city, with sectors under generals from the military schools [src:wapo-2022-sonne-battle-for-kyiv]. From 15 Mar Pavliuk headed the Kyiv Regional Military Administration [src:isw-2022-03-16-roca].
- **72nd Mechanised Brigade** (Col. Oleksandr Vdovychenko, from Bila Tserkva about 85 km south) [src:bar-2024-sladden-collins-connable-irpin-river] [src:mwi-2025-collins-spencer-battle-of-kyiv].
  - The 1st and 3rd Battalions were on the east side, covering about 30 km [src:mwi-2025-collins-spencer-battle-of-kyiv].
  - The 2nd Battalion was on the Irpin, covering about 22 km, and some companies had only 22 men. Its 4th Company held Bucha–Irpin and the E373, its 5th Company Moshchun–Chervone (fewer than 30 men at first), and its 6th Company Huta-Mezhyhirska–Liutizh [src:mwi-2025-collins-spencer-battle-of-kyiv].
  - Its artillery group had 2S1, 2S3, BM-21 and MT-12 battalions [src:mwi-2025-collins-spencer-battle-of-kyiv].
- **National Guard, 4th Rapid Reaction Brigade** (Maj. Vitalii Rudenko) at Hostomel. The rear echelon left behind numbered about 200 (WOTR), fewer than 200 (BAR) or about 300 (WaPo). They had small arms, a few BTRs, Igla MANPADS, a ZU-23-2 and two D-30s in Horenka [src:wotr-2023-collins-kofman-spencer-hostomel] [src:bar-2024-sladden-collins-connable-irpin-river] [src:wapo-2022-sonne-battle-for-kyiv].
- **Other army units.**
  - The 80th and 95th Air Assault Brigades: the 24 Feb counterattack, Makariv, and reinforcement at Moshchun [src:wotr-2023-collins-kofman-spencer-hostomel] [src:pravda-2022-romanenko-makariv-liberated] [src:euromaidan-2023-havrylets-battle-of-kyiv-tactics].
  - The 14th Mechanised Brigade at Makariv [src:pravda-2022-romanenko-makariv-liberated].
  - The 70th Support Brigade on bridge demolition [src:wikipedia-2026-battle-of-irpin].
  - Training-centre artillery, including 2S7 Pions, moved out of its bases [src:wapo-2022-sonne-battle-for-kyiv].
- **Special forces and intelligence.**
  - The SSO's 3rd Special Purpose Regiment [src:wotr-2023-collins-kofman-spencer-hostomel]. Pavliuk credits a 30-man SSO unit with disabling the convoy's lead three vehicles [src:ukrinform-2023-pavliuk-30-sof].
  - HUR teams, with the Georgian Legion mostly under HUR at the airport [src:wapo-2022-sonne-battle-for-kyiv] [src:wikipedia-2026-georgian-legion].
  - The police KORD unit at Huta-Mezhyhirska [src:mwi-2025-collins-spencer-battle-of-kyiv].
- **Aerorozvidka.** About 30 special-forces troops and drone operators on quad bikes, by Lt. Col. Yaroslav Honchar's account [src:guardian-2022-borger-aerorozvidka-convoy]. It had 50 R18 octocopter sets by 24 Feb [src:wikipedia-2026-aerorozvidka].
- **Territorial Defence and volunteers.**
  - The Kyiv city 112th TDF Brigade had nine battalions, full within three days and manning hundreds of roadblocks [src:wikipedia-2026-112th-territorial-defense-brigade].
  - Almost 100,000 had volunteered for the TDF by 6 Mar [src:wikipedia-2026-territorial-defence-forces].
  - 25,000 rifles and 10m rounds were handed out in Kyiv [src:mwi-2025-collins-spencer-battle-of-kyiv].
  - The International Legion was created on 27 Feb. Kuleba claimed 20,000+ volunteers, against 1,500–2,000 actual foreign fighters per 2023 investigations [src:wikipedia-2026-international-legion].
- **Air.**
  - The 40th Tactical Aviation Brigade's MiG-29s flew from Vasylkiv, dispersed before the first strike; Ukraine had about 50 MiG-29s and 32 Su-27s in all [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons] [src:forbes-2022-axe-mig-pilots-kyiv-day-one].
  - Su-24 and Su-25 flew strikes [src:rusi-2022-bronk-russian-air-war].
  - "Fewer than a dozen" TB2s were operational [src:mwi-2025-collins-spencer-battle-of-kyiv].
- **Chernihiv (context).** The 1st Tank Brigade (Col. Leonid Khoda, about 2,000), the 58th Motorised Brigade and the 27th National Guard Regiment, about 6,000 in all [src:wapo-2022-sonne-battle-for-kyiv] [src:wikipedia-2026-siege-of-chernihiv].
- **Artillery balance.** Russia had 2,433 barrel systems against Ukraine's 1,176. Ukraine kept artillery parity for about the first 1.5 months, and "blunted Russia's attempt to seize Kyiv using massed fires from two artillery brigades" [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons]. For a few days the Kyiv forces risked running out of 152 mm ammunition [src:wapo-2022-sonne-battle-for-kyiv].

# 02 — Electronic warfare and the measure → countermeasure cycle

**The outcome the player must reproduce:**
- **The plant holds until the ordered "evacuation" of 16–20 May 2022.** Sources count the defence as 82 days [src:wikipedia-azovstal-iron-steel-works] or 83 days [src:time-2024-spencer-collins-mariupol-helicopters]. There is no relief and no breakout. Ukraine's own position was that a military unblocking was impossible [src:militarnyi-2022-kushnikov-unblocking-mariupol].
- **Russian forces stay tied down.** The General Staff claimed "up to 17 BTGs (about 20,000 personnel)" were pinned, which thwarted a quick drive on Zaporizhzhia [src:defenceua-2022-mariupol-garrison-mission]. US officials said a dozen BTGs were still at Mariupol on 21 April and two on 9 May [src:isw-2022-04-21-roca] [src:isw-2022-05-09-roca]. Win band: hold the plant until mid-May while keeping 2 to about 12 BTGs there after the city falls.
- **The city falls in stages.** The Illich works fall on 13 Apr and the port about 16 Apr; Russia announces victory on 21 Apr [src:isw-2022-04-13-roca] [src:isw-2022-04-17-roca] [src:isw-2022-04-21-roca].
- **Civilians.** About 101 civilians leave Azovstal in the first UN/ICRC operation (29 Apr – 3 May) and 173 in the second (arriving 8 May). The plant is clear of civilians on 7 May [src:un-ukraine-2022-05-03-lubrani-azovstal] [src:pravda-2022-karlovskyi-173-civilians] [src:isw-2022-05-07-roca].
- **The air bridge.** Seven missions, 16 Mi-8s, 72 troops in, 64 wounded out, about 30 t delivered, and 3 helicopters lost [src:time-2024-spencer-collins-mariupol-helicopters] [src:twz-2022-altman-mariupol-helicopter-missions].
- **Prisoners: contested.** Russia claims 2,439 [src:pravda-2022-mazurenko-2439-shoigu]. Ukrainian officials later used "about 2,500" [src:kyivpost-2025-pehlman-azovstal-half-home]. The ICRC had registered only "hundreds" by 20 May [src:isw-2022-05-20-roca].

- **Start date.** Mid-April (Axe), May (MWI), late spring (KI York), and August counterattacks (Rybar). Kudriashov counts the stabilisation as the first phase [src:euromaidanpress-2026-axe-btr60-vbied] [src:mwi-2026-rose-vivaldi] [src:kyivindependent-2026-york-vivaldi-gains] [src:twz-2026-altman-vivaldi].
- **The July narrative.** Axe has Nove taken in July [src:euromaidanpress-2026-axe-lyman-salient-trap]. Thorkill has July and early August attacks repelled by the 144th MRD until 17–18 Aug [src:euromaidanpress-2026-axe-lyman-salient-240].
- **Season 2 area.** 40 km² (Biletskyi as quoted by KI) or 50 km² (ISW). The 125 km² total implies 40 [src:kyivindependent-2026-york-vivaldi-gains] [src:isw-2026-09-20-roca].
- **Losses do not add up.** About 1,500 (season 1) plus 800 (season 2) is not "more than 3,000" [src:hromadske-2026-lisova-vivaldi-phase1] [src:euromaidanpress-2026-murdoch-vivaldi-phase2]. Is the 2,000 of season 3 cumulative? Ukrainian losses are unpublished.

- **DeepState lag.**
  - *No change before 14 Sep:* by our computation DeepState showed no change at all in the Vivaldi box from 1 Feb to 13 Sep [src:deepstate-api-history].
  - *Conflict with the KB:* this conflicts with the KB claim that May–June gains appeared in DeepState's August versions. They may lie outside our box, or the claim may refer to AMK's "OPSEC release" [src:amk-mapping-control-map].
  - *Still behind:* on 30 Sep DeepState still showed Kolodiazi and Zelena Dolyna as Russian, against ISW's 15 Sep reading and Thorkill's satellite confirmation [src:isw-2026-09-15-roca] [src:euromaidanpress-2026-axe-lyman-salient-240].
- **Russian order of battle.** Which divisions were inside the salient: the 2nd and 144th (Axe), the "2nd and 14th" (MWI), or the 3rd and 144th (ISW)? Russian strength is unknown [src:euromaidanpress-2026-axe-lyman-salient-trap] [src:mwi-2026-rose-vivaldi] [src:isw-2026-05-23-roca].

**Key locations.** Coordinates are OpenStreetMap data from the Photon geocoder [src:osm-2026-bakhmut-geodata]. Elevations are SRTM 30 m [src:opentopodata-srtm30m]. Distances and bearings are great-circle from the Bakhmut town node.

**What Ukraine had.**
- **Funding.** A European-financed pipeline: the **EUR 90 bn EU Ukraine Support Loan (2026–27)** and about EUR 11 bn allocated in May–Jun 2026 [src:kiel-2026-nishikawa-h1-2026]. PURL reached USD 6.3 bn announced and USD 4.8 bn received by June 2026 [src:crs-2026-if12040-us-security-assistance].
- **Continued dependence on US systems.** **30% of European military aid is bought from US firms**, over 90% of PURL comes from US stocks, and Patriot remains critical [src:kiel-2026-nishikawa-h1-2026].
- **A Patriot shortage.**
  - Russia now fires about three times as many ballistic missiles a month as a year earlier, against a Patriot supply squeezed by the Iran war [src:euromaidanpress-2026-mukhina-khmara].
  - Ukraine is contracting about 1,000 Patriot missiles, but most arrive in later years. At Ramstein on 8 Sep it asked allies to release stocks now, and only Germany did [src:euromaidanpress-2026-zoria-patriot-1000].

  - Trump raised Patriot missile coproduction in July 2026 and then hedged [src:crs-2026-if12040-us-security-assistance].
- **Future fighters.** Sweden pledged 16 Gripen C/D and 20 Gripen E/F in May 2026, the E/F bought with the EU loan [src:oryx-heavy-weaponry-supplied-ukraine]. Kyiv wants Meteor missiles with them to push KAB carriers back [src:euromaidanpress-2026-mukhina-khmara].

section: 3. Per-era notes / e9-counteroffensive-26 (late Jan 2026 – present, Sep 2026)

markdown:
1. **Battlefield transparency grew, and the "kill zone" got deeper.**
   - **2022:** Surveillance came mainly from Orlan-10 drones, Bayraktar TB2s, commercial and allied satellites, and intercepted radio traffic. Artillery did the killing. Russian units with their own drones could put fire on a target 3–5 minutes after spotting it [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons].
   - **Early 2025:** RUSI described a dense drone network. The battlefield was fully visible within 3 km of the line of contact, coverage thinned out to about 15 km, and commanders could task reconnaissance out to about 40 km [src:rusi-2025-watling-tactical-developments].
   - **Mid-2026:** Ukrainian commanders put the zone of regular drone strikes at **20–25+ km on both sides**. One corps commander expects 30 km by the end of 2026 [src:pravda-2026-levytska-magyar-kill-zone] [src:euromaidanpress-2026-vivdych-kill-zone-corps].
2. **Mass became a liability.**
   - Assault groups shrank: from BTG columns (2022), to Ukrainian assault detachments of 20 or fewer, to Russian infiltration teams of 1–5 people (2025–26) [src:rusi-2025-watling-tactical-developments] [src:kyivindependent-2025-farrell-kostiantynivka] [src:rusi-2025-watling-combined-arms].
   - Vehicles hide in dug-in shelters and dart out to fire. Troops walk the last 10–15+ km [src:rbcukraine-2026-perch-kill-zone-foot].
3. **Ukrainian C2 went digital and cloud-based, with Starlink as the backbone.**
   - The tools are Kropyva, GIS Arta, Delta and its modules (Vezha, Avengers AI, Mission Control, Delta Tube), plus the ePoints bonus scheme. All of them ride on Starlink and cellular links [src:csis-2024-bondar-delta-cjadc2] [src:newamerica-2023-zikusoka-gis-arta].
   - Russia built a similar system: Strelets, drone "reconnaissance-fire circuits", and smuggled Starlink terminals. Russian C2 has been reported as more centralised and more fragile [src:rusi-2023-watling-meatgrinder].
   - That fragility was exposed in **February 2026**. A speed cap (late January), then SpaceX's whitelist (enforced 5 February), cut off unregistered Starlink terminals. Russian front-line C2 broke down, and Ukraine made its fastest gains since 2023 [src:mod-2026-starlink-whitelist-operational] [src:osw-2026-wilk-starlink-cutoff] [src:atlanticcouncil-2026-spencer-russian-comms-crisis].
   - Russia recovered partially over the summer through mesh radios, other satellites, relays and laundered whitelist registrations. The edge narrowed but did not close [src:isw-2026-03-18-roca] [src:euromaidanpress-2026-axe-quiet-counteroffensive].
4. **Logistics became the main target.**
   - 2022: HIMARS against depots [src:kyivindependent-2022-ponomarenko-himars].
   - 2024: long-range drones against arsenals such as Toropets and Tikhoretsk [src:twz-2024-altman-ammo-depots].
   - 2025: Russian drone units such as Rubikon hunting Ukrainian supply roads [src:kyivindependent-2025-farrell-kostiantynivka].
   - 2026: a Ukrainian "middle strike" / "Logistics Lockdown" campaign at 20–200 km depth. It cut M-14 freight by about 71% and caused fuel rationing in Crimea [src:kyivindependent-2026-rushton-middle-strike] [src:euromaidanpress-2026-crimea-island].
   - Both sides now net their roads, move at night, and hand the last mile to ground robots (UGVs, Ukrainian *NRK*). Ukraine logged **25,143 UGV missions in August 2026 alone** [src:united24-2026-kabachynskyi-ugv-25000].

**Roads and rail.** Road refs and extents are from OSM [src:osm-copyright].
- **T-0509** (OSM: Т-05-09) runs east–west just south of the town. It links Velyka Novosilka and Novotroitske and is the road Vuhledar overlooks [src:isw-2023-01-26-roca] [src:rferl-2023-eckel-what-happened-vuhledar].
- **T-0524** (OSM: Т-05-24) enters the town from the northeast. On 4 Feb Russian armour tried to reach it from Mykilske [src:isw-2023-02-04-roca].
- **O-0532** runs west towards Vodiane and Kostiantynivka [src:kyivindependent-2024-denisova-withdraw-vuhledar].
- **The Pavlivka–Mykilske road**, along the river, was the Russian lateral. Russia claimed it on 17 Nov 2022 [src:isw-2022-11-17-roca].
- **The approach routes were dirt roads across the fields.** Ukrainian crews "studied the roads they used" [src:nyt-2023-kramer-epic-tank-battle]. Girkin: Russian columns had to advance "along narrow roads" [src:politico-2023-melkozerova-155th-brigade].
- **The railway.** The Donetsk–Volnovakha railway passed near the town [src:kyivpost-2024-kostezh-why-lost]. Holding Vuhledar let Ukraine threaten it [src:cnn-2023-lister-vuhledar-turkeys].
- **Wider geometry.** Vuhledar is about 24 km from Marinka, Kurakhove and the N15, so even its capture would not have linked up with the Donetsk City axis [src:isw-2023-03-05-roca].

## 6. Game/sim relevance
## 9. Russia's side as reported

- **Model the kill zone as a depth band with per-hex detection and strike probability.** Transparency is near total within about 3 km and falls off to about 15 km (2025) [src:rusi-2025-watling-tactical-developments]; by 2026 it extends to 15–30 km [src:euromaidan-2026-mukhina-anti-drone-nets]. Infantry, vehicles, rotations and casevac all pay a "movement in the open" tax there. Nets, fog, rain and night should lower it, and **Russian assaults also favour bad weather** [src:rusi-2025-watling-tactical-developments].
- **Defend with 2–3 soldier positions, not lines.** Each position gets a supply state (drone drops, UGV runs), an exhaustion clock (rotation every month or more; at most 2 months after April 2026) and a morale and AWOL risk [src:euromaidan-2026-mukhina-502-days] [src:kyivindependent-2026-terajima-awol]. Rotation should be a risky, deliberate operation that the enemy can exploit.
- **Give Russian AI assault behaviour by era.** BTG columns (e1); artillery plus conscript cycle (e2); disposable teams of 2–5 (e4); mechanized battalion waves (e6/e7); motorcycle rushes; then 2–4-man infiltration that accumulates behind the line (e8/e9). Russian units should rotate out at about 30% losses [src:rusi-2025-watling-tactical-developments].
- **Wounded as a resource-time problem.** A wounded soldier on a position stays there for hours to weeks. Tourniquet timing drives amputation (a "limb loss" state). Robotic casevac succeeds or fails on terrain and FPV density [src:euromaidan-2025-kirichenko-golden-hour] [src:euromaidan-2026-kossov-evacuation]. Unrecovered dead should hurt morale and compensation [src:rusi-2025-watling-tactical-developments].
- **2026 player verbs: "interdict the reinforcement" and "exploit a C2 blackout".** The Vivaldi pattern (strike launch sites, depots and ATV or motorcycle reinforcement; isolate infiltrators; then clear them) should beat whack-a-mole hunting [src:mwi-2026-rose-vivaldi] [src:isw-2026-09-26-assessment]. A Starlink-style event could degrade Russian drone and C2 effectiveness for a window [src:euromaidan-2026-zoria-air-assault-south].
- **Mines as a persistent, remotely placed layer.** Both sides lay mines at range: Russian rocket fields 5–15 km out [src:euromaidan-2026-mukhina-zemledeliye], and Ukrainian UGV crews up to 200 m of route a day [src:euromaidan-2026-vivdych-robot-demining]. Mines should block routes, raise evacuation losses (drone-dropped AT mines on evac vehicles) [src:euromaidan-2026-mukhina-chornovol-evacuation], and leave a post-battle contamination footprint.
- **Casevac as a costed mission.** A robotic evacuation may need several UGVs and a four-role team, and it draws FPVs [src:euromaidan-2026-murdoch-robotic-medevac]. Most wounds are fragment wounds and the main killer is bleeding [src:euromaidan-2025-mukhina-trauma], so tourniquet time is the key state variable.
- **Manpower flows as a strategic layer.** Ukraine takes in about 30,000 mobilized a month [src:euromaidan-2026-helme-draft-crisis], and voluntary contract uptake is small [src:euromaidan-2026-katola-18-24] [src:euromaidan-2026-helme-syrskyi-silence]. Unrotated units break, as the territorial brigades did at Huliaipole [src:euromaidan-2025-axe-huliaipole-fell]. On the Russian side, recruitment of about 33,000 a month (January–July 2026) barely covers losses [src:euromaidan-2026-thomas-mobilization-600k], while the losses per km² gained rose from 53 to 290 [src:euromaidan-2026-tril-cost-per-km].
- **Offensives need breaching capacity and assault-qualified platoons.** Only about 2 per battalion [src:rusi-2023-watling-stormbreak]. Mine depth (120 m versus 500 m) and demining vehicle count should gate breakthroughs, and breaches should exploit poorly unless fires dominate [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].

Russia then moved the next A-50 orbit east, over land near Krasnodar [src:pravda-2024-ukdi-a50-redeploy]. On 23 February 2024 a second A-50U was nonetheless brought down over Krasnodar Krai, about 200 km or more from the front. Ukraine attributed the kill to a refurbished Soviet S-200 under a joint Air Force–HUR (military intelligence) operation [src:pravda-2024-kravets-a50-s200] [src:twz-2024-newdick-second-a50]. Both kills came in Ukraine's best month for air defence since October 2022: 10 Su-34s, 2 Su-35s and the A-50 claimed in February [src:pravda-2024-february-13-aircraft]. For more than a week afterwards no A-50 was seen near Ukraine, and glide-bomb carriers "no longer dare[d] to fly too close" [src:pravda-2024-romanenko-no-a50]. Russian milbloggers blamed friendly fire both times [src:isw-2024-01-15-assessment] [src:isw-2024-02-23-assessment].

  - 4 × Kh-59/69 from Voronezh Oblast.
- **Drones, 496** [src:pravda-2026-romanenko-570-targets]:
  - Shahed-type (Geran) piston and jet drones, Gerbera, Italmas, Banderol loitering munitions and Parodiya decoys;
  - launched from Bryansk, Kursk, Oryol, Millerovo, Primorsko-Akhtarsk, occupied Donetsk and Hvardiiske.
  - **The jet share is not published.** The Air Force and Ihnat called it "a large number", higher than in earlier packages [src:uaf-2026-kpszsu-alerts-1-2-july][src:isw-2026-07-02-roca]. Informational Resistance calls it "one of the largest ever" deployments of jet Shahed-238/Karrar types [src:euromaidan-2026-mukhina-june-strikes-slowed].
- **Platform data.**
  - Jet Gerans (Geran-3/4/5) fly at 300–600 km/h [src:united24-2026-place-jet-gerans]. Ihnat gives up to 500 km/h [src:pravda-2026-ihnat-jet-drones].
  - The Geran-5 has a range of about 1,000 km and a 90 kg warhead [src:militarnyi-2026-pryhodko-geran-5].
  - Gerbera: 2.5 m wingspan, 18 kg take-off weight, 160 km/h, 600 km range; used as a decoy, a scout or an attack drone [src:pravda-2026-konyk-gerbera-fuel-tanks].
  - Decoys made up 35–40% of Geran waves in 2026 [src:frontliner-2026-zvirynskyi-strike-intensity].
- **Industrial context.**
  - HUR estimates about 3,000 Geran-4/5s a month (Aug 2026) [src:euromaidan-2026-thomas-hur-geran-production].
  - HUR (Jun 2025): 60–70 Iskander-Ms and 60–70 Kh-101s a month, and 20–30 Onyx/Zircons [src:kyivindependent-2025-post-ballistic-production].
  - Bomber wear limited Kh-101 launches to 34 of a possible 92 in June [src:euromaidan-2026-mukhina-june-strikes-slowed].
  - After a quiet June, Russia probably stockpiled for this strike [src:isw-2026-07-02-roca].

- Lancet-3(M) use rose from about October 2022. By early March 2023, Oryx had logged 113 visually confirmed Kub/Lancet hits and 41 misses, mostly on artillery, radars and SAM launchers [src:oryx-2022-lancet-kill-list].
- **Shahed campaign begins.** The first Shahed-136/131 appears in Air Force reports on 28 Sep 2022. At least 409 were launched from September to December, with a peak of 253 in October and a biggest night of 35 (19 Dec); about 95% were reported shot down [src:kaggle-2026-ivaniuk-missile-attacks]. Early reports often gave only the number destroyed, so these are floors.
- **Shark.** Ukrspecsystems' Shark ISR drone was unveiled in October 2022 to spot for HIMARS under heavy EW. It has a 60 km link, flies for 2+ hours at a cruising speed of 70–90 km/h and weighs 10 kg [src:euromaidan-2022-shark-himars]. Its 2026 successor, the Shark-M, flies for up to 7 hours on a 180 km link [src:militarnyi-2026-shark-m].

**What Russia had.**
- About **580,000 troops** in the operational group: about 70,000 in Kursk with about 10,000 North Koreans, 80,000 on the Kharkiv axis, 230,000 in Donetsk/Luhansk and about 140,000 in the south [src:rusi-2025-watling-third-year].

- DPRK troops from Nov 2024 (about 11–12k at first). They fought in company or battalion-sized assaults, and Ukrainian troops described them as fit and cohesive [src:wikipedia-2024-kursk-offensive] [src:rusi-2025-watling-third-year].
- Shahed/Geran launches rose from about **75 to about 900 a week from Sep 2024** [src:csis-2026-jones-10-charts].
- **Fibre-optic FPVs** appear, which are immune to RF jamming [src:rusi-2025-watling-third-year].

1. **Holding the marines back after the dam (Jun 2023).** Officers say the landing was planned for summer 2023 and postponed after the dam was destroyed. The Marine Corps went to Velyka Novosilka instead. Allies asked why the marines did not exploit the washed-out first line. UP reads the move as a way to "break in" the new brigades on land [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-krynky-untold].
2. **The objective and the plan (Sep–Oct 2023).**
   - The maximum objective was Perekop, about 80 km away. The minimum was the left-bank line and the M-14 (sources in the 36th Brigade and the Rada defence committee) [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-krynky-untold] [src:wikipedia-battle-of-krynky].
   - The plan gave three brigades on foot 3–4 days for a 30 km strip, with no second echelon.
   - A brigade commander says he "wouldn't have undertaken this operation" and that it "came from political leadership" [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-krynky-untold].
   - Ukrainian higher command never passed the marines' spring 2023 equipment list on to partners [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-krynky-untold].
3. **Concentrating on Krynky (late Oct – early Nov 2023).** Unable to hold three footholds, Katran gave up the rail-bridge and solar-farm footholds and reinforced Krynky [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-krynky-untold].
4. **Going public (13–17 Nov 2023).** Yermak announced the foothold in Washington. The Marine Corps and General Staff then declared bridgeheads, while Humeniuk urged "informational silence" [src:euromaidan-2023-zoria-marines-bridgeheads].
   - Soldiers and analysts saw a political motive. Kofman said the operation "appears to have political objectives" [src:kyivindependent-2023-terajima-dnipro-hopeless].
   - Kastehelmi said it became "more politically motivated" by winter [src:nyt-2024-meheut-krynky-lost].
   - The General Staff's stated aim was to push Russian guns out of range of the west bank [src:isw-2023-11-17-roca].
5. **Russian command changes and reinforcement (Oct–Dec 2023).** Teplinsky reportedly replaced Makarevich, and the 104th VDV Division was committed [src:isw-2023-10-29-roca] [src:kyivindependent-2023-fornusek-104th-vdv-krynky]. Russia chose massed fires and attrition rather than early mechanised counterattacks [src:kyivpost-2023-korshak-glide-bombs-krynky].
6. **No bridging.** Commanders never tried to bridge the Dnipro. Analysts say Russian bombers would have destroyed any attempt [src:kyivpost-2024-korshak-krynky-retreat].
7. **When to leave (winter 2024 – Jul 2024).** The withdrawal was gradual: the 36th went first, in winter, and the 35th last, in July [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-krynky-untold].
   - Most UP sources think the operation ran "at least several months longer than it should have". One officer: "We had to withdraw in spring at the latest, during the foggy season" [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-krynky-untold].
   - Kastehelmi: "a fair question to ask if the operation should have been ended faster" [src:nyt-2024-meheut-krynky-lost].
   - A 35th Brigade company commander defends holding the bridgehead as preventing Russian landings on the right bank [src:slidstvo-2024-stanko-krynky-hell].
8. **Accounting after the withdrawal (Jul 2024).** The General Staff did not confirm the withdrawal officially [src:euromaidan-2024-tril-krynky-withdraw]. It later called its loss data a "state secret" [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-krynky-untold].
   - MP Solomiia Bobrovska said she would put Krynky before the Security, Defence and Intelligence Committee, saying that personnel had gone "without being given a proper task" and "without the appropriate support" [src:unn-2024-bobrovska-krynky-committee].
   - Families say their brigades stonewalled them [src:rferl-2024-krynky-missing-marines] [src:slidstvo-2024-stanko-krynky-hell].
   - One interviewee took part in interrogations in a criminal case against his commander for disobeying an order [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-krynky-untold].
(Reported by Ukrainian and Western sources, not Russian state media.)

1. **Channel 16, all day (24 Feb).** A horizon that slowly fills with ships. Surrender calls come every 20 minutes, then shells, then three hours of air strikes. Hotskyi splits his men across shelters so one bomb can't kill them all, and one old border guard runs back to stay with him. Around 18:00 comes the reply. On the mainland, a phone records it off a radio relay, with someone whispering "what, 'go f— yourself' too?" [src:pravda-2022-romaniuk-zmiinyi-battle] [src:pravda-2022-romanenko-zmiinyi-audio].
2. **The *Sapfir* trap (26 Feb).** Chaplains, a doctor and the crew sail with body bags to recover "the 13 dead". Russian marines board, make everyone kneel, and show them a video: everyone on the island is alive and captured. "Oh, so you're spies!" [src:pravda-2022-romaniuk-zmiinyi-battle].
3. **The blip under the clouds (13 Apr).** A basic radar shows a huge contact about 120 km out that it shouldn't be able to see. After "several minutes of pondering and consultations" two Neptunes leave the rails. Then about six minutes of not knowing. Later the cruiser turns at full speed for the Boiko towers, and four ships converge on it [src:pravda-2022-romaniuk-moskva-neptune] [src:pravda-2023-pohorilov-neptune-launch-video].
4. **Fire, tow and the night roll (13–14 Apr).** A tug hoses the listing cruiser; the life rafts are gone. An SOS at 01:05, a roll at 01:14, under by about 03:00. By the next day's calm sea there is only the "heavy black silhouette" of a ship going down [src:guardian-2022-roth-moskva-photos] [src:wikipedia-sinking-of-the-moskva] [src:pravda-2022-romaniuk-moskva-neptune].
5. **Dawn hunt (2 May).** A TB2 strikes two Raptors 13 minutes apart as they zigzag [src:janes-2022-raptor-uav-strike].
6. **The landing ramp (7 May).** A Serna lowers its ramp with a Tor's radar still turning, and the TB2 bomb arrives. The same day two Su-27s skim in from the south past the lighthouse and toss-bomb the buildings [src:navalnews-2022-sutton-tb2-ghost-snake-island] [src:twz-2022-payne-su27-snake-island].
7. **The night assault and the Mi-14 (7–9 May).** Eight helicopters and armoured boats run in. A Tor lashed to a boat deck opens up and the assault pulls back. Over the coast, the standby rescue helicopter flown by Col. Bedzai is shot down [src:pravda-2022-romaniuk-zmiinyi-battle] [src:ppu-2024-bedzai].
8. **Two Harpoons (17 Jun).** TB2 video shows the second missile arriving seconds after the first fireball on the *Vasily Bekh* [src:navalnews-2022-ozberk-vasily-bekh].
9. **Forty-six rounds from the dunes (30 Jun).** The Bohdana fires shell after shell, 90 seconds each to the island, waiting for the barrel to cool. Four rounds are held back for the pickup boats [src:militarnyi-2023-bohdana-snake-island].
10. **Two speedboats, then the flag (30 Jun – 7 Jul).** The island burns and the last Russians leave by speedboat. A day later come Russia's phosphorus runs. Then a motorboat at dawn on 7 Jul and a flag that reads "Russian warship, remember forever – Snake Island is Ukraine!!!" [src:ukrinform-2022-invaders-escape-snake-island] [src:aljazeera-2022-phosphorus-snake-island] [src:twz-2022-altman-flag-snake-island].

**What Russia had.**
- **Jet Gerans:** about 180 launched in 2025 but about **1,400 by early Jun 2026**. 15–20% of launches in Apr 2026 had jet engines, and the Geran-4 cruises at 350–500 km/h [src:militarnyi-2026-jet-geran-interceptors]. The Geran-3 was retired by Aug 2026 in favour of the Geran-4/5 [src:csis-2026-bondar-shahed-geran].
- **Slowing gains.** Russian gains slowed to **33 km²/week** by mid-Feb 2026 [src:ukrinform-2026-liskovych-front-spring].
- **Losses.** The General Staff counts about 32,800 Russian losses a month in Feb–Jun 2026, and about 290 per km² gained [src:euromaidan-2026-tril-cost-per-km].
- **Manpower.**
  - Year-round conscription from 2026 [src:wikipedia-2022-russian-mobilization].
  - A 409,000 recruitment plan (HUR) [src:euromaidan-2025-murdoch-budanov-403k].
  - Zelensky warns of a 300–500k mobilisation after the September Duma elections, which the Kremlin denies [src:euromaidan-2026-tril-cost-per-km].
- More DPRK missiles, including a reported new Hwasong-11C batch in Aug 2026 [src:wikipedia-north-korean-involvement].

markdown: ## 12. Sources
## 4. Forces

**Wagner's assault method.** The account comes from a Ukrainian intelligence report published by CNN; it is single-source and its intercepts are unauthenticated [src:cnn-2023-lister-wagner-tactics-report]:
- **The groups.** Assault groups are "about a dozen or fewer", with RPGs and Motorola radios, and drones as the "key element".
- **The waves.** Convicts make up the first wave and take up to 80% losses, by the Ukrainian claim. Veterans with thermal sights follow and consolidate in foxholes under artillery.
- **The rules.** "Unauthorized withdrawal … is punishable by execution on the spot." The wounded are left, and retreat is allowed "only at night".
- **Adoption.** The report says these were "the only" effective tactics for mobilised men, and that the army was copying them [src:cnn-2023-lister-wagner-tactics-report].

## 4. Forces

- **Win band.**
  - **Hard conditions at 30 Nov.** Robotyne is Ukrainian, Tokmak is Russian, and the salient's tip is at Novoprokopivka's northern edge and Verbove's western outskirts [src:kyivindependent-2023-khalilova-robotyne-liberated] [src:isw-2023-09-23-roca].
  - **Score the date Robotyne falls.** 22–28 Aug is historical, and earlier is a bonus [src:isw-2023-08-22-roca] [src:kyivindependent-2023-khalilova-robotyne-liberated].
  - **Score Western armour preserved against the 8 Jun benchmark.** The floor is DeepState's irrecoverable count (at least 4 APCs and 1 Leopard). The ceiling is Forbes's 25 vehicles [src:euromaidan-2023-shandra-leopards-mala-tokmachka] [src:censor-2023-forbes-25-vehicles].
  - **Russian attrition.** About 156 confirmed equipment losses on the axis is the historical yardstick [src:warspotting-api-russian-losses].
- **Self-running script.**
  - A mechanized breach on 7–9 Jun fails. Armour assaults stop about 11–12 Jun, followed by six weeks of 100 m-a-day infantry grinding [src:euromaidan-2023-wp-analysis] [src:isw-2023-07-20-roca].
  - The 10th Corps push on 26 Jul, and the 82nd and 46th committed about 15 Aug [src:isw-2023-07-26-roca] [src:warontherocks-2023-kofman-lee-three-months].
  - Robotyne falls on 22–28 Aug, Verbove is probed from 30 Aug and the Verbove belt broken on 20–23 Sep, then the front goes positional from October [src:isw-2023-08-30-roca] [src:isw-2023-09-23-roca] [src:isw-2023-11-06-roca].
  - Scripted Russian events: the Popov dismissal on 12 Jul, the 7th VDV from about 16 Aug, the 76th VDV from about 26 Aug, the 41st Army from 1 Sep, and re-mining from October [src:isw-2023-07-13-roca] [src:isw-2023-08-22-roca] [src:isw-2023-08-26-roca] [src:isw-2023-09-01-roca] [src:kyivindependent-2023-amran-remining].
- **Core mechanic: breaching order.** The player chooses:
  - lane count and depth against minefields 120–500 m deep with stacked mines [src:rusi-2023-watling-stormbreak]
  - whether to commit breaching tanks (scarce: 6 Leopard 2R, a few Wisents) [src:censor-2023-forbes-25-vehicles]
  - H-hour against a short June night, with sunrise at 04:40 and a late unit landing in daylight [src:open-meteo-historical-archive] [src:warontherocks-2023-kofman-lee-three-months]
  - smoke against its own drone picture [src:rusi-2023-watling-stormbreak]
  - **Failure modes:** stacking on one lane, and Ka-52s at 8–15 km [src:guardian-2023-beaumont-wintour-mala-tokmachka] [src:kyivindependent-2023-court-ka52m-lmur].
- **Core mechanic: dismounted against mounted.** After the switch the player trades speed (mechanized, high vehicle loss) against attrition (infantry at 700–1,200 m per five days, about two assault platoons per battalion). Bradleys are better used as armoured "taxis" than as assault vehicles [src:rusi-2023-watling-stormbreak] [src:kyivindependent-2023-farrell-47th-surovikin-line].
- **Ka-52 lob fire as a layer.** The helicopter threat should dominate the June map and decline after mid-August as MANPADS kills mount and ATACMS hit Berdiansk (17 Oct). The GPS-jamming lift is a tell for the player [src:rusi-2023-watling-stormbreak] [src:isw-2023-09-28-roca] [src:isw-2023-10-17-roca].
- **Counter-battery as the hidden win condition.** Russian artillery degradation, Popov's complaint, is what lets the infantry advance. Model it as a meter fed by GMLRS, FPVs and radar kills [src:isw-2023-07-13-roca] [src:kyivindependent-2023-farrell-counteroffensive-lurches].
- **Terrain.** The attack runs uphill from about 55 m to about 150 m, along a grid of shelterbelts 0.5–1.2 km apart. The T0408 is the spine, and the high ground south of Robotyne is the Russian last stand [src:opentopodata-srtm30m] [src:osm-overpass-2026-landscape-sample] [src:isw-2023-09-23-roca].
- **Pacing.** The window runs from heat (to 37 °C) through a dry September to November mud and storms. Milley's "30 to 45 days" from 11 Sep is the in-game clock warning [src:open-meteo-historical-archive] [src:kyivindependent-2023-court-4-8-km2].
### e7-kursk-pokrovsk (Aug 2024 – Mar 2025)
# 08 — Prior-art games and wargames

The war turned into a contest of **sensors → decision → strike** loops. Whichever side closes the loop faster, and denies the other its loop, holds ground at lower cost. Four long trends run through all nine eras.

- **EW was already the main counter-UAS tool.** Ukraine lost about 90% of the UAS it employed, and RUSI calls EW "the primary means of CUAS" [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons].
- **Russian EW hurt its own side too.** Russian EW "rarely deconflict[s]", which causes fratricide and forces effects to be used one after another [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons].
- **Big Russian systems came in with the columns.** A Krasukha-4 was filmed at Makariv (Kyiv oblast) in March 2022 [src:militarnyi-2023-kushnikov-krasukha-4-zaporizhzhia], and the first Zhitel kill came at the end of March [src:militarnyi-2022-kushnikov-zhitel-kharkiv].
- **Starlink arrived within days.** The first terminals landed on 28 February 2022, two days after Fedorov's request, and more than 5,000 were in country by 6 April [src:wikipedia-starlink-war]. For the game, this is Ukraine's first "EW-resistant comms" card.
- **Ukraine already had domestic EW.** Bukovel-AD has been in service since 2016 against Orlan-10 [src:wikipedia-bukovel].
## 8. Media

Probably 11 January 2024; the footage was published on 12 January 2024. Stepove, on the northern flank of Avdiivka, Donetsk Oblast. A tank-duel set piece inside chapter 11 (Avdiivka), with the wider record of Bradleys against Russian armour from November 2023 to February 2024.

- **The exact date and place.** The only date is a Telegram channel's "Thursday" [src:newsweek-2024-cole-bradley-t90], and there is no geolocation.
- **The identities.** The crew of the first Bradley, the full name of the second's crew, and the T-90M's unit are all unknown.
- **The ammunition problem** the gunner mentions is not explained, and whether DU rounds were used is speculation by an expert [src:twz-2024-altman-bradley-t90m-experts].
- **The Bradley record.**
  - *Losses:* Oryx counted at least 65 Bradleys lost by January 2024 [src:twz-2024-altman-bradley-t90m-experts], and by April 2024 the 47th had lost at least 40 of its roughly 200 [src:wikipedia-2026-47th-mechanized-brigade].
  - *Kills:* there is no systematic count of Bradley kills against Russian armour at Avdiivka. The incidents above are anecdotal and drawn from video.
- **The 21-tank day** rests on a single OSINT tally relayed by Forbes [src:forbes-2023-axe-21-tanks-stepove].

**Command.**
- The Tavriia (Tavriisk) operational direction, whose spokesman was Col. Oleksiy Dmytrashkivskyi [src:politico-2023-melkozerova-155th-brigade] [src:isw-2023-02-13-roca].
- The 72nd Separate Mechanised Brigade "Black Zaporozhians", commanded from summer 2022 by Col. Ivan Vinnyk [src:pravda-2024-vinnyk-transferred] [src:militarnyi-2023-vuhledar-vehicles].

- **The opening strike campaign fails to blind Ukraine.** About 75% of static Ukrainian SAM sites were engaged in the first 48 h. Mobile systems survived through dispersal and deception: dummy sites, printed "damage" sheets over hangars, and false radio reports of destroyed sites. Russian BDA (battle damage assessment) was weak [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons]. From early March the VKS lost the ability to operate over Ukrainian-held territory except at very low altitude [src:rusi-2022-bronk-russian-air-war].
- **Pre-war Ukrainian air defence** had 35 S-300PS/PT divisions, 3 S-300V, 9 S-125 and 15 Buk-M1, with MANPADS (mostly modernised Igla-1) spread through units. SAMs forced aircraft down low, into the MANPADS envelope [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons].
- **Missiles.** More than 200 Iskander strikes and about 180 Kh-22/32 and Kh-55/555 launches from February to early May 2022. By early April Russia had moved from salvos to single shots, probably because of stock shortages. Iskander-M output was estimated at about 6 a month. Russia fell back on Tochka-U, Bal and Bastion, with more civilian damage as a result [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons].
- **Helicopters.** Russian air-assault helicopters reached Hostomel low along the Dnipro, but MANPADS downed 2 in the first wave [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons]. Of the 34 helicopters in that assault Russia lost about 17%, and Oryx confirms 6 (4 Ka-52, 1 Mi-28, 1 Mi-8) [src:pravda-2026-dotsenko-helicopters-drones]. Ka-52 and Mi-28N crews began pitch-up lob firing of unguided S-8 rockets. This buys about 6–7 km of extra range and keeps the helicopter out of Stinger range, at the cost of very wide dispersion [src:twz-2022-newdick-helicopter-lob]. Ukrainian Mi-24 and Mi-8 crews adopted the same technique: they run in low, pitch up 15–30°, ripple S-8 or S-13 rockets at a pre-calculated area and break away firing flares. The salvo forces infantry to take cover but rarely kills armour or dug-in positions [src:pravda-2026-dotsenko-helicopters-drones].
- **Ukrainian aviation.** Su-24M, Su-25, Mi-24 and Mi-8 struck Russian convoys moving without air cover. MiG-29 pairs flew defensive counter-air, often outnumbered 6:2. Airspace was deconflicted from SAMs first by time, then by area [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons].
- **Sensor-to-shooter.** Russia relied on pre-planned strikes and presumed success. Ukraine's pre-war Kropyva digital fire-control software had cut the time to open counter-battery fire by 90% and the time to engage unplanned targets by two-thirds [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons].

- **Ukrainian offence (Kursk).** The 6 August 2024 break-in was led by the 80th and 82nd Air Assault brigades, with the deployment disguised as defensive. About 100 settlements and roughly 600 prisoners were taken [src:kyivindependent-2025-terajima-kursk-gambit]. Preparatory collection and shaping took up to a month, even though the initial breach was small, at two points [src:rusi-2025-watling-tactical-developments]. The salient depended on one road, which Russian fiber-optic FPVs cut. Ukraine withdrew in February–March 2025, with equipment losses of 790 Ukrainian against 740 Russian [src:kyivindependent-2025-terajima-kursk-gambit].
- **North Korean troops.** More than 11,000 combat troops were sent from October 2024 [src:koreatimes-2026-yonhap-nk-kursk].
  - They first attacked in company or battalion strength, took mass casualties, and sometimes overran sparse Ukrainian positions. After losing about a quarter of the force they adopted Russian small-group tactics [src:rusi-2025-watling-tactical-developments].
  - Ukrainian commanders describe teams of 5–8 and a 50-man group advancing 8 km on foot through mined ground. A captured diary gives the spacing for baiting drones: 7 m for the bait, 10–12 m for the shooters [src:kyivpost-2025-nk-tactics-kursk].
  - Later they fielded FPV teams, mobile ATGM crews and anti-drone drills [src:frontelligence-2025-nk-lessons]. Their later roles are in e8 and e9.
  - Casualty claims by claimant are in §4.
- **Russian assault style.**
  - The Russian group of forces numbered about 580,000 [src:rusi-2025-watling-tactical-developments].
  - Russia first probes by section: groups of about 8, or up to 30 with 1–2 IFVs, conduct reconnaissance by drawing fire and look for the boundaries between Ukrainian units. One Ukrainian brigade counted an average of 27 section attacks a day. Russian units rotate out after about 30% losses [src:rusi-2025-watling-tactical-developments].
  - Troops threatened with being "zeroed" (executed) for retreating tend to go to ground rather than fall back [src:rusi-2025-watling-tactical-developments].
  - Autumn 2024 brought battalion-sized mechanized pushes before the mud season (Kurakhove, Pokrovsk) [src:rusi-2025-watling-tactical-developments]. In early November Kurakhove was the busiest axis, with 690 clashes in two weeks (435 at Pokrovsk). ISW recorded two mechanized assaults into and south of the town on 13 November, after Russia struck the Kurakhove reservoir dam, possibly to flood the flanks [src:euromaidan-2024-tril-kurakhove]. Then came the switch to small groups on motorcycles, civilian cars and scooters. The General Staff claims over 45,000 Russian casualties in November 2024 [src:euromaidan-2024-bbc-small-groups]. Motorcycle and ATV groups of "a dozen to a hundred riders" had been formally adopted by mid-2024 [src:rusi-2025-mcgovern-motorcycles].
- **Ukrainian defence and density.**
  - An infantry section covers 70–200 m of front, in fire teams of 2–3 in positions about 50 m apart. A company is spread over about 3 km of depth and a battalion over about 7 km. One brigade held 27 km with four battalions [src:rusi-2025-watling-tactical-developments].
  - Local force ratios run 1:2 to 1:6 against Ukraine. Less than 25% of the roughly 800,000-strong Defence Forces is available as combat power [src:rusi-2025-watling-tactical-developments].
  - Armour hides and sallies out to fire directly, then returns to cover. About 50% of Ukrainian casualties are taken in the rear. Rotations are minimised, and troops stay on position for more than a month [src:rusi-2025-watling-tactical-developments].
## 4. Forces
### Russia

- Both sides used commercial and adapted quadcopters at tactical level and fixed-wing ISR at medium altitude: Ukraine's SKIF, Leleka and Furia, and Russia's Orlan-10. Ukraine flew TB2s and Russia flew Orion MALE drones (medium-altitude, long-endurance), committed only under favourable conditions [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons].
- Ukrainian battalions had been receiving Furia, Leleka and PD-1 UAVs since 2015. Linked to the Kropyva fire-control software, this sped up artillery engagements [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons]. The makers date formal adoption to 2019 (Leleka) and 2020 (Furia, after state trials) [src:deviro-2026-leleka][src:athlonavia-2026-furia].
- Attrition was extreme. About 90% of Ukrainian UAVs were destroyed. A quadcopter survived about 3 flights and a fixed-wing about 6, and only about 1/3 of missions succeeded [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons].
- FPV kamikaze drones barely existed yet: Ukraine had about 3,000–5,000 FPVs in 2022 [src:justsecurity-2026-bidochko-drone-superpower].

## 3. The diorama: geography, terrain, weather

The figures below are contested; the table shows the ranges, and this is who claims what:
- **FPV success rates.** RUSI's 60–80% failure rate comes from field interviews; makers' 2–4× gains come from marketing. No 2026 equivalent exists. The nearest 2026 data points are the fibre share (70% in the National Guard) and "drones per kill" against APS-protected tanks (15–20).
- **Excalibur.** The 55% → 6% drop is the Washington Post's reading of internal Ukrainian data. Some secondary summaries say "70% → 6%", and we could not find that in RUSI's text.
- **Starlink cut date.** 1 February (ISW, 26 Feb), 2 February (the cabinet resolution) and 5 February (terminals blocked; Ukrinform, and ISW as relayed by Euromaidan). The whitelist was phased, so these are all defensible.
- **Starlink-cut gains.** Reports range from 10–12 km (Wikipedia, southern front) to more than 200 km² (Atlantic Council). These use different units, depth of advance and area retaken, so they don't directly conflict. They still need a common measure, such as DeepStateMap's monthly km² statistics. Biletsky's 20–40% effectiveness drop is the only measured effect on Russian drone output.
- **Russian anti-Starlink effect.** A Russian industry source claims Volna has "shut down Starlink" wherever needed. A Ukrainian engineer measures 0–35% packet loss.
- **Lima claims.** The Kinzhal counts (41 of 42 in April, 61 by July) and "KABs to zero" all come from the developer and the Night Watch unit that fields Lima. Hambling flags them as unverified.
- **Interceptor shares.** Figures vary with scope: one night, the Kyiv region, or a month. Official "shot down/suppressed" totals lump kinetic and EW kills together [src:isis-2026-anokhin-shahed-monthly].
- **Rassvet numbers.** ISW counts 12 working satellites giving up to 90 minutes a day in total; Euromaidan's tracking-based count is two windows of more than an hour each. Both sources give a working altitude of about 550 km [src:euromaidan-2026-thomas-isw-rassvet; src:euromaidan-2026-vivdych-rassvet-windows].
## 5. Systems and tactics in use

**Ukraine: 47th Separate Mechanised Brigade "Magura".**
- *Fleet:* the brigade was the main Bradley user, receiving about 190–200 M2s [src:forbes-2023-axe-bradley-three-mtlb] [src:forbes-2024-axe-bradleys-t90]. It had lost about 30 by mid-December 2023 [src:forbes-2023-axe-bradley-three-mtlb] and at least 31 by January 2024 [src:forbes-2024-axe-bradleys-t90]. It also had about a dozen Leopard 2A6s left [src:forbes-2023-axe-21-tanks-stepove].
- *The crew:* the second Bradley was commanded and gunned by "Serhiy", a former infantryman, with driver "Oleksandr", who had driven for a supply unit. It was their second mission together [src:twz-2024-altman-bradley-gunner]. The first Bradley's crew is not identified.
- *Nearby units:* the 110th and 57th Brigades in the garrison [src:forbes-2023-axe-21-tanks-stepove]; the 109th Territorial Defence Brigade's infantry near Stepove [src:twz-2024-situation-report-2024-01-22].
- *Other Bradley users at Avdiivka:* the 3rd Assault and 67th Mechanised Brigades are also reported using Bradleys there [src:euromaidanpress-2024-frontline-avdiivka-2024-02-15] [src:euromaidanpress-2023-frontline-avdiivka-2023-12-05]. This contradicts Forbes's "sole user".

**Artillery and the ammunition war.**
- **Russian fire rates.**
  - Summer 2022: about 20,000 rounds a day, with peaks above 32,000. Ukraine fired fewer than 6,000 [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons].
  - Early 2023, falling, but the figures disagree by source. Budanov: from 60,000 to 19,000–20,000 a day [src:kyivindependent-2023-ponomarenko-artillery-gasps]. US officials: down "as much as 75%", to about 5,000 a day, while Ukraine averaged 4,000–7,000 [src:cnn-2023-bertrand-russian-artillery-down-75]. RUSI: 12,000–38,000 a day in Q1 2023 [src:rusi-2023-watling-meatgrinder]. RUSI gives 5:1 at Bakhmut itself [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].
- **Ukrainian rationing.**
  - A 24th Brigade battery went from 150 full loads a day to 30: "We need every single 122-millimeter round anywhere in the world" [src:kyivindependent-2023-ponomarenko-artillery-gasps].
  - Infantry in March: "If we keep getting 10 shells, Bakhmut will quickly be surrounded" [src:kyivindependent-2023-kossov-bakhmut-troops-not-protected].
  - Palisa: "painful to see how we pay with our lives for the lack of ammunition" [src:nyt-2023-kramer-final-blocks].
  - Reznikov put Ukrainian use at about 110,000 155 mm shells a month, a quarter of Russia's [src:kyivindependent-2023-cherevatyi-denies-russian-shortage].
  - The Pentagon warned Kyiv against wasting ammunition [src:nyt-2023-engelbrecht-bakhmut-success].
  - In June Zelensky said 50,000 shells were fired there every day; it is unclear by whom [src:ukrinform-2023-zelensky-best-weapons-bakhmut].
- **Western supply.**
  - US 155 mm output was about 15,000 a month, aiming for 70,000 [src:cnn-2023-britzky-ukraine-burning-ammo].
  - On 20 Mar 2023 the EU agreed €2 bn for one million 155 mm rounds within a year [src:reuters-2023-gray-eu-million-shells]. By 23 May it had delivered 220,000 [src:reuters-2023-gray-eu-220000-shells].
- **Russian "shell hunger" as politics.**
  - Prigozhin claimed 70% of needed ammunition was missing (4 May), then that he got "only 10%" (10 May) [src:cnn-2023-lendon-prigozhin-fat-cats] [src:reuters-2023-osborn-prigozhin-10pct-shells].
  - Ukraine called the shortage "fake", counting 524 Russian strikes a day [src:ukrinform-2023-cherevaty-ammo-shortage-fake].
  - Rob Lee suggested the MoD was rationing ahead of the Ukrainian counteroffensive [src:reuters-2023-light-prigozhin-lick-wounds].
## 1. Overview

- **Russia started using Starlink:** Ukrainian Defence Intelligence (HUR) confirmed Russian use in February 2024. The terminals were reportedly bought through third countries [src:wikipedia-starlink-russo-ukrainian-war].
- **RUSI fieldwork in 2024** described a mature "mass observation" battlefield [src:rusi-2025-watling-tactical-developments]:
  - Russian combat groups try to keep **five drone orbits** over each axis of advance.
  - Each orbit streams over a satellite uplink to battalion and brigade CPs, where the intelligence officer, fires officer and commander's representative authorise strikes.
  - Neither side generally uses fire controllers inside combat units.
- **Artillery shortage:** One Ukrainian brigade held 18 km of front with four working howitzers. Drones filled the gap and caused 60–70% of damaged or destroyed Russian systems. Even so, 60–80% of Ukrainian FPVs fail to reach their target [src:rusi-2025-watling-tactical-developments].
- **Decoy production grew** among volunteers and industry [src:euromaidanpress-2024-martyniuk-decoy-makers]:
  - Decoy Stugna anti-tank launchers cost $30–100.
  - Metinvest had made 250+ radar and howitzer decoys.
  - Good decoys copy radar, thermal and acoustic signatures and simulate firing or explosions.
  - The oft-repeated claim is that at least ten Kalibr missiles were spent on fake HIMARS.

- **Redeploying Khartiia (Jul–Aug 2025).**
  - *Who decided:* Khartiia proposed blocking the infiltration routes, taking the high ground and clearing the town. Syrskyi was "initially sceptical" but agreed [src:ukrpravda-2026-kyrylenko-kupiansk-is-yours].
  - *The rival account:* Drapatyi's team also asked for authority and set up the Kupiansk Tactical Group. Two accounts compete over who started the operation [src:ukrpravda-2026-kyrylenko-kupiansk-is-yours].
- **Reporting it as a "police operation".** Khartiia officers say the 10th Army Corps reported a counter-sabotage task so that it would not have to tell the president the town was lost. Others blame a lack of trained infantry. The 10th Corps did not respond [src:ukrpravda-2026-kyrylenko-kupiansk-is-yours].
- **Silence versus publicity.** Ukraine kept its gains off the news and mostly off DeepState, which let the Russian claim of capture stand until 12 December [src:ukrpravda-2026-kyrylenko-kupiansk-is-yours].
- **Destroy the pipe, or hunt its exits.**
  - *Attempts to destroy it:* engineers studied the pipe with former local employees, but every attempt failed during the active phase [src:ukrpravda-2026-kyrylenko-kupiansk-is-yours]. A demolition with about 3 t of explosives was claimed on 13 Dec [src:defenseexpress-2025-achilles-pipeline-destroyed].
  - *By Sept 2026:* the line was "damaged in sections, not destroyed", because Ukraine does not control the whole route [src:gwara-2026-diachenko-pipeline-damaged].
- **Dvorichna.** An early rush on Dvorichna was abandoned for lack of reinforcements to hold it, and the boat route stayed open [src:ukrpravda-2026-kyrylenko-kupiansk-is-yours].
- **Do not fire on the civilian column** (27 Sep 2026). Khartiia documented it for a war-crimes case instead [src:euromaidan-2026-zoria-kupiansk-pipeline].

## 7. Decision points

- **Breakthrough and exploitation, 6–12 Sep.**
  - Balakliia is retaken by 8 Sep (Ukrainian control was formally established on 10 Sep) [src:isw-2022-09-08-roca; src:wikipedia-2022-kharkiv-counteroffensive].
  - Western Kupiansk falls on 10 Sep and Izium on 10–11 Sep [src:isw-2022-09-10-roca; src:isw-2022-09-11-roca].
  - Velykyi Burluk falls on 10–11 Sep, and Ukrainian troops reach the state border at Vovchansk and Ternova on 11–12 Sep [src:isw-2022-09-11-roca; src:isw-2022-09-12-roca].
  - All of Kharkiv Oblast west of the Oskil is retaken by 13 Sep [src:wikipedia-2022-kharkiv-counteroffensive].
- **Oskil phase, 13 Sep – 4 Oct.**
  - Bridgeheads at Borova (13 Sep), east Kupiansk (16 Sep) and Kupiansk-Vuzlovyi (26 Sep) [src:mvs-2022-slobidska-sich-counteroffensive; src:isw-2022-09-16-roca; src:pravda-2022-roshchina-kupiansk-vuzlovyi].
  - Lyman is liberated on 1 Oct, and Borova town on 3 Oct [src:isw-2022-10-01-roca; src:isw-2022-10-03-roca].
  - The new Russian line runs Svatove–Kreminna, along the R66 [src:isw-2022-10-04-roca].
- **Area (contested; the win band is about 6,000–8,500 km² for the push to the Oskil):**

From spring 2025 the Russian 20th Combined Arms Army (CAA) pushed a salient into the ground north of Lyman, between the Nitrius and Zherebets rivers. Its aim was to bypass Lyman from the north, reach Sviatohirsk and the Siverskyi Donets, and form the northern pincer of an envelopment of the Donetsk fortress belt (Sloviansk, Kramatorsk, Druzhkivka, Kostiantynivka) [src:euromaidanpress-2026-axe-lyman-salient-240] [src:isw-2026-09-12-roca]. In DeepState's polygons the Russian-occupied area in a 1,096 km² box around the salient grew from 60 km² (1 Mar 2025) to 350 km² (15 Jan 2026) [src:deepstate-api-history]. Ukraine's 3rd Army Corps under Brig. Gen. Andrii Biletskyi first stabilised the line and stopped the infiltration [src:twz-2026-altman-vivaldi]. Then, under "maximum information silence", it attacked the salient's northern flank at Nove, with the first visible attack on 22 May 2026 [src:kyivindependent-2026-farrell-vivaldi] [src:euromaidanpress-2026-axe-lyman-salient-240]. Before and during the ground attacks it ran a drone and EW campaign: it blinded Russian drones, hit Rubikon's operators and launch sites, struck logistics 50 and then 120 km deep, and cut a diesel pipeline from Voronezh Oblast [src:isw-2026-09-15-roca] [src:euromaidanpress-2026-zoria-vivaldi-targeting]. Its first-phase method was to kill the ATV and motorcycle reinforcements sent to stranded Russian infiltration groups, not to chase every infiltrator [src:isw-2026-09-26-assessment].
