**Equipment and boats.**
- No heavy equipment, except what the 38th brought [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-krynky-untold]. A Russian source claims the marines had only 80 mm mortars [src:kyivpost-2023-korshak-glide-bombs-krynky]. Light mortars did cross later [src:kyivpost-2023-korshak-marines-dug-in].
- **Boats.** The Navy provided some. Most were bought by the brigades through volunteers.
  - The 36th had only eight boats of its own [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-krynky-untold].
  - Craft included "good US ones reinforced with inflatable pontoons" that self-inflate when holed. They survive shrapnel but not a direct FPV hit.
  - One inflatable from the Prytula Foundation cost 388,000 UAH (about US$9,400).
  - At first boats carried 8–10 people. After losses, three-person boats took over [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-krynky-untold].
- **Electronic warfare.** There was "hardly any" EW on the boats, only a large EW system protecting the landing points [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-krynky-untold].
- **Cargo drones.** The Prytula Foundation bought eight hexacopters (20 kg payload) and 40 "Mamont" 10-inch FPV carriers. Each of the four brigades got two hexacopters and ten Mamonts. They carried ammunition, food, water and even blood [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-krynky-untold].
- **Fires.** Artillery and HIMARS fired from the right bank [src:kyivpost-2023-korshak-marines-dug-in] [src:isw-2024-02-20-roca]. Sodol promised that "HIMARS will fire like machine guns". A 36th Brigade source says the promise was not kept [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-krynky-untold].

**The outcome the player must reproduce:**
- **Pokrovsk is lost slowly, not quickly.**
  - *Inside the city:* Russian infiltrators enter in mid-July 2025 and are cleared by 15 August [src:pravda-2025-up-russians-entered-pokrovsk] [src:pravda-2025-romanenko-pokrovsk-cleared]. The city becomes a grey zone from late October [src:pravda-2025-pohorilov-flag-destroyed].
  - *The claim:* Russia claims the capture on 1 December 2025, when a NATO official says Russia holds more than 95% of the city [src:cnn-2025-stockwell-capture-claim] [src:eurointegration-2025-nato-95-percent].
  - *The northern quarters:* Ukraine still claims about 13 of the city's 29 km² in December [src:united24-2025-litnarovych-155000].
  - *The end:* ISW last saw Ukrainian forces inside Pokrovsk on **28 January 2026** and declared the city taken on 25 February [src:isw-2026-02-25-roca].
- **Myrnohrad falls about a month after Pokrovsk.**
  - *Its last road:* the town is sustained by a single road under drone fire, and from late November the corridor is about 1 km wide [src:euromaidanpress-2025-axe-raiders-425th].
  - *The claim:* Russia claims Myrnohrad on 27–28 December 2025, when ISW sees Russians in only 49% of the town [src:isw-2025-12-28-roca].
  - *The fall:* ISW assessed on 4 February 2026 that Myrnohrad had fallen before 28 January [src:isw-2026-02-04-roca]. DeepState marked it occupied on 17 February [src:kyivindependent-2026-terajima-if-you-stop-you-die].
- **The Dobropillia breach is erased.**
  - *The wedge:* about 15 km deep and 5–6 km wide on 11 August [src:euromaidanpress-2025-zoria-deepstate-wedge]. It is cut off by late August, and Kucheriv Yar is retaken on 22 October [src:kyivindependent-2025-pakhnyuk-crab-claws] [src:pravda-2025-romanenko-kucheriv-yar].
  - *The ground:* Syrskyi claims more than 180 km² liberated [src:rbcukraine-2025-kucheriv-yar-liberated]. The operation is declared complete on 29 November [src:ukrinform-2025-apostol-dobropillia-finished].
- **No breakthrough beyond the towns.** Hryshyne, 2 km north-west of Pokrovsk, was still contested in mid-April 2026. Russia did not exploit the fall [src:isw-2026-02-25-roca] [src:euromaidanpress-2026-zoria-hryshyne-center].
- **No clean Ukrainian withdrawal order.**
  - *What the sources show:* soldiers repeatedly said there was no order to leave [src:cnn-2025-kottasova-pokrovsk-poised] [src:pravda-2026-kyrylenko-myrnohrad-staffs]. The exit came in stages: the 68th and 155th brigades left Pokrovsk from late October, the salient south of the city was abandoned on 8 December, and a short fall-back north of the towns followed in February 2026 [src:euromaidanpress-2025-axe-commandos-escape-corridor] [src:euromaidanpress-2025-zoria-salient-withdrawal] [src:euromaidanpress-2026-axe-falling-back-north].
  - *Who called it a regrouping:* "a deliberate regrouping" is the description of the analyst Oleksandr Kovalenko, not an official statement [src:ukrinform-2026-liskovych-front-spring].
- **The price: a slow advance at a huge cost.**
  - *Pace:* just under 50 km from late February 2024 to early January 2026, about 70 m a day, slower than the Allies on the Somme [src:csis-2026-jones-grinding-war].
  - *Losses on the axis (Ukrainian claims):*
    - January 2025: about 7,000 Russians killed and 15,000 casualties in total (Syrskyi). The Guardian's reading of the same briefing is 7,000 killed plus 15,000 wounded or missing [src:euromaidan-2025-mukhina-chechen-war-losses] [src:guardian-2025-harding-pishchane].
    - Dobropillia: 3,185 casualties, including 1,769 killed (Syrskyi, 29 September), against 12,000 including 7,000 killed (Zelensky, 8 October) [src:kyivindependent-2025-hodunova-syrskyi-encircled] [src:isw-2025-10-09-roca].
    - October 2025: about 25,000 Russians confirmed killed on video front-wide, "most" of them on the Pokrovsk front (Zelensky) [src:united24-2025-kulakova-25000-october].
    - An unattributed analytical range of 30,000–40,000 Russians killed in the whole battle [src:euromaidanpress-2025-mukhina-flag-on-mine].
  - *Per km²:* no source gives a Pokrovsk-only figure. The national benchmark is 53 casualties per km² gained (September–November 2024, ISW) and about 85 per km² for 2025 (Radio Svoboda from General Staff and DeepState data) [src:euromaidan-2024-zoria-53-per-km2] [src:euromaidan-2026-tril-cost-per-km].
  - *Force ratio:* Russia committed 110,000–170,000 troops, against a Ukrainian force put at about 30,000; the ratio was 5:1 to 8:1 [src:uacrisis-2025-day-1251-mashovets] [src:dw-2025-oelofse-170000-troops] [src:euromaidanpress-2025-axe-turtle-tanks-myrnohrad] [src:kyivindependent-2025-terajima-8-to-1].
- **Contested points.**
  - *The fall dates:* Russian claims (1 and 27 December) against ISW (28 January for Pokrovsk, some time before 28 January for Myrnohrad). Ukrainian units claimed positions in Myrnohrad on 1 March and on Pokrovsk's northern outskirts on 16 April [src:euromaidanpress-2026-zoria-myrnohrad-quad-bikes] [src:euromaidanpress-2026-zoria-hryshyne-center].
  - *How many Russians were inside Pokrovsk:* about 200 (General Staff, 26 October), at least 250 (UP, 24 October), and 300–500 (military, 11 November) [src:pravda-2025-petrenko-genstaff-200-in-pokrovsk] [src:pravda-2025-kyrylenko-250-russians-pokrovsk] [src:bbc-2025-abdurasulov-fog-pokrovsk].
  - *Whether the Dobropillia fight cost Pokrovsk* (section 7).

## 3. Kill-zone / transparency table

- After the HIMARS strikes, Russia could no longer mass ammunition beside its guns and had to haul it from depots further back [src:rusi-2023-watling-meatgrinder]. This over-stretched logistics is the backdrop to Ukraine's Kharkiv and Kherson offensives (our inference; not a direct claim of the source).
- **The Shahed campaign begins.** Russia sent hundreds of Iranian Shahed-136 against substations, together with cruise and ballistic missiles. RUSI urged more MANPADS, radar-guided AA guns and Western fighters as affordable counters [src:rusi-2022-bronk-russian-air-war].

**Sea and season.**
- The developers say the Black Sea suits drone testing from late March to early November [src:pravda-2024-romaniuk-magura-target-eliminate].
- The Magura V5 handles up to sea state 2. The V7 handles sea state 3, with waves up to 1.25 m [src:euromaidan-2025-zoria-magura-v7][src:defenseexpress-2025-magura-v7].
- The Ivan Khurs mission started late because of bad weather [src:pravda-2024-hur-ivan-khurs-details].

- **The Chelyabinsk warehouse.** A rented shed on Sverdlovsky Trakt. Two agents build 150 quadcopters and eight cabins under video-call instruction from Kyiv, and one roof hinge keeps tearing loose [src:nv-2025-semenova-wsj-spiderweb]. SBU photos show rows of black drones under the roof beams [src:bbc-2025-gozzi-how-ukraine-did-it] [src:guardian-2025-mazhulin-visual-guide].
- **"There are drones under the roof."** About 300 km out on a 3,200 km run, a roof slides off. The driver phones the agent, the agent phones his SBU handler, and Maliuk improvises the hunting-cabin story. The driver fixes the roof with a local tractor driver's help [src:nv-2025-semenova-wsj-spiderweb]. This is the long game's signature risk event.
- **The reveal.** On 1 June Maliuk tells the pilots the target only then, showing maps and aircraft diagrams. One pilot recalls: "there was no alarm" [src:nv-2025-semenova-wsj-spiderweb].
- **Roofs open at Olenegorsk.** A truck by a petrol station 6–7 km from Olenya releases drones. Black smoke rises over the runway, residents count at least 10 explosions, and the driver runs around shouting that "someone would meet me" [src:barentsobserver-2025-chentemirov-olenya-attack] [src:euromaidanpress-2025-zoria-bombers-ablaze]. On the southern apron four Tu-95MS and a propeller transport burn [src:barentsobserver-2025-chentemirov-olenya-attack].
- **Stones against drones at Usolye.** Drivers and onlookers at a Siberian car park climb onto the truck and hurl stones to pin the drones down [src:bbc-2025-gozzi-how-ukraine-did-it] [src:twz-2025-altman-rogoway-bombers-destroyed].
- **"This is what Belaya looks like now."** Maliuk's voice over drone video of Belaya burning, the first strike ever in Siberia [src:pravda-2025-petrenko-pavutyna-first] [src:isw-2025-06-01-roca]. A full single-drone path video runs from the cabin roof to a Tu-22M3 at Belaya [src:wikipedia-operation-spiderweb].
- **Two radomes at Ivanovo.** Drones touch down on the radar domes of two A-50s, one sandbagged and one under tyres. The feed cuts at impact [src:telegraph-2025-barnes-a50-spy-planes] [src:bbc-2025-adams-turning-point]. Whether either was operational is debated (§9).
- **The burning truck at Seryshevo.** The fifth truck, already troubled by its unstable link, burns on the Amur highway. It explodes as a man opens the trailer, and the driver dies [src:euromaidanpress-2025-zoria-trojan-truck] [src:nv-2025-semenova-wsj-spiderweb].
- **The applause room.** In Kyiv, hit after hit lands. Later pilots simply climb and steer for the black smoke [src:nv-2025-semenova-wsj-spiderweb].

**Weather and light** (ERA5 reanalysis, local time) [src:openmeteo-2026-c06-weather]:
- **6–11 Sep at Balakliia and Kupiansk was dry**: 0.0–0.2 mm a day, lows of 5–11 °C and highs of 15–20 °C, with mean cloud cover of 33–77% until it closed in on 10–11 Sep.
- Sunrise was about 05:55 and sunset about 19:05 on 6 Sep. The 03:30 H-hour was in darkness.
- **Rain set in on 12–14 Sep**: 7–14 mm a day at Kupiansk on 12–13 Sep, with 92–100% cloud. This coincided with the halt on the Oskil; no source links the two.
- Around Lyman, 28 Sep – 3 Oct was mild (highs 19–24 °C) and wet: 10 mm on 28 Sep, 8.5 mm on 1 Oct and 13 mm on 2–3 Oct.
- Kyiv Post reported Ukrainian units in the Sviati Hory forests advancing "at night, in fog or rain" [src:kyivpost-2022-korshak-lyman-surrounded].
## 10. Game/sim relevance

**Key locations.** Coordinates are OSM/Nominatim points queried on 2026-10-01 (© OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL) [src:osm-copyright]. They mark settlements and airfields, not the aircraft's actual positions, which no source publishes precisely.

- **Launch from inside Russia, not from Ukraine.** The SBU chose short-range FPVs brought to the fence over long-range drones. The Guardian notes that launching from Ukraine would have meant huge distances through Russian air defences [src:guardian-2025-mazhulin-visual-guide]. ISW credits the choice with operational surprise and a minimal Russian response window [src:isw-2025-06-01-roca].
- **Ukrainian means only, and no notice to the US.** Zelensky wanted "to use only what we produce" [src:euromaidanpress-2025-tril-spiderweb]. Ukraine and the US both say Washington was not told in advance. Axios first reported the opposite and corrected itself [src:twz-2025-altman-rogoway-bombers-destroyed] [src:reuters-2025-stewart-ali-us-estimate].
- **Choosing and vetting agents.** The SBU polygraphed the couple in Lviv before giving them the assembly phase. They then had to pass an FSB questioning at the border. The drivers had to be "reliable but not curious" and were secretly vetted by the SBU [src:nv-2025-semenova-wsj-spiderweb].
- **The strike date.** The original date was about 9 May, and it slipped because of the drivers. The trucks then left on 23–26 May [src:nv-2025-semenova-wsj-spiderweb]. The strike fell the day before the Istanbul talks, which the BBC and others read as deliberate leverage [src:bbc-2025-adams-spiders-web-strike] [src:istories-2025-airfield-attacks-main]. Zelensky said it would not have happened under a ceasefire [src:bbc-2025-adams-turning-point]. He also cited intelligence on a Russian massed strike being prepared [src:istories-2025-airfield-attacks-main], and a Russian outlet had trailed bombers waiting at Olenya and Engels [src:texty-2025-zeus-lightning].
- **The roof-slip crisis.** Maliuk chose a plausible cover story over aborting [src:nv-2025-semenova-wsj-spiderweb].
- **Swapping the broken truck.** Replacing the truck kept the schedule but left an unstable link. The SBU tried to talk the driver through the cabin wiring, and the truck later burned. Ukrainka was never hit [src:nv-2025-semenova-wsj-spiderweb].
- **Target and timing on the day.** Daylight, small quadcopters and aim points on fuel tanks and loaded pylons [src:texty-2025-butusov-pavutyna-preparation] [src:bbc-2025-brown-spencer-satellite]. The bases were struck while Tu-95MS stood fuelled with Kh-101 [src:twz-2025-newdick-confirmed-losses].
- **Withdraw first.** All operatives and helpers were extracted on the eve [src:euromaidanpress-2025-zoria-trojan-truck]. SBU sources pre-empted any Russian arrests as "staged" [src:twz-2025-altman-rogoway-bombers-destroyed].
- **What to publish.** Zelensky told the SBU to release what could be disclosed. The SBU spokesman: "We disclose the details only when it will not hamper the future operations" [src:twz-2025-altman-rogoway-bombers-destroyed] [src:twz-2025-altman-what-we-know-spiderweb]. The BBC notes that almost all information came from the SBU itself [src:bbc-2025-adams-turning-point].
- **Russia's choices.** Russia kept bombers in the open with tyres rather than shelters. Milbloggers and Gurulev blamed the command and the security services [src:isw-2025-06-01-roca] [src:istories-2025-airfield-attacks-main]. Afterwards Russia chose dispersal, a "retaliation" salvo flown by a reduced bomber force, and shelter construction [src:moscowtimes-2025-bombers-relocated] [src:defenseexpress-2025-seven-bombers-kh101] [src:twz-2026-newdick-bomber-shelters].

**Footprint.** The diorama is a horseshoe salient about 12–15 km wide, projecting about 10 km into Russian lines [src:kyivpost-2023-korshak-worst-defeat-avdiivka] [src:kyivpost-2024-korshak-zenit-withdrawal]. A box of about 20 × 15 km holds it: from Berdychi and Krasnohorivka in the north to Opytne and Vodiane in the south, and from Tonenke and Orlivka in the west to Kamianka and the industrial zone in the east. In November Kyiv Post described the central pocket as "funnel-shaped ... less than 15 kilometers wide" [src:kyivpost-2023-korshak-factory-district].
All coordinates come from OSM via Photon [src:osm-2026-vivaldi-geodata], except the forest reserve, which is from the same lookup.
## 3. The diorama: geography, terrain, weather

- **Shell balance improves.** By July 2025 Russia was firing about 27,000 rounds a day and the ratio was 1:1.8 [src:liga-2025-shell-ratio]. The Western counterpart is far lower: open-source estimates compiled by West Point's Modern War Institute put Russian expenditure at 10,000–15,000 rounds a day, against Russian production of about 19,000 rounds a day of all types (about 7M in 2025, including 3.4M howitzer shells). They put Ukrainian fire at 2,000–7,000 rounds a day [src:mwi-2026-meneguzzo-industrial-window].
- **Ammunition supply, 2025.** The Czech initiative gives different totals for the year: 1.8M [src:kyivindependent-2026-pakhnyuk-czech-withdraw], or "almost 2M" and 4.4M cumulative, according to Pavel in February 2026 [src:pravda-2026-czech-initiative-4-4m]. Pavel says it moved the ratio from 1:10 to 1:2 [src:kyivindependent-2025-czech-initiative]. The EU had delivered 80% of its 2M-round 2025 target by September [src:militarnyi-2025-kallas-2m-rounds], and by February 2026 Commissioner Kubilius claimed EU output of "more than two million shells a year" [src:interfax-2026-kubilius-2m-shells]. Ukrainian 155 mm production stayed marginal: the first 10,000 shells came in late 2024, and a planned 100,000 for 2025 did not materialise, for lack of a domestic propellant plant [src:mezha-2025-ukrainian-155mm]. Budanov says North Korea covers about 40% of Russia's artillery needs [src:militarnyi-2025-budanov-dprk-shells], and RUSI calls those shells low quality [src:rusi-2025-watling-third-year]. North Korean deliveries had fallen by more than half by late 2025 [src:mwi-2026-meneguzzo-industrial-window].
- **How artillery is used now.** A fire mission is rarely more than 10 rounds before the gun is spotted, and 8–10 rounds are generally enough to destroy a soft target. Laser-guided rounds handle hard targets that UAVs cannot kill. Ukrainian analysts think about half of the Russian guns claimed as destroyed by UAVs are only damaged and later repaired [src:rusi-2025-watling-combined-arms]. By 2025, Ukraine's MoD counted 819,737 video-confirmed drone hits and credited drones with more than 80% of enemy targets destroyed. Zelensky: "artillery matters, but in a different way" [src:defensenews-2026-ruitenberg-epoints].
- **KAB surge.** About 3,500 a month in early 2025 [src:japcc-2026-zanier-glide-bombs]. A 2025 high of 5,328 in October, with about 40,000 in January–October [src:kyivindependent-2025-taradiuk-kab-october]. About 3,500 in November, for about 44,000 in January–November (130 a day) [src:euromaidanpress-2025-mukhina-84000-kabs].
- **HUR's glide-bomb figures.** HUR says 120,000 glide bombs were planned for 2025, with 200–250 launched a day. About 500 are extended-range (about 200 km), and work on 400 km versions is under way [src:pravda-2025-hur-glide-bomb-production]. Ukrainian SAM units killed up to 100 KABs in September–November 2025, which is the first real anti-KAB capability [src:euromaidanpress-2025-mukhina-84000-kabs]. Pokrova jamming degrades KAB accuracy [src:japcc-2026-zanier-glide-bombs]. Ukrainian officers see the newer powered bombs (Molniya type) as having a low success rate and being easy to intercept [src:rusi-2025-watling-combined-arms].
- **Anti-Shahed adaptation.** Interceptor drones took a growing share of Shahed kills from late 2025. File 01 puts them at about $2,000 each, and a Shahed-type drone costs roughly $20–50k [src:mwi-2026-meneguzzo-industrial-window]. A Shahed carrying an R-60 air-to-air missile, aimed at helicopters, appeared in December 2025 [src:pravda-2026-dotsenko-helicopters-drones].
- **Ukraine opens a SEAD/DEAD campaign** (suppression and destruction of enemy air defences) in late 2025. Oryx confirms 77 Russian SAM systems and 23 radars destroyed in 2025, and ISW counts at least 107 strikes on Russian air defences from November 2025 [src:isw-2026-barros-intermediate-range-strikes].
- **Missile production (HUR, June 2025, per month).** Iskander-M 60–70 (up from 40 in May 2024), Kinzhal 10–15, Kh-101 60–70, Kalibr 25–30, Iskander-K 20–30 and Onyx/Zircon 20–30. Russia also holds a stock of 60 North Korean KN-23 [src:kyivindependent-2025-post-ballistic-production]. RUSI cites Russian MoD plans for more than 750 9M723 and more than 560 Kh-101 in 2025, and notes the Kh-101 upgrades: better terminal visual navigation, cluster warheads and flares against MANPADS [src:rusi-2025-watling-third-year].
- **Strike tempo (October 2025).** About 5,300 Shaheds, 148 ballistic and 74 cruise missiles, roughly three times October 2024. The record was 26 ballistic missiles on 16 October. About 20% of Shaheds hit [src:csis-2025-atalan-october-air-campaign]. Ballistic launches grew more than 700% from 2023 to 2025 [src:csis-2026-jensen-two-strategic-attacks].
- **Ukrainian strike weapons.** Officials said Sapsan (about 300 km, >480 kg warhead) entered serial production in June 2025, and that Neptune production was scaled up [src:kyivindependent-2025-taradiuk-sapsan]. Zelensky dates Sapsan's combat use from 9 Dec 2025, but evidence of wide production "has remained elusive" [src:kyivindependent-2026-rushton-ballistic-gap]. An OSINT tally counts at least 31 Neptunes hitting 26 Russian sites from August 2023 to July 2026, with 2024 the busiest year. The R-360M reaches about 500 km with a 350 kg warhead; the Long Neptune (R-360L) has a 260 kg warhead [src:pravda-2026-harbuz-neptune-record]. The FP-5 Flamingo (about 3,000 km, about 1,150 kg payload) was first used on 30 Aug 2025, against an FSB post in Crimea [src:rbc-2026-vialko-flamingo]. Imagery of its September 2025 strike showed one of three missiles near the aimpoint, with the others 80–100 m and about 200 m off [src:missilematters-2026-hoffmann-flamingo-votkinsk]. A Gripen letter of intent followed in October 2025 [src:wikipedia-ukrainian-air-force].

**Russia: Western Group of Forces** (Col. Gen. Sergei Kuzovlev [src:isw-2025-11-21-roca]).
- *68th Motor Rifle Division (6th CAA, Leningrad MD):* its 121st and 122nd regiments formed the assault groups inside Kupiansk, alongside the 27th Motor Rifle Brigade and the 1855th Battalion [src:isw-2025-12-13-roca].
- *Credited by the MoD with the claimed capture:* the 27th Brigade and the 1486th Regiment [src:isw-2025-11-21-roca].
- *47th Tank Division (1st GTA):* its 153rd Tank Regiment and 272nd Regiment were active on the left bank to the south-east [src:isw-2025-12-12-roca].
- *Drone units:* operators of the 16th Spetsnaz Brigade (GRU) [src:isw-2025-09-15-roca]. Butusov says Rubikon, the Sudniy Den project and the 7th Regiment (11th AC) built the kill zone [src:isw-2025-12-13-roca].
- *Pipe specialists:* troops called "Veterans", with a mining background, run the pipeline operations [src:kyivindependent-2026-terajima-kupiansk-pipelines].
- *Strength inside the town:* see the range in section 1.

By about 21 August the corps had cut across the salient to Kolodiazi. Most of the Russians inside escaped toward the Zherebets [src:euromaidanpress-2026-axe-lyman-salient-240]. Biletskyi revealed the operation only on 15 September, named after Vivaldi's *Four Seasons*: "Vivaldi, as we know, has four seasons, and this is only the first of them" [src:kyivindependent-2026-farrell-vivaldi]. Three "seasons" were made public by 28 September [src:isw-2026-09-28-roca].

1. **The Nove raid (22 May).** M113s, Strykers, BTR-4s and armoured trucks under heavy-bomber cover drive at Nove while Russian drones are jammed. Only fibre FPVs fly, and about five vehicles are hit [src:euromaidanpress-2026-axe-lyman-attacks-sloviansk] [src:euromaidanpress-2026-axe-lyman-salient-240].

3. **The pipeline burns.** Strikes on the intake and the tanker loading point of the Voronezh diesel line halve the fuel of the Western Group [src:euromaidanpress-2026-zoria-vivaldi-targeting].
4. **The cut to Kolodiazi (about 21 Aug).** Pincers from Nove and the west close a loose ring. The Russians slip out through the treelines toward the Zherebets [src:euromaidanpress-2026-axe-lyman-salient-240].
5. **Clown noses (7 Sep).** Biletskyi films himself in front of the Sviatohirsk Lavra, six days after Putin "took" the town [src:kyivindependent-2026-farrell-vivaldi].
6. **Serednie.** Armour rolls in with no losses. Russian bloggers call the footage AI [src:isw-2026-09-18-roca] [src:euromaidanpress-2026-vivdych-serednie-terrain].
7. **Robots from the sky (season 2).** Heavy bombers drop kamikaze UGVs onto mapped command posts more than 10 km deep [src:euromaidanpress-2026-zoria-vivaldi-targeting].
8. **The feint and Nove (season 3, 28 Sep).** Russia burns its reserves on the Shandryholove–Zelena Dolyna axis. BTR VBIEDs crack the fortifications at Nove, and whole units surrender, 250+ prisoners in all [src:euromaidanpress-2026-mukhina-vivaldi-phase3-nove].
9. **The Zherebets withdrawal.** Russians try to hold the west bank at Ivanivka and Zarichne while pulling back across the river [src:isw-2026-09-27-roca].

**The front at the end of September.**
- **ISW's measure.** Between 8 Mar and 8 Sep 2026 Russia lost a net 195.19 km² of ground it had advanced into. Only if infiltration zones are counted does it show a net gain (361.47 km²) [src:isw-2026-09-08-roca]. ISW's summary is "near-zero net gains since March 2026" [src:isw-2026-09-26-assessment].
- **DeepState's measure.** Russian gains fell to 36 km² in July 2026, which is DeepState's figure and 07's computation. Radio Svoboda's 27 km² looks wrong (see 07 §2.7) [src:deepstate-api-history] [src:euromaidan-2026-tril-cost-per-km]. DeepState publishes Ukrainian recaptures late, so Vivaldi's May–Jun gains show up only in its Aug–Sep versions.
- **Putin's deadline** for taking all of Donetsk Oblast is 31 Dec 2026, and ISW judges Russia to be failing against it [src:isw-2026-09-06-roca].

**The water.**
- **The river.** The main river is "around a kilometer wide in its southern parts" [src:kyivindependent-2023-terajima-dnipro-hopeless].
- **The route.** The marines' route was longer than one channel. They crossed the Dnipro, landed on islands, walked "a few kilometres" across them, sheltered in holes, and then crossed more channels such as the Konka or the Krynka. One soldier felt it was "twelve and a half kilometres" [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-krynky-untold].
- **Crossing time.**
  - Before December 2023 a crossing took several hours to a full day.
  - From December, once the small rivers were cleared of mines, the route was continuous and took 40–50 minutes [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-krynky-untold].
  - The Telegraph gives "a 30 to 60-minute boat journey through open water" [src:telegraph-2024-barnes-krynky-1000].
- **The danger points.** These were the bends, where boats slow down, the Konka–Dnipro junctions and the landing points [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-krynky-untold].
- **The last leg.** In March 2024 marines walked 2–3 km of no man's land at night between the village and the boats [src:kyivpost-2024-korshak-krynky-drones].

Vuhledar is a coal-mining town of about 14,000 pre-war residents. Its Soviet-era apartment blocks stand on high ground above flat, open fields, about 2 km north of Pavlivka [src:rferl-2023-eckel-what-happened-vuhledar] [src:forbes-2023-axe-vuhledar-halt]. From those roofs Ukrainian observers overlooked the T-0509 highway and threatened the Donetsk–Volnovakha railway, Russia's only rail link between Donbas and the south [src:rferl-2023-eckel-what-happened-vuhledar] [src:kyivpost-2024-kostezh-why-lost].

**Water and approaches.**
- The strait is the only passage between the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov. The arch's height limit forced some ships to cut their masts [src:wikipedia-crimean-bridge].
- Sea drones reach the bridge from the Black Sea side. The 2023 block-ship line was "about 15 miles north of where the mouth of the Kerch Strait meets the Black Sea, which is the route Ukrainian USVs have almost certainly taken" [src:twz-2023-altman-sinks-ships].
- The ferry route runs north of the bridge [src:maritimeexecutive-2026-rail-ferries].
- On the northern (Sea of Azov) side, a parallel structure with air-defence platforms was under construction in late 2024 [src:usm-2024-bridge-security].

- **nul / na nuli** (нуль, "zero" / "at the zero") — the zero line: the most forward positions.
- **sira zona** (сіра зона) — grey zone: contested ground between the lines. In 2025–26 it is increasingly used as a synonym for the kill zone.
- **kilzona** (кілзона) — kill zone: the belt where drones reliably strike anything that moves. It is measured by strike density, not the maximum range of a drone.
- **posadka** (посадка, plural *posadky*) — tree line or windbreak between fields; the main cover for infantry and for infiltration.
- **blindazh** (бліндаж) — dugout or covered bunker.
- **NRK** (НРК, *nazemnyi robotyzovanyi kompleks*) — ground robotic system, i.e. a UGV.
- **BpLA** (БпЛА) — uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV).
- **REB** (РЕБ, *radioelektronna borotba*) — electronic warfare (EW), especially jammers.
- **RER** (РЕР, *radioelektronna rozvidka*) — radio-electronic reconnaissance; SIGINT/ELINT and direction finding.
- **skyd** (скид) — "drop": a munition dropped from a drone; *skydy* are bomber-drone strikes.
- **optovolokno** (оптоволокно) — fibre optic: FPVs guided through a thin cable that cannot be jammed.
- **ptashka** (пташка, "birdie") — slang for a drone.
- **mavik** — generic slang for a small quadcopter used for reconnaissance or drops, after the DJI Mavic.
- **Kazhan** (Кажан, "Bat") / **Baba Yaha** — heavy multirotor bomber drones, also used for resupply drops.
- **moped** (мопед) — Ukrainian slang for a Shahed/Geran drone, from the sound of its engine.
- **evak** (евак) — casualty evacuation.
- **maket** (макет) — decoy or mockup, e.g. a fake HIMARS or M777.
- **Kropyva** (Кропива, "nettle") — Ukrainian artillery and mapping app (from 2014).
- **GIS Arta** — Ukrainian "Uber for artillery" fire-allocation software.
- **Delta** — Ukrainian cloud-based situational awareness and battle-management system.
- **Vezha** (Вежа, "tower") — Delta's video-analysis platform.
- **Avengers** — MoD AI platform that detects targets in drone and camera video.
- **Mission Control** — Delta's drone-mission planning and reporting module.
- **ePoints / Army of Drones Bonus** — scheme that awards points to units for confirmed strikes.
- **Strelets** — Russian reconnaissance, fire-control and communications data system.
- **RFC / reconnaissance-fire circuit** — Russian term for the sensor-to-shooter kill chain.
- **middle strike** — Ukrainian drone strikes at about 20–200 km depth, against logistics, air defence and command posts.
- **Logistics Lockdown** — the MoD programme (27 May 2026) funding middle-strike units through ePoints; the Kyiv Independent calls it "Logistical Lockdown". Launched under Fedorov and continued under Khmara.
- **whitelist** (*bilyi spysok*, білий список) — the registry of verified Starlink terminals; unregistered terminals stop working in Ukraine from 5 Feb 2026.
- **BAI** — battlefield air interdiction: ISW's term for Russia's drone campaign against Ukrainian supply routes and vehicles in the near rear.
- **Molniya** (Молния, "lightning") — cheap Russian fixed-wing strike drone, also used as an FPV "mothership".
- **mesh modem** — a radio in which every drone relays for the others, so the network survives losing nodes; e.g. the Chinese XK-F358 on Gerans.
- **Rassvet** (Рассвет, "dawn") — Bureau 1440's Russian LEO satellite constellation, the planned Starlink substitute.
- **Volna Kupol Garant** — Russian dish-array jammer that deafens Starlink satellites over about 20 km².
- **Glaz/Groza** (Глаз/Гроза, "eye/thunderstorm") — Russian volunteer-built drone-to-fires software; **Svod** is the Russian MoD's tactical situational-awareness complex.
- **People's Satellite** — the crowdfunded ICEYE SAR satellite whose imagery goes to HUR.
- **Rubikon / Rubicon** — Russia's elite Centre for Advanced Unmanned Technologies.
- **GEGD** — the US government programme that gave Ukraine access to commercial Maxar imagery; suspended for about a week in March 2025.

Kherson Oblast, the Dnipro's left (east) bank between the Antonivskyi bridges and Korsunka; prelude Feb – Sep 2023 (island raids, the Antonivskyi bridge lodgement, the Kozachi Laheri raid), main window 10–17 Oct 2023 to 17 Jul 2024, coda to mid-Aug 2024.

- **Preparation first.**
  - *Restoring command:* rebuild command, replace commanders, set up the surveillance-and-strike system and stockpile [src:twz-2026-altman-vivaldi].
  - *EW:* nine months of EW preparation to blind Russian drones [src:euobserver-2026-vasilko-vivaldi].
  - *An air-defence and EW "dome":* over the assault area, so Russian drones "could not read the operation's design" [src:euromaidan-2026-mukhina-vivaldi-ugv-drop].
  - *"Protective Drone":* Zhorin's EW system, credited with about 20,000 Russian drones [src:euromaidanpress-2026-zoria-isw-drones-out].
- **Counter-drone first.**
  - *Rubikon as the priority target:* reconnaissance identified Rubikon as the unit able to isolate the area. A senior Russian commander pulled it back "just as the assault began" [src:euromaidanpress-2026-zoria-vivaldi-targeting].
  - *Launch sites:* the 60th Brigade hit Russian drone launch points at set times to open windows for the infantry [src:euromaidanpress-2026-mukhina-akhmet-stealth].
- **Middle strike on logistics.**
  - *Depth:* strikes went to 50 km, then 120 km [src:isw-2026-09-15-roca], and over 205 km into Luhansk Oblast [src:euromaidanpress-2026-zoria-luhansk-skies]. Hornet drones hit river crossings more than 150 km deep [src:mwi-2026-rose-vivaldi].
  - *The diesel pipeline:* strikes on both ends of the Voronezh–Luhansk pipeline forced Russia to dismantle it, and fuel now goes by truck on a 400 km run [src:euromaidanpress-2026-zoria-vivaldi-targeting]. Russian drone units could not refuel the generators that charge their batteries, and Russian EW ran in reduced mode [src:isw-2026-09-22-roca].
  - *Repair bases:* the repair base of the 20th CAA and the 144th MRD was pushed to Voronezh Oblast, a 250 km route [src:euromaidanpress-2026-zoria-vivaldi-targeting].
- **Kill the reinforcements, not the infiltrators.** Fires went into the ATV and motorcycle runs sent to stranded groups, which were then cleared by "strike-search" teams [src:isw-2026-09-26-assessment] [src:kyivindependent-2026-farrell-vivaldi]. Many infiltrators surrendered without food or water [src:euobserver-2026-vasilko-vivaldi].
- **C2 decapitation by robot.** Corps and brigade reconnaissance mapped Russian command nodes. Heavy bomber drones then dropped kamikaze UGVs onto them more than 10 km behind the line, forcing Russia to divert troops to guard its headquarters [src:euromaidanpress-2026-zoria-vivaldi-targeting]. The 93rd Brigade's "Desantnyk" uses the same marsupial idea [src:euromaidanpress-2026-mukhina-desantnyk-drop].
- **Robots first.**
  - *Demining:* UGVs cleared 30 km of routes in two nights [src:euromaidan-2026-vivdych-robot-demining].
  - *Bullspike UGVs:* armed UGVs fire into shelters and then detonate [src:euromaidanpress-2026-mukhina-bullspike-ugv].
  - *APC VBIEDs:* remote BTRs packed with TM-62 mines are driven into bunkers. The corps and Euromaidan say BTR-60, ISW says BTR-80 [src:euromaidanpress-2026-axe-btr60-vbied] [src:isw-2026-09-28-roca].
  - *Robot share:* the corps aims to replace 30% of its infantry with robots by the end of 2026 [src:euromaidanpress-2026-mukhina-robots-30pct].
- **Limited mechanised manoeuvre returns.** Mechanised manoeuvre came back in a limited way once drone overmatch was won: armour entered Serednie with no losses [src:isw-2026-09-18-roca] [src:isw-2026-09-20-roca]. "Vehicles didn't win it, they showed up because the conditions… were already gone" (Vitaly) [src:euromaidanpress-2026-axe-lyman-salient-240].
- **Deception and OPSEC.** The corps kept an information blackout and used camouflage, disinformation and the season 3 feint [src:isw-2026-09-25-roca] [src:isw-2026-09-28-roca].
- **The Starlink context.** Losing Starlink grounded Russia's deep strike drones and blinded its HQs but not its fibre FPVs [src:euromaidan-2026-axe-starlink-counterattacks] [src:euromaidan-2026-zoria-air-assault-south]. On 22 May only fibre-optic drones could still fly [src:euromaidanpress-2026-axe-lyman-salient-240]. No source ties Vivaldi directly to the cutoff [src:isw-2026-feb-26-assessment].
- **Russian counters.**
  - *Infiltration:* small groups and flag-planting, including flags flown in by drone [src:isw-2026-09-22-roca].
  - *Glide bombs:* on Izium and Raihorodok [src:isw-2026-09-17-roca].
  - *Blind bombing:* of windbreaks [src:isw-2026-09-25-roca].
  - *Reserves:* sent to hold the Zherebets [src:isw-2026-09-22-roca].

**Ukraine (Kharkiv and Slobozhanske grouping).**
- **Command.** Col Gen Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of the Ground Forces, planned and ran the operation; Brig Gen Oleksandr Tarnavsky was his deputy. C-in-C Zaluzhnyi was above them [src:wapo-2022-khurshudyan-inside-counteroffensive; src:wikipedia-2022-kharkiv-counteroffensive].
- **Manoeuvre brigades**, with their roles as reported:
  - **25th Airborne**: Volokhiv Yar on day 1, Izium on 10 Sep, then Korovii Yar and into Lyman from the Drobysheve side [src:wikipedia-25th-airborne-brigade].
  - **92nd Mechanised**: from Andriivka to Kupiansk, taken on 10 Sep [src:wikipedia-2022-kharkiv-counteroffensive].
  - **80th Air Assault**: at the Oskil at Senkove on 8 Sep; later Oskil village, Yatskivka, Pisky-Radkivski and Borova [src:wikipedia-2022-kharkiv-counteroffensive; src:wikipedia-80th-air-assault-brigade].
  - **3rd Tank**: Nova Husarivka, Bairak, Shchurivka and Balakliia; elements at Izium per Neil Hauer [src:wikipedia-3rd-heavy-mechanized-brigade].
  - **14th Mechanised**: Ternova on the border on 12 Sep [src:wikipedia-2022-kharkiv-counteroffensive].
  - **81st Airmobile**: Bohorodychne by 11–12 Sep; Novoselivka near Lyman on 28 Sep [src:wikipedia-2022-kharkiv-counteroffensive; src:wikipedia-2022-lyman-front].
  - **54th Mechanised**: also listed [src:wikipedia-2022-kharkiv-counteroffensive].
  - Wikipedia's 4th Guards Tank Division article cites a Ukrainian **4th Tank Brigade** trying to encircle that division outside Izium [src:wikipedia-4th-guards-tank-division].
- **Territorial Defence.**
  - 113th (Shevchenkove, Velykyi Burluk, border near Vovchansk) and 112th (45 km advance to Vovchansk by 12 Sep).
  - 128th, 124th, 107th (93rd Bn at Velyka Komyshuvakha), 127th (north of Kharkiv) and 111th.
  - 103rd, whose battalions worked the Donets and Lyman flank from 3 Sep [src:wikipedia-2022-kharkiv-counteroffensive].
- **Fires.** 26th, 40th, 43rd and 44th Artillery Brigades, the 107th Rocket Artillery Brigade and the 15th Artillery Reconnaissance Brigade, as named by Zelensky on 14 Sep [src:wikipedia-2022-kharkiv-counteroffensive]. Each attacking brigade had at least eight M777s, some delivered the night before H-hour [src:wapo-2022-khurshudyan-inside-counteroffensive].
- **Special and security forces.**
  - HUR (Main Intelligence Directorate) [src:wikipedia-2022-kharkiv-counteroffensive]. Its Kraken unit is reported as key at Izium [src:wikipedia-kraken-regiment].
  - Special forces, including the "Bohun" unit whose press officer was Taras Berezovets [src:guardian-2022-koshiw-southern-offensive-trick].
  - Military-intelligence and SBU units acting as "raid squads" in the exploitation echelon [src:euromaidan-2022-shandra-kharkiv].
  - The Kharkiv special-forces detachment of the Azov Regiment [src:isw-2022-09-12-roca].
  - The National Guard's 15th Regiment and the volunteer battalion "Slobidska Sich" [src:wikipedia-2022-kharkiv-counteroffensive; src:mvs-2022-slobidska-sich-counteroffensive].
- **Strength.** No total is published. WaPo says "thousands" of soldiers were assembled [src:wapo-2022-khurshudyan-inside-counteroffensive], and Bielieskov says Ukraine "concentrated everything we could" in the Balakliia–Kupiansk–Izium area [src:euromaidan-2022-shandra-kharkiv]. A typical lead company was about 100 men in columns of three IFVs [src:wapo-2022-khurshudyan-inside-counteroffensive].
- **Ammunition.** About 32,500 artillery rounds were used in five days, against a feared need of over 100,000 [src:wapo-2022-khurshudyan-inside-counteroffensive].

- **No Oryx list for Vuhledar alone.** Oryx's master list [src:oryx-russian-equipment-losses] does not tag locations. The only Oryx-derived figure found covers Avdiivka and Vuhledar together for 8–10 Feb [src:insider-2023-oryx-103-vehicles].
  - Wikipedia cites WarSpotting at "107+ armoured vehicles (17+ tanks)" for the whole 2022–24 battle [src:wikipedia-battle-of-vuhledar]. This was not checked directly, and a location-filtered WarSpotting export would settle it.
- **The Ukrainian order of battle is thin.** The roles of the 68th Jaeger Brigade and the Kalinouski Regiment rest on Wikipedia's citations of the Washington Post [src:wikipedia-battle-of-vuhledar]. Battalion dispositions, artillery numbers, RAAM rounds fired, and minefield extents and locations are not public.
- **Ukrainian personnel losses for Jan–Mar 2023 are unknown.** Wikipedia cites a Times figure for Sep 2022, a CBC figure for one battalion, and BBC Ukrainian name counts, none of them checked [src:wikipedia-battle-of-vuhledar].
- **Exact dates of the iconic videos.** The "second column on the same route" video and the 13+12 engagement can be dated only to early February from their posting dates [src:politico-2023-melkozerova-155th-brigade] [src:isw-2023-02-09-roca]. GeoConfirmed's geolocations could give exact positions.
- **The Ka-52 claims** (5–6 shot down on 24–28 Jan) and the strike on a building of reinforcements at "Kyrylivka" come via Tom Cooper's blog, relayed by Wikipedia. They are unverified [src:wikipedia-battle-of-vuhledar].
- **Sergey Polyakov's** death and brigade are reported only by unofficial Russian sources via CNN [src:cnn-2023-lister-vuhledar-turkeys].
- **The size of the 155th** before the battle is disputed: about 2,000 (Kyiv Post) against 5,000 (Ukrainian spokesman) [src:kyivpost-2023-korshak-vuhledar-marines] [src:politico-2023-melkozerova-155th-brigade].
- **The "Pivdennodonbaska No. 3"** mine near Vodiane needs matching to its OSM feature [src:isw-2024-09-30-roca] [src:osm-copyright].
- **Not examined:** satellite imagery of the battlefield (Sentinel-2 or commercial) and the UK MoD image itself.

## 6. Set pieces

section: 5. Russia's side as reported (Ukrainian and Western sources)

markdown: ### e2-donbas-artillery (May – Aug 2022)

**Ukrainian.**
- **Small-boat night crossings and casevac.** Disembarkation was drilled (the 501st recce dropped life jackets because taking one off on shore costs about 30 seconds). "Camels", or "logisticians", waited at the shore to guide new arrivals [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-krynky-untold]. Men keep apart so that "at least one of them survives to call in an evacuation" [src:kyivindependent-2023-terajima-dnipro-hopeless].
- **Hobby and FPV drones.** Ukraine had "particularly effective use of small attack uncrewed aerial vehicles" (UK MoD) [src:euromaidan-2023-zoria-uk-intel-krynky]. One example was a drone carrying an RPG-7 warhead that hit a vehicle 7–8 km inland [src:kyivpost-2023-korshak-marines-dug-in].
  - Brovdi claims 2,900 Russian drones downed or jammed since October and about 77% of incoming drones defeated. Some were hijacked and flown back [src:kyivpost-2024-korshak-krynky-drones].
- **Counter-battery and deep fires from the right bank.** HIMARS struck the 35th MRB column at Hladkivka [src:kyivpost-2023-korshak-marines-dug-in]. A regimental commander said Russian long-range artillery was "heavily suppressed" by December [src:nyt-2023-gall-marines-suicide-mission].
- **Drone resupply** to the left bank by hexacopters and Mamonts [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-krynky-untold].
- **What was missing.** Air defence against glide-bomb carriers, enough boats, EW on the boats, long-range fires and armour [src:kyivpost-2023-korshak-glide-bombs-krynky] [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-krynky-untold] [src:kyivindependent-2023-terajima-dnipro-hopeless]. The US aid delay of early 2024 "likely only aggravated the problem" [src:kyivindependent-2024-ostiller-krynky-lost].

- **Ukrainian losses and strength.** No figures were found for casualties, total troops, brigade strengths or vehicle numbers.
- **Russian strength on 6 Sep.** Only fragments exist: the Balakliia force's percentages, and an Izium grouping of about 9,000–10,000. Total Russian personnel losses exist only as claims.
- **The precise area for 6–12 Sep.** ISW's daily figures stop at "over 3,000 km²". The 6,000 and 8,000 km² figures mix the south and later days. A DeepState-based computation for 6–13 Sep only, inside Kharkiv Oblast, would settle it; it was not run here.
- **Date conflicts.**
  - Balakliia: 8 Sep (ISW) against formal control on 10 Sep (Wikipedia).
  - Izium: 10 Sep (Wikipedia, WaPo) against 11 Sep (ISW geolocation).
  - Kharkiv Oblast "completely liberated" on 4 Oct (NGU), against 6% still occupied on 27 Sep (Syniehubov) and Russian presence east of the Oskil afterwards.
- **The start line.** Pryshyb (Wikipedia, about 9 km NW of Balakliia by OSM, not the 15 km stated) or Andriivka for the 92nd.
- **Unit roles.** The roles of the 3rd and 4th Tank Brigades and of Kraken rest on Wikipedia citing Hauer and Butusov; they need primary confirmation. HUR and SSO actions are almost undocumented in English.
- **Not fetched.**
  - The Forbes (Axe) pieces on 4th GTD tank losses and the "10,000 surrounded" story returned 403, so they are cited only via Wikipedia.
  - The CNN source of the "338" Oryx figure was not fetched.
  - The FT interactive did not render without JavaScript.
- **The Ukrainian reasoning for halting at the Oskil** is not documented in the sources found. Only Reznikov's caution and ISW's "if they choose" are available.
- **Rail detail.** Exact Russian railheads and their daily throughput in Kupiansk-Vuzlovyi and Izium before the attack are unknown.
- **Weather** is ERA5 reanalysis, not station data. There are no sources on fog or visibility for 6 Sep.

- **The pre-war track record was mixed.** A Marine Corps University game two weeks before the invasion anticipated the main axes. It missed because it had Russia destroy Ukrainian air defences first and could not model Zelenskyy's leadership or Ukrainian morale [src:wotr-2022-lacey-wargame-before-the-war]. The long-war follow-up (three-month turns, drones, munitions depletion, mobilisation, aid and sanctions) forecast stalemate and found that political objectives overrode military advice [src:mwi-2022-lacey-wargaming-long-war]. Earlier RAND Baltic wargaming shows how pre-2022 professional work centred on NATO–Russia massed manoeuvre [src:rand-2016-shlapak-baltics].
- **The 2023 counteroffensive showed the limits.** Eight US–Ukrainian tabletop exercises shaped the plan. A senior Ukrainian officer said afterwards that the methods "doesn't work" given ubiquitous drones, trenches and no air superiority. Brynen argues for proper post-mortems rather than rejecting wargaming [src:paxsims-2023-brynen-wargaming-doesnt-work].
- **The 2025 battlefield described by RUSI** has three zones (contested, a ~30 km middle and deep), a seven-phase offensive cycle, small dispersed packets, EW integral down to platoon, and FPV crews who "can see far more targets than they can hit" [src:rusi-2025-watling-combined-arms]. Soft vehicles cannot operate within about 10 km of the front, resupply goes by foot, quad bike, horse and UAV, and few commercial wargames model any of this [src:paxsims-2025-brynen-emergent-approaches].
- **Western training still lagged the drone war in 2025.** Interviews with trainers in Germany found that the German colonel running staff training for Ukrainians "used a wargame scenario straight out of the Cold War, refusing to add drones and other modern weaponry". The US training group cited "broken simulation platforms", and Ukrainian trainees rejected a drone course until it was rebuilt around frontline tactics in June 2025 [src:mwi-2025-hood-matisek-tingle-learn-or-lose]. A retired US general argues for digital games as training for fights full of "electronic jamming, drones, sensors, and missiles". He notes that Russia has codified PC-based simulator training for drone and anti-drone operators [src:wotr-2025-votel-military-gaming].
- **NATO–Russia games since 2025 put drones at the centre.**
  - A December 2025 game by Die Welt and the German Wargaming Center (Helmut Schmidt University) had Russia seize Marijampolė with about 15,000 troops. The German brigade in Lithuania failed to intervene "in part because Russia used drones to lay mines on roads leading out of its base". A Baltic ambassador disputed the premise that Lithuania would not fight [src:paxsims-2026-hybrid-warfare-nato-cohesion].
  - The ARRC's exercise Arrcade Strike (May 2026) rehearsed defending Estonia in 2030 from a "Ukraine-style bunker" under Charing Cross station. The plan has thousands of drones lead the counterattack. Yet the British Army is estimated to be 80–90% short of the drones it needs and would run out in under a week at a few hundred a day [src:guardian-2026-sabbagh-arrcade-strike].
  - Canadian Army structure games (2024–26), run by Maj Ed Farren, reached the lesson that "a platoon with a drone is better than platoon without a drone, but that wasn't the problem". The problem was that the enemy's "sense and strike complex was pretty much unassailable" by jamming, counter-UAS or counter-battery fire [src:canadianarmytoday-2026-thatcher-wargaming-modernization].
- **Dstl builds on commercial engines.** Since 2019 Dstl and Slitherine/Matrix Pro Simulations have built professional wargames on commercial game technology. They have been used for contingency planning, British Army structure and "the potential of remote and autonomous systems", and Dstl claims they cut analysis time and cost by 50% [src:govuk-2024-dstl-slitherine-gaming-tech]. No public Dstl game specifically on Ukraine's drone lessons was found.
- **Ukrainian military simulation.** From Dec 2022 to May 2023, volunteers used Steel Beasts PE to run brigade and battalion CPXs for newly generated formations. They integrated JCATS, SBPro and VBS3, with VBS3 drones feeding commanders' picture [src:llnl-2023-lasch-simulation-support-uaf]. By 2025 the National Guard had adopted a Ukrainian-localised Steel Beasts Pro [src:defender-2025-pokotylo-steel-beasts]. VBS4 now ships Ukrainian terrain with drones and loitering munitions, and its vendor concedes that brigade ops, logistics and morale were weak points [src:nextgov-2024-breeden-vbs4-ukraine]. Domestic tools fill the drone and air-defence end: UFDS and Obriy for crews and interceptors, and the MoD-codified Chaika VR trainers for shooting down drones [src:euromaidanpress-2026-ufds-interceptors][src:ukrainesarmsmonitor-2026-obriy][src:euromaidanpress-2025-seagull-flyswatter].
- **The Russian side** runs command-staff games (KShVI) that rehearse procedure, including EW and counter-UAV, but do not test assumptions. That left planners blind to drone saturation and ISR transparency [src:paxsims-2026-brynen-how-russia-wargames].
- **AI in wargaming.** A September 2026 GPT-assisted negotiation game was drafted in about two hours. Its designer insists that humans choose the abstractions and that AI output needs verification and playtesting [src:paxsims-2026-taylor-gpt-negotiation-game].

1. **The drama theatre (16 Mar).** A theatre sheltering hundreds, with "children" painted on the square, is hit by two 500 kg bombs shortly after 10:00. The death toll is contested: at least a dozen (Amnesty), at least 15 (HRW), about 300 (Ukrainian officials) and about 600 (an AP investigation) [src:amnesty-2022-mariupol-theatre] [src:hrw-2024-beneath-the-rubble] [src:wikipedia-siege-of-mariupol]. As a set piece it is a civilian-shelter event the player cannot prevent; it is part of the prelude.
2. **The first night run (21 Mar).** The first mission had been scrubbed on 19 Mar and men had phoned home to say it was off. Two Mi-8s lift off from Dnipro at 03:30 and refuel at the line. They cross 60 mi of occupied ground at treetop height, and one clips a tree. They land beside a tunnel mouth while Azov fires to cover them, take on about 16 wounded and are back by 07:30 [src:twz-2022-altman-flint-helicopter-rescue] [src:time-2024-spencer-collins-mariupol-helicopters]. One pilot volunteered because his wife was a combat medic in the plant [src:twz-2022-altman-flint-helicopter-rescue].
3. **Fog over the sea (28 Mar).** On mission 3 the guns are stripped for 200 kg more medicine, and the crew is told the flight is "two missions with one helicopter each". Dawn breaks over the sea. The pilot finds the plant by its stacks through the fog, pops up over the 30–40 m power lines and dives in, then spends 12 minutes on the ground [src:time-2024-spencer-collins-mariupol-helicopters].
4. **The Illich breakout (night 11–12 Apr).** The marines' pocket in the northern works is out of ammunition. Two groups break out: one north (Baraniuk, captured) and one to Azovstal (Volynskyi, about 500 men). Russia parades its claimed "1,026 prisoners" [src:wikipedia-siege-of-mariupol] [src:wikipedia-serhii-volynskyi] [src:isw-2022-04-13-roca].
5. **Blockade, not storm (21 Apr).** In the staged Putin–Shoigu meeting, the storm of the plant is called off in favour of starvation [src:isw-2022-04-21-roca]. This is a pacing beat: the map goes quiet and the bombing grows heavier.
6. **The field hospital (28 Apr).** Heavy bombs hit the plant's field hospital [src:isw-2022-04-28-roca]. Inside, amputations are done without painkillers and infections turn deadly [src:time-2024-spencer-collins-mariupol-helicopters] [src:kyivindependent-2024-shulzhenko-kozatskyi].
7. **The convoy (29 Apr – 3 May).** A UN/ICRC convoy drives 230 km and civilians climb out of the bunkers. Firing resumes the moment the pause ends [src:un-ukraine-2022-05-01-ocha-azovstal] [src:un-ukraine-2022-05-03-lubrani-azovstal] [src:isw-2022-05-03-roca].
8. **"Orest's" light (10 and 20 May).** Kozatskyi's photos of bunkers and the wounded, including his own portrait in a shaft of light, go out from inside the plant. His last post before captivity reads: "I am thankful to Azovstal for shelter – the place of my death and my life" [src:kyivindependent-2024-shulzhenko-kozatskyi] [src:euronews-2022-kozatskyi-photos].
9. **The walk-out (16–20 May).** Before leaving, the defenders destroy phones, weapons and documents; then the wounded go to Novoazovsk and the rest to Olenivka [src:pravda-2025-palamar-mariupol-interview] [src:pravda-2022-tyshchenko-general-staff-garrison-mission].
10. **Epilogue: Olenivka (28–29 Jul).** The barracks explosion kills at least 50 prisoners. The UN later rules out a HIMARS strike [src:un-news-2023-olenivka-justice] [src:kyivpost-2023-afp-olenivka-not-himars]. This belongs in the debrief, not in play.

- **The night crossing.** Inflatables and three-man boats run a 40–50 minute route (from December) through channels and islands, with loud motors and Russian drones overhead. The boats must slow at the bends, the most dangerous points, and land where mortars follow within minutes [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-krynky-untold] [src:kyivindependent-2023-terajima-dnipro-hopeless].
- **The Iskander strike on the rail-bridge embankment (~19 Oct 2023).** The 36th Brigade asked for a chain of 10–15 supply posts along a 3.5 km embankment with swamp on both sides. It was told to keep pushing to Poima. Iskanders, air strikes and tank fire then cost it 90 killed or wounded [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-krynky-untold].
- **The first landing in Krynky (27 Oct 2023).** Thirteen men leave a three-man boat and sink waist-deep in silt. There is no guide. One marine shouts to the next crews to follow his voice. They take over abandoned Russian trenches and fight street by street toward Kozachi Laheri [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-krynky-untold].
- **The woods.** Marines hold the forest on both flanks for up to two months, under branches in the cold. The forest floor is strewn with Russian dead [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-krynky-untold].
- **The FPV-struck evacuation (11 Dec 2023).** A wounded marine's boat is hit. He swims one-armed to an island and paces the shore, soaking wet, from midnight to 06:00 so as not to freeze [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-krynky-untold].
- **Shoigu's flag (20–21 Feb 2024).** Shoigu reports Krynky cleared. A clip shows two Russian soldiers raising a flag at the edge of the village and then hurrying back. Ukraine's Southern Command says "this information is not true" [src:isw-2024-02-20-roca] [src:kyivpost-2024-shoigu-krynky-denial].
- **The cellars.** By March 2024, 60–100 marines live underground through the daylight drone hours and come out at night to meet the boats [src:kyivpost-2024-korshak-krynky-drones].
- **The last swim.** When no boat can get through, drones drop life vests to the last men, who swim back [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-krynky-untold].

**Key battles and operations.** Supporting attacks at Bakhmut began in mid-May. The main **Orikhiv–Tokmak** axis opened on **3 Jun 2023**. Meteorit line charges were used to clear lanes through minefields [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons]. The **Kakhovka dam** was destroyed in the first week, and the **Wagner mutiny** followed in late June [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons] [src:wikipedia-russo-ukrainian-war]. A breakthrough was likeliest in early August. By mid-September the goals were tactical, and **Krynky** (across the Dnipro) was the last attempt [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons]. Over 2023 as a whole the line barely moved: Ukraine lost about 540 km² and regained about 430 km² (DeepState) [src:euromaidan-2025-hrudka-2024-3600].

**Ukraine: Operational Command South**
- **Command.** Maj. Gen. Andrii Kovalchuk commanded at first; Brig. Gen. Oleksandr Tarnavskyi took over in October. The "Kakhovka" operational group fought in the northern sector [src:wikipedia-2022-kherson-counteroffensive].
- **Strength.** About three dozen army, marine and territorial battalions, perhaps 20,000 combat troops [src:forbes-2022-axe-attacking-everywhere].
- **Brigades named in sources.**
  - 28th Mechanized: Oleksandrivka and Posad-Pokrovske sector, then Kyselivka on 10 Nov and Kherson on 11–12 Nov [src:wikipedia-28th-mechanized-brigade] [src:wikipedia-2022-kherson-counteroffensive].
  - 59th Motorized and 63rd Mechanized: named by Zelensky with the 28th as liberators of Kherson [src:kyivpost-2022-60-settlements] [src:wikipedia-63rd-mechanized-brigade].
  - 57th Motorized: Velyke Artakove, Bila Krynytsia, Andriivka and Sukhyi Stavok [src:wikipedia-57th-motorized-brigade].
  - 60th Mechanized: Ivanivka in July, then one battalion with one of the 128th's in the October drive on Zolota Balka, Dudchany and Mylove. It had had no break since February [src:wikipedia-60th-mechanized-brigade].
  - 128th Mountain Assault: heavy losses in the first days, then Myroliubivka on 3 Oct [src:wikipedia-128th-mountain-assault-brigade].
  - 35th and 36th Marine: the push south from the Inhulets, Bruskynske, and Davydiv Brid on 4 Oct [src:forbes-2022-axe-attacking-everywhere] [src:wikipedia-2022-kherson-counteroffensive] [src:isw-2022-10-04-roca].
  - 46th Airmobile: reported by Russian sources near Ishchenka [src:isw-2022-10-13-roca].
  - 131st Reconnaissance Battalion: Snihurivka [src:wikipedia-2022-kherson-counteroffensive].
  - Special Operations Forces, the GUR, National Guard and partisans [src:kyivpost-2022-60-settlements] [src:twz-2022-newdick-antonivskyi-bridge].
- **Long-range fires.** Ukraine had 4 HIMARS by 24 June and 8 by mid-July [src:kyivindependent-2022-himars-arrive]. Four more arrived on 1 August together with German MARS II [src:pravda-2022-reznikov-four-himars]. By 8 September the US had sent 16 launchers and "thousands" of GMLRS rockets [src:defenseone-2022-tucker-milley-himars], and British M270s were in service from July [src:oryx-heavy-weaponry-supplied-ukraine]. No source splits the launchers between the Kherson and Kharkiv fronts.
- **Losses.** Ukraine published no figures.
  - Wounded soldiers interviewed by the Washington Post spoke of units with almost all 120 men wounded, 7 killed and 20 wounded out of 100, and 16 of 32 wounded. One said "We lost five people for every one they did" [src:stripes-2022-hudson-kherson-toll].
  - RUSI counts the Kherson push, with the Donbas defence, among the two main sources of the roughly 30,000 Ukrainian killed and missing in 2022 [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].
  - Russia claimed 9,500 Ukrainian killed and wounded [src:wikipedia-2022-kherson-counteroffensive].

- **Official denial.**
  - *Sviatohirsk:* Putin claimed on 1 Sep that it had been seized [src:isw-2026-09-02-roca].
  - *19 Sep:* the MoD said the Western Group was "successfully" attacking toward Oskil, Krymky and Studenok and "clearing" Lyman and Sviatohirsk, and accused Ukraine of lies [src:isw-2026-09-19-roca].
  - *29 Sep:* the MoD published older videos "in" Ridkodub, Novomykhailivka and Nove [src:isw-2026-09-29-roca].
  - *Encirclements:* the Dobropillia "encirclement" claim (22 Sep) and the earlier Rubtsi claim (June) [src:isw-2026-09-22-roca].
- **Milblogger admissions.**
  - *Radov (6 Sep):* "a counteroffensive for 2.5 months, which our command is trying not to notice" [src:kyivindependent-2026-farrell-vivaldi].
  - *Rybar:* Russian units advanced in the first half of summer, but Ukraine counterattacked in August, then "deployed reserves… toward Zherebets in order to align the front along the water barrier and return it to the configuration of the end of 2025". It also says Russian forces "do not even control the airspace immediately near the front line" [src:twz-2026-altman-vivaldi] [src:euromaidanpress-2026-axe-lyman-salient-240].
  - *Dva Mayora and Starshe Edy (28 Sep):* the "information policy" and lying wrecked planning and reinforcement [src:isw-2026-09-28-roca].
  - *Tsaryov:* denial let Ukraine set off an "information bomb" [src:isw-2026-09-29-roca].
  - *A rank-and-file blogger:* "We're totally f*cked on the Lyman front" [src:mwi-2026-rose-vivaldi].
- **Command consequences.** A Western Group source said Gerasimov may have dismissed the 20th CAA commander, Yurchenko [src:isw-2026-09-16-roca]. Russian sources spoke of withdrawing from south of Lyman to the Zherebets [src:isw-2026-09-26-assessment]. Another blogger said commanders hid losses by throwing together half-trained assault groups [src:euromaidanpress-2026-isw-vivaldi-fortress-belt].
- **Counter-narrative.** On 30 Sep a milblogger insisted that Ukraine was faking its Shandryholove footage and that Russia still held positions in Lyman [src:isw-2026-09-30-roca]. Russians had called the Serednie videos AI fakes [src:euromaidanpress-2026-vivdych-serednie-terrain].
- **Independent Russian outlet.** Meduza (as relayed by EUobserver) called it a series of local successes rather than a strategic breakthrough [src:euobserver-2026-vasilko-vivaldi].

- **Total losses.** No reliable totals for the Battle of Kyiv exist (MWI) [src:mwi-2025-collins-spencer-battle-of-kyiv]. No count of vehicles destroyed on the convoy road was found. Oryx (`oryx-russian-equipment-losses`) has no breakdown by road, and its aircraft list gives no places [src:oryx-2022-aircraft-losses-list].
- **No km² figure** for the ground regained in the north was found. Note that the KB source `kyivpost-2022-60-settlements` is about Kherson, not Kyiv.
- **The Kozarovychi blast** is contested on three counts:
  - the date: 25 or 26 Feb;
  - the actor: a volunteer team with an army engineer (MWI), the Armed Forces (Wikipedia), or HUR and "The Diver" (WaPo);
  - the area (2,800 or 13,000 ha) and the rise (0.5 to 2 m).
  The Ukrainian-language sources were not used.
- **Hostomel numbers** are contested:
  - helicopters: 20 in two waves (RUSI), or 34;
  - Il-76s: 18 or 41;
  - troops in the airlift: 1,000 to 5,000;
  - defenders: 200 to 300;
  - border crossing: 08:00 or 09:30.
  Which of Oryx's six airport-perimeter helicopters fell on 24 Feb is unclear [src:oryx-2022-janovsky-hostomel-destination-disaster].
- **Who destroyed the Mriya**, and exactly when between 24 and 27 Feb, is not established [src:kyivindependent-2022-ponomarenko-an225-chief-pilot].
- **Aerorozvidka.**
  - The claim is the commander's own and was not independently verified [src:guardian-2022-borger-aerorozvidka-convoy]. It is undated and located only "near Ivankiv".
  - **The KB claim 05-0009-02 reverses the order.** The Guardian original has the lead vehicles first, then the supply depot. Defense Express's rewrite put the depot first [src:defenseexpress-2022-aerorozvidka-convoy].
  - Pavliuk's "30 SSO soldiers" disabling the lead three vehicles is probably the same action [src:ukrinform-2023-pavliuk-30-sof].
- **The tyre theory** (cheap tyres, poor maintenance) is carried only by the BBC and a Wikipedia relay of Forbes [src:bbc-2022-why-convoy-stopped] [src:wikipedia-2026-russian-kyiv-convoy].
- **Units, unconfirmed.**
  - The 98th VDV Division's presence.
  - The 155th Naval Infantry at Moshchun, which rests on Ukrainian identifications.
  - Which unit died at Vokzalna.
  - The numbers of the "two artillery brigades" in Kyiv and of the TDF brigades other than the 112th.
- **Makariv.** Credit for the 2 Mar recapture is contested: the 14th Mechanised (ISW) or the 95th Air Assault (MWI) [src:isw-2022-03-02-roca] [src:mwi-2025-collins-spencer-battle-of-kyiv]. The town was a "gray zone" again on 25 Mar [src:wikipedia-2026-battle-of-makariv].
- **The Moshchun hold-or-withdraw exchange** is dated about 14 Mar by most sources and 21 Mar by SWJ.
- **Air losses near Kyiv** could not be placed. The Su-27 crash street of 25 Feb and the S-400 attribution for Oksanchenko are unconfirmed.
- **Unfetched sources.**
  - ISW warning updates for 28 Feb, 1 Mar and 29 Mar.
  - The NYT Bucha investigations: the satellite analysis of 4 Apr and the 234th Regiment piece of Dec 2022.
  - The OHCHR primary reports, so the figure of 73 comes via Wikipedia.
  - Forbes on the tyres, Reuters on the convoy, the DoD statements of 16 and 31 Mar, and WaPo's 30 Mar Moshchun report.

- **8th Combined Arms Army** (Lt Gen Andrei Mordvichev), incl. the 150th MRD (68th Tank Regiment, 102nd MR Regiment) [src:hrw-2024-mariupol-whos-responsible].
- **Black Sea Fleet**: 810th Naval Infantry Brigade and 382nd Marine Battalion. The 810th was still blockading the plant on 30 Apr [src:hrw-2024-mariupol-whos-responsible] [src:isw-2022-04-30-roca].
- **Spetsnaz**: 22nd and 346th brigades [src:hrw-2024-mariupol-whos-responsible].
- **Chechen forces**: the 141st Special Motorized Regiment and a Rosgvardia special-purpose police regiment [src:hrw-2024-mariupol-whos-responsible].
- **DNR 1st Army Corps**: Vostok Battalion, "Somalia" tank battalion, 9th Marine Regiment, Slovyansk Brigade, 107th Regiment, Kaskad [src:hrw-2024-mariupol-whos-responsible].
- **Overall siege commander** per Wikipedia: Mikhail Mizintsev [src:wikipedia-siege-of-mariupol].
- **Strength over time.** About 14,000 in March [src:wikipedia-siege-of-mariupol]. The Ukrainian General Staff claimed up to 17 BTGs (about 20,000) were pinned [src:defenceua-2022-mariupol-garrison-mission]. US officials: a dozen BTGs on 21 Apr, two on 9 May [src:isw-2022-04-21-roca] [src:isw-2022-05-09-roca].
- **Air**: Tu-22M3 strikes from about 16 Apr [src:isw-2022-04-16-roca] [src:isw-2022-04-17-roca].
- **Losses**: Ukraine claims 6,500 killed [src:wikipedia-siege-of-mariupol].

- **Commit the second Bradley.** "There was another crew that came first. It didn't work out, so we had to muster up the courage and go" [src:twz-2024-altman-bradley-gunner].
- **Switch from AP to blinding fire.** The gunner changed rounds and aim point after a problem with the AP ammunition, choosing a mission kill over penetration [src:twz-2024-altman-bradley-gunner].
- **25 mm instead of the TOW.** This is debated: an expert says the TOW is the trained answer, "unless they were out". A master gunner says the 25 mm can be "just as good as the TOW in certain situations" [src:twz-2024-altman-bradley-t90m-experts].
Foliage matters: Russia was racing the winter leaf-fall that strips cover from infiltrators [src:euromaidanpress-2026-axe-lyman-attacks-sloviansk].

- **The foothold.** Hold a foothold on the left bank in and around Krynky from mid-October 2023 until about late June to mid-July 2024, roughly nine months.
  - The marines probably never controlled all of Krynky. They held about half of it [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-krynky-untold].
  - Soldiers put the bridgehead at 300–500 m to 2.5 km deep [src:kyivindependent-2023-terajima-dnipro-hopeless]. A Russian milblogger claimed 10 km² on 16 November 2023 [src:isw-2023-11-17-roca].
  - The M-14, 5–7 km inland, was never reached [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-krynky-untold].
- **The withdrawal.** By mid-July 2024 the village is lost, and fighting moves to the islands and to positions north of Krynky [src:slidstvo-2024-stanko-krynky-hell] [src:kyivindependent-2024-hodunova-krynky-new-positions].
- **Ukrainian losses (contested).**
  - Police data: 788 missing and 262 dead recovered and buried, October 2023 to end of June 2024 [src:slidstvo-2024-stanko-krynky-hell] [src:euromaidan-2024-martyniuk-krynky-missing].
  - "More than 1,000" feared killed [src:telegraph-2024-barnes-krynky-1000].
  - UALosses, as of 21 June 2026: 306 named killed, 730 missing and 54 or 64 captured. The article gives both figures [src:wikipedia-battle-of-krynky] [src:ualosses-2026-soldiers].
  - One marine brigade lost about 700 dead and wounded [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-krynky-untold].
- **Russian losses (Ukrainian claims).**

1. **Launching the air bridge (Mar).** Budanov (GUR) devised a plan that a US aviation veteran called work for highly proficient crews only. Several pilots opted out once read in [src:time-2024-spencer-collins-mariupol-helicopters] [src:twz-2022-altman-flint-helicopter-rescue]. Each flight needed the ground commander's final "all clear" (Prokopenko) [src:time-2024-spencer-collins-mariupol-helicopters]. After the seventh mission GUR judged further flights too risky [src:time-2024-spencer-collins-mariupol-helicopters]. Hromov said deliveries stopped once news of them spread and Russia strengthened its air defences [src:twz-2022-altman-mariupol-helicopter-missions].
2. **Flight-level choices** (sources describe these as real dilemmas):
   - payload against defensive guns (the guns were removed);
   - re-routing around updated air-defence positions, while keeping the supporting artillery in sync;
   - extra minutes on the ground to load every wounded man, at a cost in fuel;
   - the "single-ship mission" rule, under which no one turns back to save a downed partner.
   [src:time-2024-spencer-collins-mariupol-helicopters]
3. **The breakout from Illich (11–12 Apr).** The 36th Marine Brigade split: one group went north to break the ring, the other went to link up with Azov. Prokopenko later called Baraniuk's breakout "uncoordinated" [src:wikipedia-siege-of-mariupol]. ISW and Ukrainian officials confirmed that the link-up succeeded in part [src:isw-2022-04-13-roca] [src:isw-2022-04-14-roca].
4. **Russia: storm or starve (21 Apr – 4 May).** Putin halted the assaults to limit casualties [src:isw-2022-04-21-roca]. Ground attacks resumed on 25 Apr and became a full storm on 3–4 May, which ISW linked to the 9 May Victory Day deadline [src:isw-2022-04-25-roca] [src:isw-2022-05-04-roca].
5. **Civilian evacuation deals (late Apr – 7 May).** The UN/ICRC safe passage was agreed after Guterres visited Moscow and Kyiv [src:un-ukraine-2022-05-03-lubrani-azovstal]. Russia had first refused any pause until the defenders surrendered [src:isw-2022-04-22-roca].
6. **Relief, breakout or "extraction" (Apr – May).**
   - **Relief.** Defenders asked for an offensive towards them [src:twz-2022-altman-mariupol-helicopter-missions]. Hromov and Maliar ruled out unblocking: 150–200 km of fortified ground and heavy losses [src:militarnyi-2022-kushnikov-unblocking-mariupol] [src:defenceua-2022-mariupol-garrison-mission].
   - **Extraction.** Volynskyi appealed to world leaders for a "Dunkirk" [src:wikipedia-serhii-volynskyi]. Turkey offered to carry the defenders by ship from Berdiansk and intern them until the war's end. Russia would release only civilians [src:lb-2022-erdogan-azovstal-offer]. Ukraine separately proposed swapping the seriously wounded for Russian prisoners [src:lb-2022-erdogan-azovstal-offer].
   - **Breakout.** No source examined describes a planned breakout from Azovstal itself. Russian claims of captured "escapees" (6 May) are unconfirmed [src:isw-2022-05-06-roca].
7. **The order of 16 May.** The Supreme Military Command ordered the unit commanders to save their men. Ukraine framed it as an "evacuation" with later exchange; Russia called it a surrender [src:defenceua-2022-mariupol-garrison-mission] [src:pravda-2022-ru-mod-959-left-azovstal]. ISW judged that the Kremlin might have agreed to a conditional surrender to speed up its claim of control, and warned that it might refuse exchanges [src:isw-2022-05-17-roca].
8. **Exchanges (Sep 2022 onward).** The five commanders were freed on condition they stay in Turkey under Erdoğan's guarantees [src:pravda-2022-swap-215-medvedchuk]. They returned with Zelensky on 8 Jul 2023 [src:wikipedia-serhii-volynskyi]. The slow return of Azov fighters remained contested in 2025: Prokopenko called a swap without Azov fighters "a disgrace" [src:kyivpost-2025-pehlman-azovstal-half-home] [src:rferl-2025-peretiatko-azovstal-captivity].
## 4. Key-figures table

1. **Pavlivka in the mud (late Oct – mid-Nov 2022).** Two marine brigades attack a village across the Kashlahach in rain and mud. They take it street by street and lose half their equipment in four days. The episode ends with their men's public letter of protest [src:isw-2022-11-03-roca] [src:isw-2022-11-07-roca].
2. **The SOF ambush (3 Feb 2023).** Two 155th tanks move up to firing positions. The lead T-80 hits a mine and burns, and SOF and the 72nd capture two crew [src:pravda-2023-sof-ambush-t80].
3. **Black Monday (6 Feb 2023).** A daylong assault by about two battalions under exhaust smoke, led by a plow tank, drives into the minefields. Artillery fires into the smoke, about 30 vehicles are left behind, and the Alga battalion is mauled [src:forbes-2023-axe-vuhledar-halt] [src:rferl-2023-eckel-what-happened-vuhledar].
4. **"The second one went exactly the same route" (filmed early Feb).** In a video published by Ukrainian marines, artillerymen comment as one column blows up and a second follows the same path [src:politico-2023-melkozerova-155th-brigade]. This is the signature shot. In the filmed engagement that ISW counted, 13 tanks and 12 BMPs were lost [src:isw-2023-02-09-roca].
5. **The RAAM corridor.** A plow tank clears a lane, and minutes later 155 mm shells scatter magnetic mines back into it. The followers are trapped between old and new mines [src:forbes-2023-axe-minefield-raam] [src:novayagazeta-2023-ukmod-raam].
6. **HIMARS on a column.** Guided rockets, normally used against depots, strike a stalled column [src:nyt-2023-kramer-epic-tank-battle]. In a related strike reported on 13 Feb, HIMARS hit the Vostok battalion's headquarters [src:isw-2023-02-13-roca].
7. **The Wanderer.** In the grey pre-dawn, a Ukrainian T-64 crew says a prayer and drives out against a column of 16 Russian tanks and armoured vehicles. It stops about three miles short of the ambush site and fires on coordinates from a drone pilot as the column stalls on mines [src:nyt-2023-kramer-epic-tank-battle].
8. **The officer's notebook (1–5 Mar 2023).** An infantry-phase coda: one assault group's daily tallies of 100, 116, 103 and 115 men sent and 16, 23, 15 and 3 back [src:forbes-2023-axe-diary-1100].

1. **The 14-day walk** (July 2025). Three groups of about 50 men move from Selydove to the Pishchane industrial zone, then creep about 600 m a day towards Zakhysnykiv Ukrainy Street. Drones drop their water and food, and cloaks hide them from thermal cameras. About 120 die from drone drops, and some 30 reach the city [src:nv-2025-horova-deepstate-150-saboteurs]. The player's drone line sees some groups and misses others.
2. **"The brigade ran out of infantry."** On 21 July DeepState reports that Russians walked in through Zvirove because one brigade had no infantry left and positions were misreported. The 155th and 68th brigades have to plug the hole [src:pravda-2025-up-russians-entered-pokrovsk].
3. **The Dobropillia "rabbit ears"** (11–17 August). A 15 km wedge appears on the map in five days. DeepState and the General Staff publicly disagree about it [src:euromaidanpress-2025-zoria-deepstate-wedge] [src:pravda-2025-shumilin-military-deny-breakthrough]. The Azov Corps arrives, and the 93rd Brigade's tanks and gun robots clear Zolotyi Kolodiaz, Hruzke and Vesele [src:kyivindependent-2025-farrell-dobropillia-lessons] [src:euromaidanpress-2025-axe-armed-robots].
4. **The Kucheriv Yar pocket** (22 October). The 132nd Reconnaissance Battalion retakes the village and captures more than 50 Russians, and civilians are found in basements [src:pravda-2025-romanenko-kucheriv-yar] [src:euromaidanpress-2025-murdoch-kucheriv-yar].
5. **The railway station** (about 20 October). An infiltration team reaches the centre, kills civilians and is destroyed inside a station building [src:rbc-2025-sabotage-team-railway-station].
6. **The flag on the entrance sign** (29 October, 09:40–10:40). A Russian flag goes up on the western entrance sign by the Pavlohrad highway and is destroyed within an hour [src:pravda-2025-pohorilov-flag-destroyed].

HUR special forces land by helicopter in the northern part of the city, in an operation overseen by Budanov, to hold the corridor out [src:reuters-2025-dysa-balmforth-special-forces-pokrovsk]. 9. **The road into Myrnohrad** (November – January). A single road, 1–3 km of corridor, Rubikon FPVs overhead. **Reading the table.**
- Huliaipole E is the clean reference grid. OSM and Sentinel-2 agree within 1% on the 550 m main-belt spacing, and the imagery shows cross-belts about 1.1–1.3 km apart. That gives **blocks of about 0.55 × 1.2 km**, split into 40–50 ha crop fields.
- Robotyne is the same pattern rotated about 10°, with main belts at about 0.5–0.6 km and cross-belts at 1.0–1.2 km.
- East of Kupiansk the forest-steppe fields are larger and less regular, and wooded balkas cut across them.
- South of Chasiv Yar the ground is dissected, with large woods and fragmented fields.

4 Jun – 30 Nov 2023 (shaping and first breach 4–12 Jun; attrition June–July; second mechanized push 26 Jul; Robotyne taken 22–28 Aug; Verbove breach 20–25 Sep; positional end-state November), the Orikhiv–Robotyne–Tokmak axis, Polohy raion, western Zaporizhzhia Oblast.
