## 7. Terms

- **Victory before the end.** Putin and Shoigu declared victory on 21 Apr while the plant still held. Putin framed the halt to assaults as a way to limit Russian casualties [src:isw-2022-04-21-roca]. ISW read the Kremlin as setting up a claim of control by 9 May, with propagandists brought into the city [src:isw-2022-05-04-roca].
- **Inflated numbers.** Shoigu claimed more than 8,000 Ukrainian troops at the time of encirclement [src:wikipedia-siege-of-mariupol], 1,026 marines surrendered at Illich [src:isw-2022-04-13-roca], and 2,439 surrendered at Azovstal [src:pravda-2022-mazurenko-2439-shoigu]. ISW suggested Russia might overstate the totals, either to maximise exchange leverage or to avoid admitting a months-long siege against only "hundreds" [src:isw-2022-05-20-roca].
- **Framing.** Russia presented evacuated civilians as "hostages" freed [src:isw-2022-05-02-roca]. It said a downed helicopter had been sent to evacuate Azov commanders [src:wikipedia-siege-of-mariupol]. Volodin said the defenders must be tried for war crimes and not exchanged [src:isw-2022-05-17-roca].
- **Domestic reaction.** Pro-Russian channels were angry about the negotiated deal [src:isw-2022-05-17-roca] and complained that Russian wounded were moved out of DNR hospitals for Ukrainian ones [src:isw-2022-05-19-roca].
- **Aftermath.** Pushilin announced that Azovstal would be demolished and Mariupol made a "resort city" [src:isw-2022-05-18-roca]. Russia blamed Olenivka on HIMARS, which the UN rejected [src:kyivpost-2023-afp-olenivka-not-himars]. Russian courts sentenced 12 Azov members to 13–23 years in March 2025 [src:rferl-2025-peretiatko-azovstal-captivity].
- **Russian losses.** Paly, deputy commander of the Black Sea Fleet, was confirmed killed [src:isw-2022-03-20-roca]. A Ukrainian claim names the 150th MRD commander, Maj Gen Mityaev, as killed [src:wikipedia-siege-of-mariupol].

**Russia (VKS)**
- **A-50/A-50U Mainstay.** Il-76-based, with the Shmel radar. Militarnyi gives detection of aircraft "up to 700 km", air-defence systems at 400 km and armour at 450 km, a crew of 15–16, and a home base at Ivanovo-Severny with the 610th Centre for Combat Use and Retraining [src:militarnyi-2024-a50-lost-eyes]. Ukrainska Pravda gives a crew of 19 (5 pilots, 11 radio engineers, 3 technical engineers) [src:pravda-2024-balachuk-a50-azov]. For fleet size see §1. Known A-50U board numbers include RF-92957, RF-50602, RF-94268, RF-93952 and RF-50610 [src:militarnyi-2024-a50-lost-eyes]. The lost aircraft were RF-93966 "Sergey Atayants" (14 Jan) [src:militarnyi-2024-a50-lost-eyes] and, by ASN's search listing, RF-50610 "42 Red" (23 Feb) [src:asn-2024-a50u-rf50610].
- **Il-22M11 (Il-20M family) airborne command post and radio relay.** Fewer than a dozen in service [src:theaviationist-2024-cenciotti-a50-il22]. One was damaged, RF-95678 [src:wikipedia-2024-a50-il22-shootdowns]. In the Russian C2 chain the Il-20M relays the picture from command posts to fighters and SAMs [src:rusi-2022-bronk-russian-air-war].
- **Strike and escort aircraft.**
  - **Su-34 and Su-35S** fly glide-bomb runs and CAPs from bases such as Millerovo [src:pravda-2024-petrenko-a50-five-aircraft], and Su-30 crews fly over the Azov [src:twz-2024-altman-rogoway-a50-claims].
  - **Su-34 losses:** Oryx confirms 42 Su-34s lost over the war [src:oryx-russian-equipment-losses].
  - **The ground layer:** S-400s in Crimea and Belarus [src:rusi-2022-bronk-russian-air-war] and, by Russian claims, near Mariupol [src:militarnyi-2024-kushnikov-second-a50].
- **Industrial base.** The Beriev TANTK plant at Taganrog, 150–160 km from the front, is the only plant that repairs and modernises A-50s [src:armada-2025-oliver-berievs] [src:euromaidanpress-2025-mukhina-taganrog-a50]. The A-100 successor had still not entered production in 2026 [src:theaviationist-2026-satam-new-a50u].

**The Irpin line.**
- *The river:* "only ten to twenty meters wide in many places", hard to ford and easy to pontoon. Irrigation ditches keep vehicles on roads and bridges [src:mwi-2025-collins-spencer-battle-of-kyiv].
- *The only vehicle crossings, clockwise:* four-lane E40 at Stoianka; two-lane P30 south of Irpin; four-lane E373 between Bucha and Horenka; two-lane P02 south of Demydiv, 3 km above the dam; two single-lane track bridges at Moshchun and Chervone [src:mwi-2025-collins-spencer-battle-of-kyiv]. OSM puts the Moshchun bridge 6.4 km from the E373 bridge, against MWI's "six and a half" [src:osm-2026-c01-kyiv-geodata].
- *Moshchun:* a village of 794 people (MWI) or about 1,500 (WaPo), "ringed by a pine forest, a river and a lake", with WWII pillboxes in the woods [src:mwi-2025-collins-spencer-battle-of-kyiv] [src:wapo-2022-sonne-battle-for-kyiv].
- *The suburbs:* Irpin had 70,000 people, Bucha 37,000 and Hostomel 17,000 [src:mwi-2025-collins-spencer-battle-of-kyiv]. The Bucha River separates Bucha and Irpin, and its last bridge was on Vokzalna Street [src:mwi-2025-collins-spencer-battle-of-kyiv].

- `dw-2025-shepeleva-is-ukraine-losing`: "Krasnoarmeysk" claim. Lykhovyi: north along the railway held as of 3 Dec. DeepState (Pohorilyi, Mykula) on Myrnohrad. Reisner: "the city has already fallen".
- `interfax-2016-rada-renames`: Dymytrov became Myrnohrad and Krasnoarmiysk became Pokrovsk (Resolution No. 4468).
- `euromaidanpress-2025-axe-reinforce-pokrovsk`: Reserve dilemma: Azov Corps mopping up the 40 km² Dobropillia salient vs Huliaipole; 68th and 155th began retreating north in late October; ISW: Russia very likely to seize both towns. Analysis.
**The outcome the player must reproduce**

- **Act 1 (8 Oct 2022).** A truck carrying a concealed charge exploded at 06:07 on the Crimea-bound road lanes. It dropped road spans into the strait and set fire to fuel tank cars of a freight train on the rail bridge alongside [src:wikipedia-2022-crimean-bridge-explosion; isw-2022-10-08-roca]. The SBU was named by Ukrainian sources the same morning [src:pravda-2022-sbu-behind-bridge], and confirmed it in July and August 2023 [src:euromaidan-2023-shandra-sbu-confirms; militarnyi-2023-kushnikov-malyuk-details]. Two days later Putin called the 10 Oct missile and drone strike on Ukrainian energy and cities retaliation for the bridge [src:isw-2022-10-10-roca].
- **Act 2 (17 Jul 2023).** Two SBU "Sea Baby" surface drones, in a joint operation with the Navy, struck the bridge at night. One road span collapsed and an adjacent span was knocked loose [src:cnn-2023-walsh-sea-baby; isw-2023-07-17-roca].
- **Between Acts 2 and 3.** Russia surrounded the bridge with sunken ferries, barge lines, booms, nets, "hedgehogs", smoke and patrol craft. Storms broke the barrier more than once [src:twz-2023-altman-sinks-ships; navalnews-2024-sutton-kerch-defenses; espreso-2023-storm-barrier; unn-2025-bridge-protection-restored].
- **Act 3 (3 Jun 2025).** The SBU set off charges that its agents had placed at the underwater supports over several months. It went under the barrier rather than through it [src:pravda-2025-prots-third-strike].
- **Coda (2026).** The bridge still stands, but it carries no heavy trucks, and the Kerch Strait ferries that replaced it for dangerous cargo have been struck out of service [src:rusi-2026-ferris-logistics-targeting; kyivindependent-2026-pakhnyuk-ferry-75].
## 2. Timeline

**Mines.**
- **Two kinds.** There were deliberate TM-62 belts, and RAAM shells fired onto corridors Russian mine plows had just cleared, "filling up the cleared corridor" according to a moderator of the pro-Russian forum Lost Armour [src:forbes-2023-axe-minefield-raam].
- **UK MoD.** Ukraine's successful use of RAAM was the reason behind the heavy losses, as Novaya Gazeta Europe relays the update. It was sometimes fired over and behind advancing units, to trap them on withdrawal [src:novayagazeta-2023-ukmod-raam].
- **Surprise.** Kyiv Post called artillery-delivered mines a tactical surprise and the first large-scale use in the war [src:kyivpost-2023-korshak-vuhledar-marines].
- **Typical footage.** One vehicle detonates a mine and the next drives past without slowing, only to hit another [src:kyivpost-2023-korshak-vuhledar-marines] [src:cnn-2023-lister-vuhledar-turkeys].
- **Training.** A captured marine said the mobilised men could not identify minefields or react to them [src:isw-2023-02-13-roca]. A tank milblogger blamed rushed mine clearing [src:isw-2023-03-15-roca].

**Footprint.** The diorama is a box of about 13 × 10 km. It runs from Prechystivka in the west to Mykilske and Vodiane in the east, and from Yehorivka in the south to Bohoiavlenka in the north. Most of the 2022–23 fighting sits within about 6 km of the town; only the flank attacks towards Prechystivka and Bohoiavlenka reach further [src:isw-2023-02-10-roca]. ISW measured Russia's best effort as falling short of a 4 km advance [src:isw-2023-03-05-roca].

- **e1:** A pre-war professional army of BTGs with contract soldiers, VDV spearheads and huge artillery parks (2,433 barrel systems and 3,547 MLRS). It planned a 10-day campaign. Logistics and C2 failed, and the force was too small for the frontage [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons] [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].
- **e2:** Russia reverted to what it does well: rail-fed massed artillery, a 10:1 fire advantage and slow city-by-city advances. Volunteers took the brunt of Russian dead from mid-2022 [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons] [src:mediazona-2026-casualties-count].
- **e3:** After Kharkiv exposed the manpower shortage, Russia mobilised 300,000, pulled back behind the Dnipro and began building the Zaporizhzhia lines. It started a war economy from May 2022 [src:wikipedia-2022-russian-mobilization] [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons]. The Iranian Shahed arrived in Aug–Sep 2022 [src:csis-2026-bondar-shahed-geran].
- **e4:** **Wagner and the convict conveyor.**
  - Prisoners were the largest category of named dead by Mar 2023, and 88% of Wagner's Bakhmut dead were convicts [src:mediazona-2026-casualties-count] [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].
  - Trained Wagner troops lost only about 40–60 a week, and convicts were treated as disposable fixing forces [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].
  - The army moved back from BTGs to divisions and regiments, padded with Storm-Z units [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].
- **e5:** A textbook prepared defence. Three belts, regiments rotated to stay fresh, 35 days of cached ammunition, Lancets and helicopters, and early glide bombs [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons]. Wagner mutinied in June 2023 [src:wikipedia-russo-ukrainian-war]; its fate after the mutiny is left to the manpower file.
- **e6:** Industrial-scale glide bombs (about 40k UMPK in 2024). DPRK shells shored up ammunition supply, and Russia's shell advantage was 5:1 or more. Shahed volume grew but early interception rates were high [src:rusi-2025-watling-third-year] [src:wikipedia-north-korean-involvement] [src:wikipedia-battle-of-avdiivka] [src:csis-2026-bondar-shahed-geran].
- **e7:** A **volunteer/contract model** replaces mobilization.
  - Recruitment was 400k+ in 2024, and was expected to keep exceeding losses of 1,200+ casualties a day [src:rusi-2025-watling-third-year]. Bonus structures are left to the manpower file.
  - Volunteers are again the largest category of Russian dead from Sep 2024 [src:mediazona-2026-casualties-count].
  - North Korean troops appear in Kursk, and Russia's armoured-vehicle stocks from storage were running down [src:rusi-2025-watling-third-year].
- **e8:** Drone-centric, infantry-infiltration warfare.
  - Fibre-optic FPVs, 50,000+ Shaheds a year and 70k UMPK ordered [src:rusi-2025-watling-third-year] [src:csis-2026-jones-10-charts].
  - Recruitment met its 403,000 plan (HUR) [src:euromaidan-2025-murdoch-budanov-403k].
  - Up to half of Russia's artillery ammunition may be North Korean (Ukrainian intelligence claim) [src:wikipedia-north-korean-involvement].
  - Migrants and vulnerable groups are coerced into service [src:wikipedia-2022-russian-mobilization].
  - Late in the era, Russian drone units used Starlink to extend mid-range strikes on the Ukrainian rear [src:isw-2026-02-01-roca].
- **e9:**
  - **C2.** The loss of Starlink and throttled Telegram hurt Russian C2 [src:isw-2026-02-12-assessment] [src:united24-2026-litnarovych-starlink].
  - **Summer offensive.** In early February Russia was struggling to seize the start lines for its planned summer 2026 offensive, towards Sloviansk–Kramatorsk and/or Orikhiv–Zaporizhzhia. The southern counterattacks set it back further [src:isw-2026-02-15-roca].
  - **Losses exceed recruitment.** Losses stay at about 32,800 a month (General Staff) while gains shrink to about 290 casualties per km² [src:euromaidan-2026-tril-cost-per-km]. Syrskyi and the unmanned-systems commander Brovdi say losses now outrun recruitment [src:kyivindependent-2026-farrell-syrskyi-march].
  - **"Beautiful reports."** ISW and Russian milbloggers describe a culture of inflated reports that misleads Putin and set up Vivaldi's surprise [src:isw-2026-09-06-roca] [src:isw-2026-09-26-assessment].
  - **Strike arsenal.** It moves to jet Gerans (Geran-4/5), with ballistic missiles aimed at the Patriot gap [src:militarnyi-2026-jet-geran-interceptors] [src:csis-2026-bondar-shahed-geran] [src:isw-2026-09-26-assessment].
  - **Conscription** becomes year-round [src:wikipedia-2022-russian-mobilization].
  - **Oil revenue.** The Iran war's oil spike cushions Russia's budget [src:kyivpost-2026-struck-feshchenko-oil-windfall].

## 5. Russia's side as reported

- **Concern, then blame.** From 18 October 2023 one prominent milblogger led alarmed reporting of an "offensive across the Dnipro" and accused the MoD of ignoring the threat [src:isw-2023-10-18-roca]. Milbloggers blamed Makarevich for the repeated landings [src:isw-2023-10-29-roca].
- **Putin's framing.** On 18 October Putin called the activity the "next counteroffensive" and a failure [src:isw-2023-10-18-roca]. In December he framed the defence as luring Ukrainians in to attrit them [src:isw-2023-12-16-roca], and said Russian troops had pulled back "several meters" [src:kyivindependent-2023-terajima-dnipro-hopeless].
- **Saldo's denial.** Kherson occupation head Saldo denied the Kozachi Laheri landing, likely to avoid panic [src:isw-2023-08-08-roca].
- **Command failures.** Russian sources reported poor coordination, too few drones, weak artillery support and unevacuated wounded in the 810th Brigade [src:kyivpost-2023-korshak-glide-bombs-krynky]. They also reported desertions from the 144th MRB (a General Staff claim) [src:kyivpost-2023-korshak-marines-dug-in].
  - A pro-Kremlin channel: the Ukrainians "have no chance of expanding the occupied bridgehead" [src:kyivpost-2023-korshak-glide-bombs-krynky].
  - A pro-Russian blogger: "constant attacks by small aircraft (hobby drones)... There are a lot of them" [src:kyivpost-2023-korshak-glide-bombs-krynky].
- **The February claim.** Shoigu claimed that Krynky was cleared and up to 3,500 Ukrainians killed, and called it the end of the 2023 counteroffensive. ISW judged the claim premature and timed for the March election [src:isw-2024-02-20-roca]. Milbloggers accused him of lying to Putin [src:isw-2024-02-21-roca]. A Kremlin claim in March that the whole left bank was cleared angered milbloggers, who called it fake [src:kyivpost-2024-korshak-krynky-retreat].
- **The July claims.** On 17 July Russian sources claimed the Ukrainian withdrawal from Krynky before Ukraine acknowledged it. They also reported small-arms fighting on the Dnipro delta islands [src:isw-2024-07-17-roca].

- **Pier geometry.** The total number of piers, the pier numbering origin, typical span lengths per section (only the 64 m replacement span is sourced) and pier coordinates for supports 145 and 235–236 are not in any source used. A figure of 595 supports appeared only in search snippets and could not be tied to an acceptable source, so it was not used.
- **Barrier dimensions.** Boom heights, net mesh, mine positions and the exact standoff distance from the bridge are unpublished. The spacing of the 2023 block ships is given as 160 m (UK DI), just over 0.1 mi (TWZ) or about 200 m (Militarnyi). Their direction is given as "south" (TWZ, UK DI) or "western approaches" (Sutton's post).
- **Barge counts** swing with storms and reporting: 7 sections (May 2024), 21 in a second line (Jun), 30+ (Jul), 36 (Oct), 17 (Jan 2025). No clean time series.
- **Act 1 charge.** The SBU says 21 t TNT equivalent of RDX; the Russian case file says about 10 t TNT equivalent of rocket fuel in 22.7 t of cargo. Spans down: 2 (case file) or 3 damaged with 2 down (Wikipedia). The explosion site is described three ways (§3).
- **Act 2 launch point, route, range and endurance** of the Sea Babies are not disclosed. Neither is whether the CNN "road" and "rail" impacts struck the same pier group.
- **Act 3 damage** is not independently verified. Reuters confirmed only the location [src:reuters-2025-polityuk-underwater]. The delivery method (divers, UUV, agents) is unknown, and Malyuk's "two × 1,100 kg" adds to the initial "1,100 kg".
- **Unverified Russian claims:** whether the Aug–Sep 2023 and Aug 2024 attacks on the bridge happened as Russia described them.
- **Not researched (search budget exhausted):**
  - the 2024 German Taurus debate over the bridge;
  - Russian rail-bridge load limits after 2022;
  - the Ukrainian Navy's role in planning Act 3;
  - the UK MoD's original wording on repair estimates (cited here via Wikipedia).
- **Weather** comes from ERA5 reanalysis, not station observations, and gives no sea state or visibility.

- **The pincer, October.** At dawn on 10 October 2023 Russia opened the offensive with what Ukrainian soldiers called its strongest fire preparation in Donbas of the war. Armoured assault groups attacked the northern flank (Krasnohorivka–Stepove–Berdychi, towards the coke plant) and the southern flank (Sieverne, Vodiane–Opytne) to encircle the garrison [src:osw-2023-ber-battle-avdiivka-day-596] [src:isw-2023-10-11-roca]. A second wave followed on 19–20 October. Russia lost at least 109 vehicles to satellite count in the first ten days [src:frontelligence-2023-avdiivka-losses]. ISW judged these losses larger than those at Vuhledar [src:isw-2023-10-26-roca].
- **The grind, November–January.** Russia switched to dismounted infantry assaults [src:isw-2023-11-04-roca]. It took the waste heap (terrikon) north of the city in late October [src:lwj-2024-hardie-avdiivka-analysis] [src:wikipedia-battle-of-avdiivka] and the fortified southeastern industrial zone ("promka") between mid-November and early December [src:isw-2023-11-14-roca] [src:wikipedia-battle-of-avdiivka]. The coke plant held [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-last-days-avdiivka].
- **The two breaches.** About 15 January Russian troops came up a service-water pipe behind the "Tsarska Okhota" strongpoint in the south. In early February they infiltrated through the northern dachas between the quarry and the lakes, bypassing the coke plant [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-last-days-avdiivka] [src:lwj-2024-hardie-avdiivka-analysis].
- **The neck closes.** On 12–14 February the Russians reached Industrialnyi Avenue and cut the city in two, with the coke plant to the north and the centre to the south. The main supply road through Lastochkyne was lost [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-last-days-avdiivka].
- **Air and ammunition.** Glide bombs fell at 30–50 a day by early February (UK MoD) and about 60 a day by mid-February (Ukrainian units) [src:wikipedia-battle-of-avdiivka] [src:isw-2024-02-17-assessment]. Ukrainian guns were starved by the stalled US supplemental [src:bbc-2024-lukiv-us-warns-avdiivka] [src:liga-2025-shell-ratio].
- **The last reserve.** The 3rd Assault Brigade was rushed in, and the exhausted 110th Mechanised Brigade began to rotate out [src:kyivindependent-2024-khalilova-reinforcing-avdiivka] [src:lwj-2024-hardie-avdiivka-analysis].
- **The withdrawal.** Zenit, the southern bastion, was abandoned on 14–15 February. On the night of 16–17 February the new commander-in-chief, Oleksandr Syrskyi, announced the withdrawal "to avoid encirclement" [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-last-days-avdiivka] [src:isw-2024-02-16-roca]. It was completed on 17 February [src:pravda-2024-lykhovii-tavria-losses].

**Wagner's strength.**
- **Two tiers.** Professionals wore "M" tags. Convicts wore "K" tags numbered by colony, hence "Kashniki" [src:mediazona-2024-price-of-bakhmut].
- **Estimates of size:**
  - US, January 2023: about 50,000 in Ukraine, of whom 10,000 were contractors and 40,000 convicts [src:guardian-2023-kirby-wagner-tco].
  - Prigozhin, May 2023: 35,000 men plus 50,000 convicts [src:euromaidan-2023-prigozhin-video-losses].
  - Mediazona: at least 48,000 convicts recruited, the last on 7 Feb 2023 [src:mediazona-2024-price-of-bakhmut].
- **Casualty estimates:**
  - White House, 17 Feb 2023: more than 30,000 casualties, about 9,000 of them killed. About 90% of those killed since December were convicts [src:reuters-2023-shalal-wagner-30000-casualties].
- **Frontage.** Prigozhin said Wagner's front shrank from 85 km to under 5 km [src:euromaidan-2023-prigozhin-video-losses].

- FPV — first-person-view drone, flown via goggles; usually a one-way strike drone.
- Dropper / bomber — a multirotor that drops munitions (e.g., Vampire, Baba Yaga) rather than diving in.
- Loitering munition — a drone munition that searches before striking (e.g., Lancet, Shahed-type).
- Shahed — Iranian-designed long-range one-way attack drone used by Russia; the target of interceptor sims.
- EW — electronic warfare: jamming, spoofing, direction finding.
- RSSI/LQ — received signal strength / link quality; the drone-link health measures used in the Arma mod.
- Kill zone — the ~10+ km band near the front where drones make vehicle movement lethal.
- ISR — intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance.
- ADB / ePoints — Army of Drones Bonus, a points-for-verified-strikes programme.
- DELTA — Ukraine's situational-awareness system; strike videos are verified there.
- Brave1 Market — Ukrainian defence marketplace where units spend ePoints.
- WeGo — simultaneous-turn system (Combat Mission) where both sides plot, then execute together.
- OOB — order of battle.
- CPX — command post exercise; staff training driven by a simulation.
- Matrix game — argument-based adjudicated wargame, common in professional gaming.
- KShVI — Russian command-staff military games (procedural rehearsal).
- P500 — GMT's preorder system; a game goes to print after 500 orders.
- PvPvE — players fight each other and AI at the same time.
- Double-blind — neither side sees the other's forces except through reports.
- Goodhart's law — when a measure becomes a target, it stops measuring what matters.
- Sense-and-strike complex (recon-strike complex) — the linked sensors, C2 and fires that find and hit targets within minutes; the thing Canadian games found hardest to break.
- Loitering ammunition — Broken Arrow's term for its planned one-way attack munitions (missiles with man-in-the-loop or AI terminal guidance).
- Chaika / Chaika-M ("Seagull" / "Flyswatter") — Ukrainian VR air-defence simulators codified by the MoD in 2025.
- RTCA — "real-time command action", Hell Of War's label for a command-drone view with drop-in direct control.
- SOP — standard operating procedure; in Flashpoint Campaigns, standing rules that units follow between orders.

- **CSIS wargames on Russia–Ukraine or NATO–Russia**: not found. csis.org returns 403. The archived Futures Lab page lists Ukraine analysis (an energy-truce piece) but no Russia–Ukraine wargame, and PAXsims only references CSIS's Taiwan games. The NATO–Russia games that were found are German, British and Canadian (§5).
- **Dstl on Ukraine drone lessons**: the gov.uk search API found only the Dstl–Slitherine case study, the Defence Wargaming Centre pages and a strategic-communications game (Defending Defender). No Ukraine drone game was public.
- **Commercial FPV sims in Ukrainian schools**: no first-party source names Liftoff, VelociDrone, Uncrashed or DCL. Searches of Euromaidan Press's archive for each name found nothing. Only the vendor claim [src:vgi9-2025-drone-simulators] remains, and the verified military sims are all domestic.
- **Combat Mission: Black Sea community mods** for FPV or 2022 content: the Battlefront forums returned 403. Official content was checked via the Steam news API, and none has shipped [src:steam-2023-cmbs-update-2-18].
- **Developer countries still unverified**: Sand Table Software (the store page and the studio site give none), Bird's Eye Games (Regiments), Cats Who Play (Gostomel Heroes), Ravens Row (Hell Of War) and Battlestate Games (Escape from Tarkov). Death From Above's makers are confirmed German.
- **ADB values before April 2025** beyond the infantry price, and the exact date of the 6→12 repricing, which falls between April 2025 and January 2026.
- Why *Gostomel Heroes* is missing from the Ukrainian and German Steam stores (regional withdrawal, rating or developer choice) is not established.
- The *Play for Ukraine* full text (Taylor & Francis) returns 403. Only its abstract and metadata were read.
## 11. Sources

- **Standards family.** NATO APP-6 (STANAG 2019) and US MIL-STD-2525 are aligned standards. APP-6A (1999) is equivalent to MIL-STD-2525A. Later editions are APP-6B (2008) and APP-6C (2011), and APP-6E is listed as current [src:wikipedia-nato-joint-military-symbology]. milsymbol supports MIL-STD-2525C/D/E, FM 1-02.2 and APP-6 B/D/E [src:github-milsymbol].
- **Affiliation is encoded twice, by frame shape and by colour** [src:wikipedia-nato-joint-military-symbology]:
  - **Friend:** rectangle, **blue**
  - **Hostile:** diamond, **red**
  - **Neutral:** square, **green**
  - **Unknown:** quatrefoil, **yellow**
  - Further states: pending, assumed friend, suspect, and exercise variants.
  - Because the shape carries affiliation too, symbols work in monochrome.
- **Frame modifiers** [src:wikipedia-nato-joint-military-symbology]:
  - Solid frame = present; **dashed frame = planned/anticipated**.
  - Closed frames = land and sea surface; bottom-open = air/space; top-open = subsurface.
- **Symbol anatomy** [src:wikipedia-nato-joint-military-symbology] [src:spatialillusions-battle-staff-tools]:
  - Frame, central icon, optional fill.
  - Modifiers/amplifiers arranged around the frame: unique designation, additional information, altitude/depth, combat effectiveness, headquarters/task force/dummy, echelon/mobility.
- **Echelons.** Coded in the SIDC and drawn above the frame: Team/Crew, Squad, Section, Platoon/detachment, Company/battery/troop, Battalion/squadron, Regiment/group, Brigade, Division, Corps, Army, Army Group/front, Region/Theatre, Command [src:github-milsymbol].
- **SIDC formats.** Older standards use letter-based symbol identification codes, 15 characters in the APP-6A lineage [src:wikipedia-nato-joint-military-symbology]. Current 2525D/E and APP-6D/E use numeric codes; milsymbol's README example is a 30-digit SIDC. milsymbol implements both schemes [src:github-milsymbol].
- **Renderers:**
  - **milsymbol** (Måns Beckman / spatialillusions):
    - Pure JavaScript, **MIT licence**, SVG or Canvas output.
    - Filled/unfilled and framed/unframed symbols, text fields, movement indicators.
    - Since v3.0 it renders to MIL-STD-2525E/APP-6E appearance for every SIDC version. The latest release is v3.0.4 (March 2026).
    - Integrations include Leaflet, OpenLayers and Cesium [src:github-milsymbol].
    - This is the safe choice for game assets, e.g. pre-render SVGs to a texture atlas at build time.
  - **Spatial Illusions "Battle Staff Tools"** (the "unit generator"):
    - A browser tool for MIL-STD-2525E/APP-6E and 2525C/APP-6B symbols with PNG/SVG export, ORBAT building and a map.
    - © 2025 Måns Beckman. Free on spatialillusions.com with watermarks and donation prompts; offline use or use on other sites needs a paid licence file [src:spatialillusions-battle-staff-tools].
    - Treat its exports as **not** cleared for redistribution in a game.
- **Who follows NATO conventions:**
  - Black Bird Group explicitly uses the NATO convention "red is the Russian adversary, blue is Ukrainian" [src:blackbirdgroup-map].
  - Delta was "built according to NATO standards" [src:militarnyi-2022-delta-unveiled].
  - DeepState does not use APP-6 frames [src:deepstate-api-history].
# The Brovary ambush (vignette)
## 10. Game/sim relevance
### e9-counteroffensive-26 (Feb 2026–present)

- **Hostomel.** The Russian MoD claimed the capture involved some 200 helicopters and killed about 200 Ukrainians, with no Russian losses. The claim was met with scepticism [src:wikipedia-2026-battle-of-antonov-airport]. A Ka-52 pilot told Russian TV: "In the first attack, we immediately lost the leader of our group" [src:wapo-2022-sonne-battle-for-kyiv]. A captured paratrooper said of the 26 Feb barrage: "Almost nobody survived that day" [src:moscowtimes-2022-beardsworth-31st-brigade].
- **The plan.** A captured 1st Guards Tank Army synchronisation matrix expected the "blocking and destruction of individual scattered units" by D+10 [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons]. Planners assumed Ukraine could generate only about 40,000 more troops [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons].
- **The turn.**
  - Kremlin-run media claimed paratroopers crossed the Irpin on 16 Mar; ISW judged it likely false [src:isw-2022-03-16-roca].
  - Rudskoi, 25 Mar: "the main tasks of the first stage of the operation" are complete and the "main goal" is Donbas [src:isw-2022-03-25-roca].
  - Medinsky, 29 Mar: two "de-escalatory steps", including drastically reducing activity towards Kyiv and Chernihiv [src:euromaidan-2022-day-35-kyiv-attacks].
  - Russia presented the drawdown as a goodwill gesture [src:aljazeera-2022-kyiv-region-retaken].
- **Bucha.** Lavrov called it "staged". The MoD claimed the bodies were "moving" and that the mass grave held victims of Ukrainian strikes [src:wikipedia-2026-bucha-massacre]. Satellite imagery from 19 Mar contradicts the claims [src:bbc-2022-bucha-satellite-image]. Putin honoured the 64th Brigade on 18 Apr 2022 [src:rferl-2022-krutov-64th-brigade].
- **Losses as seen from Russia.** The Kostroma VK memorial pages for the 331st Regiment said "The 331st regiment is disappearing" [src:bbc-2022-urban-331st-regiment]. Leaked hospital data show 898 servicemen treated in Gomel and Khoiniki after the march on Kyiv (an RFE/RL investigation, relayed) [src:pravda-2025-kizilov-898-wounded-belarus].
- **Hindsight.** Putin (June 2024): "There was no political decision to storm the three-million-strong city" [src:pravda-2024-kizilov-putin-no-storm].
## 10. Game/sim relevance

- **Artillery, HIMARS and glide bombs in Vivaldi and the southern counteroffensive.** No source quantifies them. Vivaldi was run under "maximum information silence", and the ISW special report and daily assessments (read via Wayback) describe drone-led shaping fires, not tube fire. A later RUSI fieldwork report is the likeliest source.
- **Per-town KAB counts.** Avdiivka (February 2024) is sourced. Vovchansk has only qualitative reporting, and Kharkiv city only a strike count (more than 50 by mid-June 2024). ISW assessments from May–June 2024 via Wayback had no per-town numbers.
- **KAB monthly series gaps.** February 2026 is derived (March minus "more than 1,500"). Most 2024 and 2025 months are missing; only April–May 2024, early 2025, October and November 2025 are sourced. A full Air Force/MoD series was not found in English.
- **Artillery's share of casualties.** Only the complement is sourced: drones cause 70–80% (Latvian SAB), and more than 80% of targets destroyed (UA MoD). No source splits the remaining 20–30% between artillery, glide bombs, mines and small arms.
- **Conflicting production figures.** RUSI's 70,000 UMPK ordered for 2025 against HUR's 120,000 planned. Actual drops (~44,000 in Jan–Nov 2025) suggest stockpiling or overstated plans. Flamingo's maker claims (30–210 a month) are contradicted by the strike record (~10 strikes). Sapsan's production is unverified.
- **Czech initiative totals.** Pavel's figures differ between February 2026 (4.4M cumulative, almost 2M in 2025) and May 2026 (just over 3M: 1.5M plus 1.8M). The difference may be calibre scope (122 mm included) or counting method.
- **Interceptor-drone kill share.** Official counts conflict (USF: over 1,200 in May 2026; Sting's maker: over 3,000), and the Air Force stopped publishing Shahed counts from May 2026. Cost per kill is only implied (a ~$2k interceptor against a $20–50k Shahed); file 01 has the detail.
- **Ballistic intercept methodology.** CSIS, the MoD monthly and Air Force per-salvo figures are now all sourced, but none separates PAC-3 from SAMP/T or counts interceptors fired per kill.
## 9. Russia's side as reported

**Peace talks and ceasefires.**
- **Abu Dhabi, second round (4–5 Feb 2026):** a 314-person exchange and no ceasefire. A short energy-strike moratorium was in force at the time [src:isw-2026-02-05-roca].
- **Geneva (17–18 Feb):** talks failed on Donbas [src:kyivindependent-2026-fenbert-300km].
- **Orthodox Easter truce (11–13 Apr 2026):** 32 hours from 16:00 on 11 Apr. The General Staff logged 10,721 Russian violations. Long-range strikes paused for about a day, but artillery, FPVs and assaults did not [src:euromaidanpress-2026-zoria-easter-truce]. Pass 1's figure of 469 violations, taken from Wikipedia, is superseded.
- **Victory Day.** Ukraine declared a unilateral ceasefire from 6 May, which Russia ignored [src:isw-2026-05-06-roca]. Both sides then agreed a **9–11 May** ceasefire with a POW exchange. The Kremlin restated that Ukraine must withdraw from the rest of Donetsk Oblast before any ceasefire [src:isw-2026-05-08-roca]. Limited fighting went on, and Russia used the pause to rotate and resupply [src:isw-2026-05-09-roca].
- **The envoys' visit (5–8 Sep).**
  - Kyiv and Moscow halted long-range strikes on each other's capitals from 5 to 7 Sep.
  - Ukrainian brigades were ordered to hold fire along the front from 5 to 8 Sep, a truce Ukraine proposed and Putin rejected [src:isw-2026-09-05-roca].
  - On 6 Sep Zelensky and Witkoff/Kushner agreed "fundamental principles", including security and economic guarantees, while Putin restated maximalist aims [src:isw-2026-09-06-roca].
  - Sources differ on the outcome: CSMonitor reports that Zelensky rejected the plan's terms [src:csmonitor-2026-weir-peace-talks].
- **"Energy ceasefire" (14 Sep):** Trump announced a mutual halt to energy strikes. Zelensky offered one on condition of reciprocity, and Russia did not respond [src:isw-2026-09-14-roca]. By 25 Sep Putin was signalling a winter strike campaign instead [src:isw-2026-09-26-assessment].
section: 3. Per-era notes / e9-counteroffensive-26 (late Jan 2026 – present, Sep 2026)

markdown:
**The outcome the player must reproduce:**
- **Kupiansk held and cleared, not lost.** About 90% of the town was retaken by December 2025 [src:euromaidan-2026-zoria-kupiansk-pipeline]. The Ukrainian flag went up over the City Council on 12 January 2026, and by late February 2026 99% of the town was under Ukrainian control, with up to 10 buildings still uncleared [src:ukrpravda-2026-kyrylenko-kupiansk-is-yours].
- **Area.** ISW counts 305 km² lost to Russian control in late December 2025 as Ukraine liberated "much of Kupyansk and its surroundings" [src:isw-2026-02-15-roca].
- **The pipeline route closed, and the boat route not closed.** The pipeline was brought "almost fully under control" within the first couple of months, but Ukraine never shut the second route, the boat crossings near Dvorichna, and had to drop a push towards Dvorichna for lack of men [src:ukrpravda-2026-kyrylenko-kupiansk-is-yours]. A Russian bridgehead on the west bank north of Kupiansk still existed in September 2026 [src:isw-2026-09-26-assessment].
- **Losses.** Ukraine claims Russia lost nearly 2,000 soldiers: Khartiia's group killed more than 1,500 and the Kupiansk Tactical Group about 400 [src:ukrpravda-2026-kyrylenko-kupiansk-is-yours]. The Times put the kill ratio at 1:27 in Ukraine's favour (as relayed by [src:ukrpravda-2026-kyrylenko-kupiansk-is-yours]). These are Ukrainian claims.
- **Contested points.**
  - *When the pipeline was cut:* Butusov says Ukrainian forces reached the Oskil and cut the northern supply lines by 21 October 2025, while Khartiia announced the breakthrough to the river on 12 December [src:isw-2025-12-13-roca] [src:isw-2025-12-12-roca].
  - *How many Russians were inside:* about 40 per the Ukrainian military on 21 November [src:wikipedia-2026-kupiansk-offensive]; 100–250 at the start per Ukrainska Pravda's sources [src:ukrpravda-2026-kyrylenko-kupiansk-is-yours]; about 200 encircled per Khartiia on 12 December [src:isw-2025-12-12-roca]; about 500 earlier, with about 100 trapped, per the Achilles regiment [src:defenseexpress-2025-achilles-pipeline-destroyed]; 300 falling to about 50, per a December frontline report [src:euromaidanpress-2025-frontline-kupiansk-pipeline-killzone].
## 6. Set pieces

**Russia (Western Group of Forces, then partly Lapin's command).**
- **Command.**
  - Lt Gen Andrei Sychevoy commanded the western grouping until 26 Aug, then Lt Gen Roman Berdnikov.
  - From about 11 Sep, Col Gen Alexander Lapin (Central MD) took over the western grouping.
  - Western MD commander Zhuravlyov was replaced by Berdnikov, as reported on 3 Oct.
  - [src:isw-2022-09-11-roca; src:isw-2022-10-03-roca]
- **The Izium grouping.**
  - It peaked at 24 BTGs, about 18,000 troops, and had at least halved by August [src:wapo-2022-khurshudyan-inside-counteroffensive]. Syrskyi gives about 9,000 in about 12 BTGs in August [src:wikipedia-2022-kharkiv-counteroffensive]. Other estimates are "more than 10,000" near Izium [src:novayagazeta-2022-fedorov-dual-pushback] and 10,000 per David Axe [src:wikipedia-2022-kharkiv-counteroffensive].
  - Main formations: elements of the 1st Guards Tank Army, namely the 4th Guards Tank Division (not fully reconstituted) and the 2nd Guards MRD, plus the 11th Army Corps and the 64th Motor Rifle Brigade. The 2nd Guards MRD's 1st MRR left fatigue letters dated 30 Aug [src:wikipedia-4th-guards-tank-division; src:wikipedia-2022-kharkiv-counteroffensive; src:isw-2022-09-19-roca].
- **The Balakliia force.** It was commanded by Col Ivan Popov of the 11th Army Corps (Baltic Fleet), from a bunker in a vehicle-repair complex [src:reuters-2022-saito-balakliia-base].
  - Units: the 9th MRR at Hrakove, elements of the 336th Marine Brigade, Luhansk conscripts (one corporal was 64, and some carried Mosin rifles) and the 9th BARS brigade.
  - On 30 Aug it was at 71% strength overall. The 2nd assault battalion had 49 of 240 men and the 9th BARS was at 23%.
  - Its equipment fell from 8 APCs to 3 and from 24 Fagot ATGMs to 4. It had 2 drones left, its only Zoopark counter-battery radar was gone, and two of three jammers were broken.
  - [src:reuters-2022-saito-balakliia-base]
- **Rosgvardia.** SOBR and Rosgvardia units held Balakliia and lost it without coordination or adequate artillery [src:isw-2022-09-08-roca; src:wikipedia-2022-kharkiv-counteroffensive]. Bielieskov describes a single defensive tier north of Balakliia, held mainly by SOBR teams [src:euromaidan-2022-shandra-kharkiv].
- **The Lyman garrison**, late September:
  - BARS-13 and BARS-16 ("Kuban"), DNR and LNR units, the 752nd MRR and rear troops of the 20th CAA, and the 3rd Guards Spetsnaz Brigade [src:wikipedia-2022-lyman-front; src:kyivpost-2022-korshak-lyman-surrounded].
  - Reinforcements came late: the partly mobilised 503rd MRR (58th CAA) at Torske [src:isw-2022-09-30-roca], and 144th MRD elements on the Oskil and at Svatove [src:isw-2022-09-26-roca].
  - Strength was "up to 5,000" encircled [src:wikipedia-2022-kharkiv-counteroffensive], or about 5,500 per Berezovets [src:kyivpost-2022-korshak-lyman-surrounded].
- **Force ratio.** The only explicit figure is the occupation head Ganchev's "8 times" Ukrainian superiority [src:aljazeera-2022-ganchev-eight-times]. It is an interested excuse, not a count.
- **Context.** Bielieskov put Russia at 200,000–250,000 troops on a front of more than 1,300 km, too few for a tiered defence [src:euromaidan-2022-shandra-kharkiv]. Russia held 25,000 [src:wapo-2022-khurshudyan-inside-counteroffensive] to 25–30,000 [src:novayagazeta-2022-fedorov-dual-pushback] on the Dnipro right bank.
- **Change over the window.** The units that had left came back as reinforcements by road and by helicopter on 9 Sep [src:isw-2022-09-09-roca]. LNR units withdrawn from Kharkiv Oblast were sent to Donetsk Oblast rather than to the Oskil [src:isw-2022-09-14-roca]. The LNR 206th Regiment was screening the Valuyki rail line inside Russia [src:isw-2022-09-16-roca].

The Telegram, X and YouTube links come from the fetched articles and from ISW footnotes [src:pravda-2026-romanenko-570-targets][src:pravda-2026-balachuk-17-killed][src:pravda-2026-oliynyk-zelensky-warning][src:isw-2026-07-02-roca][src:euromaidan-2026-tril-kyiv-toll-30].

markdown: ## 8. Media

**Russia.**
- **Strength (contested).**
  - About 50,000 against Kyiv in all (MWI). The Northern Front had about 30,000 from the 29th, 35th and 36th Combined Arms Armies of the Eastern Military District, staged in Belarus on the west bank. The Northeastern Front had about 20,000 from the 41st and 2nd CAAs of the Central MD, on the east bank [src:mwi-2025-collins-spencer-battle-of-kyiv].
  - Pavliuk claims about 70,000 men and 7,000 armoured vehicles came from Belarus alone [src:ukrinform-2023-pavliuk-30-sof].
  - RUSI gives a 12:1 ratio on the Gomel axis [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons].
- **Plan.** Group "V" formed at Gomel for the right bank, and group "O" at Bryansk to encircle from the left bank, both under the Eastern MD command post [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons]. Units moved in administrative column, were told to bypass resistance and expected to switch to stabilisation by D+10 [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons].
- **Command.** Col. Gen. Aleksandr Chaiko, commander of the Eastern MD [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons] [src:isw-2022-03-27-roca].
- **The air assault.** The 31st Guards Air Assault Brigade and the 45th Guards Spetsnaz Brigade flew from Bolshoy Bokov, about 170 km north [src:wotr-2023-collins-kofman-spencer-hostomel]. The 31st likely committed about 2,000 men in 2 BTGs around Kyiv. Mediazona counted 34 of its dead from 25 Feb to 7 Mar, and HUR says up to 50 were killed at Hostomel [src:moscowtimes-2022-beardsworth-31st-brigade]. The airlift on standby was the 76th Guards Air Assault Division at Pskov (18 Il-76) [src:wotr-2023-collins-kofman-spencer-hostomel].
- **VDV and motor rifles on the west bank.**
  - The 76th Division's 234th Regiment, the 56th Air Assault Regiment and the 64th Separate Motor Rifle Brigade at Bucha [src:wikipedia-2026-battle-of-bucha].
  - The 64th (Khabarovsk) deployed about 1,500 and has at least 44 named dead for February–March [src:rferl-2022-krutov-64th-brigade].
  - The 331st Guards Parachute Regiment lost its commander and at least 39 others [src:bbc-2022-urban-331st-regiment].
  - The 106th VDV Division had 2 BTGs withdrawn on 27 Mar (General Staff) [src:isw-2022-03-28-roca].
  - The 37th MRB and 5th Tank Brigade (36th CAA) pushed on Makariv and Yasnohorodka [src:isw-2022-03-09-roca].
  - The 155th and 40th Naval Infantry Brigades came in as replacements by 19 Mar [src:isw-2022-03-19-roca]. Some naval infantry units reportedly lost up to 90% [src:isw-2022-03-20-roca].
  - Rosgvardia OMON/SOBR (Kemerovo) and Chechen units, the latter geolocated at Borodianka [src:wikipedia-2026-battle-of-irpin] [src:isw-2022-03-24-roca].
  - The 165th Artillery Brigade (35th CAA) [src:isw-2022-03-27-roca].
- **The east bank.** The 90th Guards Tank Division (6th and 239th Tank Regiments) with the 2nd and 41st CAAs, against Brovary and Chernihiv [src:isw-2022-03-10-roca] [src:interfax-2022-hur-brovary-zakharov]. The 41st CAA had about 30,000 at Chernihiv [src:wikipedia-2026-siege-of-chernihiv].
- **The convoy.** An estimated 15,000 troops [src:guardian-2022-beaumont-convoy-siege], with fuel tankers, food and ammunition trucks, towed and self-propelled artillery, BMP-3s and tanks [src:guardian-2022-beaumont-convoy-siege] [src:independent-2022-james-convoy-40-miles]. Pavliuk mentions about 2,000 convoy guards [src:ukrinform-2023-pavliuk-30-sof].
- **Changes over the window.**
  - 27 Feb – 2 Mar: a 72-hour pause, then ad hoc groupings of battalions [src:isw-2022-03-02-roca].
  - 2–5 BTGs committed at a time from 9 Mar [src:isw-2022-03-09-roca].
  - Digging in from 19 Mar [src:isw-2022-03-19-roca], and damaged units rotated to Belarus from 27 Mar [src:isw-2022-03-27-roca].
  - Withdrawal behind a screen of the 38th and 37th MRBs and the 5th Tank Brigade from 1 Apr [src:euromaidan-2022-day-38-kyiv-recaptured].
  - By 4–6 Apr the force was "likely a spent force" [src:isw-2022-04-04-roca] [src:isw-2022-04-06-roca].

**Alternatives** (no dossier, but documented):
- **7 Sep 2025.** The record drone night of 2025: 810 drones, 4 ballistic and 9 cruise missiles across Ukraine. The Cabinet of Ministers building was hit for the first time. In Kyiv, Sviatoshynskyi and Darnytskyi were struck and two people were killed [src:wikipedia-kyiv-strikes-2022-present][src:isis-2026-anokhin-shahed-2025]. It is the better choice for a drone-saturation chapter with a working Patriot shield, but it has few missiles and was spread across the whole country.
- **19 Jul 2026.** The record ballistic barrage: 41 missiles, 35 of them ballistic (25 Iskander-M/S-400 and 10 Zircon), fired at Kyiv in under an hour, plus 125 drones. Only 18 missiles were downed. One person was killed [src:euromaidan-2026-murdoch-19-july-ballistic]. It is a pure ballistic-defence puzzle with few drones.

Night, fog and rain reduce drone effectiveness; this is when rotations and infiltration happen. Scale the depth up by era, from about 3 km (2023) to 25+ km (2026). Sources: rusi-2025-watling-tactical-developments, pravda-2026-levytska-magyar-kill-zone.
- **Detection → strike latency as a core stat.**
  - About 3–5 minutes with an organic drone; 20–30 minutes through an HQ; hours to days at operational level (2022–23).
  - Ukrainian digital tools (GIS Arta at 30–45 s, Avengers detection at 2.2 s) shorten the loop.
  - Loss of a C2 bearer (Starlink-cutoff event, EW) lengthens it and can cause friendly fire.
  - 2025–26 figures are thin and not independent. Russia's Glaz/Groza cut its drone-to-artillery loop "from hours to minutes" (CSIS, from Russian developer channels). Euromaidan Press says Delta cut Ukraine's detection-to-strike time "from roughly 20 minutes to a few" (unattributed). RUSI gives slower timings for everything else: 24–48 hours for each of the first three attack phases, and 2–3 hours from UGV rendezvous to medical post [src:csis-2026-bondar-russian-c2] [src:euromaidanpress-2026-hryfon-zakhid] [src:rusi-2025-watling-combined-arms].

**The water.**
- *The dam:* the Kozarovychi dam is 1.4 km long and separates the drained Irpin floodplain from the Kyiv Reservoir, which stood 3 m higher [src:wikipedia-2026-kozarovychi-dam]. The floodplain had been drained in the 1960s [src:guardian-2022-mundy-irpin-hero-river].
- *The flood:* the river would grow from 10–20 m wide into a lake "over four hundred meters wide in some places", and in the end more than 31 billion gallons flowed in [src:mwi-2025-collins-spencer-battle-of-kyiv].
- *Contested area:* more than 2,800 ha [src:wikipedia-2026-kozarovychi-dam] or 13,000 ha [src:guardian-2022-mundy-irpin-hero-river].
- *Contested rise:* 0.5–0.7 m (RUSI) [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons], 1.5–2 m [src:wikipedia-2026-battle-of-moshchun] or 2 m [src:euromaidan-2023-havrylets-battle-of-kyiv-tactics].
- *Demydiv:* about 750 households, roughly 50 of them flooded. The village "never became a front line" [src:nyt-2022-kramer-demydiv-flood].

None was independently verified.
- **Internal criticism.** In 2022 nationalist milbloggers criticised Putin and Medvedev's silence after Medvedev's "red line" threats [src:isw-2022-10-09-roca]. In 2023 they faulted the neglect of maritime security in favour of checking cars [src:isw-2023-07-17-roca].
- **Retaliation framing.** Russia presented the 10 Oct 2022 missile strike and the 18 Jul 2023 Odesa strike as retaliation [src:isw-2022-10-10-roca; pravda-2023-peskov-odesa-revenge].

## 6. Set pieces

- **The break-in, 6–15 Aug 2024.**
  - The border is breached on two axes on 6 Aug, with confirmed depth of about 10 km along the 38K-030 by 7 Aug [src:isw-2024-08-07-roca].

Through 2023, missiles and sea drones together drove most of the fleet from Sevastopol to Novorossiysk (October 2023) [src:pravda-2023-mt-anderson-bsf-novorossiysk]. Ukraine opened its own export corridor along the western coast on 16 Aug 2023 [src:pravda-2023-first-ship-corridor].

- **Date of the first bridge strike.** ISW reports 19 July [src:isw-2022-07-19-roca], while Miller gives 20 July in one article and implies 19 July in the other [src:wavellroom-2023-miller-kherson-withdrawal] [src:wavellroom-2022-miller-river-too-far].

The ORBAT figures come from open sources and Ukrainian claims, and are partly unverified.
- **Size of the Russian force and of the withdrawal.** Estimates range from 20,000 to 42,370 (see section 1).
- **Equipment losses.** There is no Kherson-specific Oryx-type count of equipment destroyed or abandoned in July–November, or of the trophies taken in November.
- **Ukrainian losses.** Ukraine has never published figures. Only unit-level anecdotes and Russian claims exist.
- **Date of the strike on the 247th Regiment and Chornobaivka.** The sources give 22 or 23 August [src:wikipedia-2022-kherson-counteroffensive].
- **Did weather force the withdrawal?** Miller argues that winter ice would have stopped ferries, but ERA5 shows no daily minimum below 0 °C through 15 November [src:wavellroom-2023-miller-kherson-withdrawal] [src:openmeteo-era5-kherson-2022]. Treat the freeze as a looming threat, not a fact of the window.
- **Paywalled sources not checked first-hand.** The Washington Post (29 Dec 2022) and NYT (Entous, 29 Mar 2025) accounts of the planning, Kovalchuk's dam test and his dismissal are cited only through Wikipedia's summary of them.
- **Coordinates.** The Darivka bridge itself was not geolocated; only the village centre is given. An Overpass query failed.

- **Ukrainian offence.** Kherson began on 29 August 2022 and drew in Russian reserves. Kharkiv followed on a thinly held front: Ukraine did not surprise Russia about its intentions, but did surprise it on timing [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons]. Ukraine advanced 75 km in four days (Balakliia, Izium, Kupiansk) against a Russian defence of "one tier" [src:euromaidan-2022-shandra-kharkiv]. At Kherson, Russia withdrew in good order across the Dnipro in October–November [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].
- **Russian response.** Russia declared mobilization, took the Dnipro as a barrier, and began building deliberate defence lines (the "Surovikin line") in Zaporizhzhia. By May 2023 its group of forces was about 420,000 strong [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].

**What Russia had.** Wagner plus mobilised convicts, with VDV support. **19,547 Wagner fighters killed in Bakhmut**, 88% of them convicts, and a similar number seriously wounded. ### Russia and the DNR
## 9. Terms
## 5. Systems and tactics in use

- **Russian assault style.** Meatgrinder describes a four-tier infantry system:
  - Disposable infantry came from DNR/LNR conscripts, Wagner convicts and under-trained mobilized men. They were first organised in companies of about 60, later in platoons of about 15, and attacked in fire teams of 2–5, with up to 5 teams on one axis.
  - The teams skirmished "often until killed". Some were shot by their own side when retreating, and Ukrainian troops report many appeared to be on amphetamines.
  - Specialised and assault troops were then sent against the Ukrainian positions this exposed [src:rusi-2023-watling-meatgrinder].
  - At Artemivske in December 2022, four UAVs flew over each assault group, covering reconnaissance, reserve routes, ambush detection and the commander's view.
- **Losses.** 19,547 Wagner fighters were killed at Bakhmut and a similar number seriously wounded. 88% of them were convicts; trained Wagner deaths averaged 40–60 a week. About 10,000 Ukrainians were killed or severely wounded in and around the city, and Russia held a 5:1 artillery advantage [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].
- **Russian penal units.** Storm-Z convict companies in regular units offered a pardon after six months and ended in August 2023. From late 2023 they were replaced by Storm-V, with no pardon and contracts lasting until the end of the war [src:ukrpravda-2024-isw-storm-v].
- **Vuhledar.** The ill-prepared January–February 2023 offensive "beginning in Vuhledar" was extremely costly. The Russian command appears to have judged it could "trade lives for time" [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].
- **Ukrainian defence.** Ukraine lost about 10,000 UAVs a month to Russian EW [src:rusi-2023-watling-meatgrinder]. Ukrainian losses turned unfavourable once Russian artillery controlled the roads into Bakhmut [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].

**Terrain.**
- *Rivers.* The Siverskyi Donets has a high right bank and a low, swampy left bank with pine forest on sandy terraces at Lyman, Kreminna and Serebrianka [src:wikipedia-siverskyi-donets] [src:kyivindependent-2022-ponomarenko-donbas-woods]. The Zherebets is "canalizing terrain" for a stable line [src:isw-2026-09-12-roca]. The Siverskyi Donets loop and the canals form a moat for Sloviansk [src:euromaidanpress-2026-vivdych-eastern-approach].
- *Woods.* The Serebrianka forest mixes forest, swamp and meadow. It was "severely damaged" over three years [src:wikipedia-serebriansky-forest]. A "Drobysheve forest area" lies north-west of Lyman [src:isw-2026-09-06-roca].
- *Ground.* Ukrainian assault groups moved "through ravines and gullies" [src:kyivindependent-2026-york-vivaldi-gains]. Heights command Nove [src:euromaidanpress-2026-mukhina-vivaldi-phase3-nove]. Treelines and windbreaks are where infiltrators shelter and where Russia bombs blind [src:isw-2026-09-25-roca].
- *Concealment.* Russians built burrow-like shelters with a single opening in dense vegetation [src:isw-2026-08-26-roca].
- *Roads.* The T-05-14 road runs Lyman–Sloviansk via Raihorodok and the T-05-13 Lyman–Siversk [src:isw-2026-09-17-roca] [src:isw-2026-09-23-roca]. The Izium–Sloviansk highway was under Russian FPV range [src:kyivindependent-2026-farrell-vivaldi].

**Command change.** Defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov was sacked in mid-July, which set off street protests. Special-operations commander Yevhen Khmara became acting minister on 16 Jul [src:euromaidanpress-2026-mukhina-khmara]. On 21 Jul Maj Gen **Mykhailo Drapatyi** replaced Syrskyi as Commander-in-Chief. Zelensky said the mid- and long-range strike programmes would continue unchanged [src:guardian-2026-murray-drapatyi].
section: 3. Per-era notes / e9-counteroffensive-26 (late Jan 2026 – present, Sep 2026)

markdown: ## 9. Terms

- **Official triumph in June.**
  - The Russian MoD praised the Southern Military District with "an uncharacteristic degree of coherency" [src:isw-2023-06-08-roca].
  - Romanchuk said the attack was telegraphed by artillery preparation. Popov credited the 58th Army's minefields [src:isw-2023-06-08-roca].
  - The MoD claimed 150 Ukrainian tanks and AFVs were used and 30 tanks destroyed, including 3 Leopards. Unofficial Russian sources stressed that Ukraine was using far more wheeled vehicles than tanks [src:euromaidan-2023-rfu-mala-tokmachka-assaults].
  - ISW called the Russian claims of destroyed vehicles "highly inflated" [src:isw-2023-06-09-roca], and DeepState said Russia recirculated the same footage from new angles [src:euromaidan-2023-shandra-leopards-mala-tokmachka].
- **Milbloggers' explanations.** They cited EW, an "unprecedented" amount of helicopter support, landmines and layered fortifications [src:isw-2023-06-08-roca], and a "strategic defense" to attrit Ukraine on the first line [src:isw-2023-06-15-roca]. Some prematurely declared the counteroffensive failed [src:isw-2023-06-09-roca].
- **Popov's revolt.** "The armed forces of Ukraine couldn't break through our army on the frontline; we were hit from behind by our highest boss" [src:politico-2023-camut-popov-fired]. Milbloggers called him "intelligent" and "competent", and none disputed his complaints [src:isw-2023-07-13-roca]. In 2025 he was jailed for stealing metal meant for the very fortifications his army defended [src:kyivindependent-2025-fornusek-popov-jailed].
- **Alarm in August.** Milbloggers wrote of exhausted, unrotated units [src:isw-2023-08-25-roca], called the situation at Verbove "very dangerous" [src:isw-2023-08-29-roca], and worried about the Robotyne–Verbove line [src:isw-2023-08-28-roca]. Shoigu called Zaporizhzhia "the tensest" direction [src:isw-2023-09-05-roca].
- **Denial in September.** A Kremlin-affiliated milblogger insisted the "Surovikin" line west of Verbove was unbroken [src:isw-2023-09-22-roca]. "Storm Ossetia" and "Alania" called breakthrough reports false [src:isw-2023-09-28-roca]. Russian sources later credited the Ka-52 with disrupting the early assaults [src:isw-2023-09-28-roca].
- **Claimed totals.** Shoigu claimed over 90,000 Ukrainian killed and wounded, almost 600 tanks and about 1,900 armoured vehicles across the counteroffensive. ISW called this "implausible" [src:isw-2023-10-30-roca].
- **Western analysis.**
  - RUSI calls the e5 defence "textbook" (three belts, rotated regiments, cached ammunition, Lancets and helicopters, early glide bombs) [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].
  - Kofman and Lee note that, unlike in Kherson in 2022, Russia manned its forward positions most heavily [src:warontherocks-2023-kofman-lee-three-months].

**Russia: Western Group of Forces**, responsible for the Kupiansk, Borova and Lyman directions; Lyman was its main effort [src:isw-2026-09-26-assessment].
- *20th CAA* (Moscow MD; Lt Gen Roman Yurchenko, reportedly dismissed) was focused north of Lyman [src:isw-2026-09-12-roca] [src:isw-2026-09-16-roca]:
  - *144th Motor Rifle Division* (MRD): its 283rd MRR [src:isw-2026-06-11-roca], its 856th SP Artillery Regiment and its 1032nd Logistics Battalion [src:isw-2026-09-30-roca], and probably the 254th MRR [src:euromaidanpress-2026-mukhina-atesh-voronezh-rail];
  - *3rd MRD:* the 99th SP Artillery Regiment and the 217th Tank Regiment [src:isw-2026-09-16-roca];
  - *2nd MRD:* elements were "encircled" [src:euromaidanpress-2026-axe-lyman-salient-trap]. MWI names the "2nd and 14th" MRDs [src:mwi-2026-rose-vivaldi]. ATESH names the 1st and 15th Guards regiments [src:euromaidanpress-2026-mukhina-atesh-voronezh-rail].
- *25th CAA* (Central MD) was attacking Lyman itself, including the 11th Tank Brigade near Ozerne [src:isw-2026-09-12-roca] [src:isw-2026-08-18-roca].
- *Assault detachments of the 1st Guards Tank Army* reinforced after Vivaldi and took "critical losses" on the roads in [src:euromaidanpress-2026-zoria-vivaldi-targeting].
- *Rubikon* (Center for Advanced Unmanned Technologies) detachments were attrited, then withdrawn [src:kyivindependent-2026-farrell-rubicon-vivaldi].
- *Russian drone units in the sector* were at 70–90% strength [src:euromaidanpress-2026-zoria-vivaldi-targeting].
- *Strength:* "at least six Russian regiments" faced Lyman [src:euromaidanpress-2026-axe-lyman-salient-trap]. Rybar says the "concentration of units… in the salient remained relatively low" [src:twz-2026-altman-vivaldi]. Trehubov: no elite units were sent, only new recruits [src:isw-2026-08-18-roca].
**Key locations.** Coordinates are OSM place nodes [src:osm-overpass-2026-c09-places]. Elevations are SRTM 30 m [src:opentopodata-srtm30m]. Distances are great-circle from Robotyne.
## 7. Decision points

**What Ukraine had.** Pre-war stocks, plus rapid Western light anti-armour and MANPADS deliveries (Javelin, NLAW, Stinger) and Bayraktar TB2s. US deliveries over the whole war reached more than 10,000 Javelins, 10,000 TOWs and 3,000 Stingers, but the fact sheet gives totals rather than arrival dates [src:state-2025-us-security-cooperation-ukraine]. Ukraine kept **artillery parity for about the first six weeks**, until its ammunition ran short [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons]. "From April, the West became Ukraine's strategic depth" [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons]. The first Western 155 mm guns arrived at the very end of the era: Canada announced its M777s delivered on 23 Apr 2022, "in conjunction with our American Allies" [src:ukrinform-2022-canada-m777].
section: 3. Per-era notes / e1-invasion (24 Feb – early Apr 2022)

markdown:
- The Orlan-10 was the Russian workhorse. Russian units with their own UAVs could fire within 3–5 minutes of detection, against 20–30 minutes when the request went through a fire-control headquarters. Even so, Russia did not have enough Orlans to sustain its loss rate in Donbas [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons].
- **Army of Drones** (Armiia Droniv) launched in July 2022, run by UNITED24, the General Staff and the Ministry of Digital Transformation. Within 9 months it had contracted 3,200 UAV complexes (over UAH 4bn, about $107m) and trained 7,000+ operators [src:pravda-2023-fedorov-army-of-drones].

Per era (computed net Russian change): e2 (May–Aug 2022) +3,782; e3 (Sep–Nov 2022) −17,533, with 18,256 recaptured; e4 (Dec 2022–May 2023) +703; e5 (Jun–Nov 2023) −441; e6 (Dec 2023–Jul 2024) +989, about 124 a month; e7 (Aug 2024–Mar 2025) +3,037, about 380 a month; e8 (Apr 2025–Jan 2026) +3,928, about 393 a month; e9 (Feb–Sep 2026) +620, about 78 a month, against 444 km² recaptured. Russian-held territory including the pre-2022 zone rose from 107,553 km² (end 2022) to 116,195 km² (27 Sep 2026), about 19.3% of Ukraine; DeepState's own total at the end of 2025 was 116,165 km² against the computed 115,330 [src:euromaidan-2026-tril-2025-4336]. The routed Radio Svoboda figures (450–550 km² a month at the 2025 peak, 27 in July 2026) fit the series for May–Aug 2025 (439–564) but not for July 2026, where DeepState's own report and the computation both give 36 [src:euromaidan-2026-tril-cost-per-km].

## 2. Timeline
**Defining features.** Russia's firepower-driven attrition against a Ukraine short of ammunition. Glide bombs "gave the VKS teeth" without air superiority [src:rusi-2025-watling-third-year].

- **DeepStateMap is the reference.** It is Ukrainian, run by the DeepState UA NGO, fed largely by Ukrainian military sources, and deliberately published 2–3 days late for operational security [src:wikipedia-deepstatemap-live] [src:kyivindependent-2025-farrell-front-line-mapping]. Its visual grammar is simple. Semi-transparent area fills show control status (occupied, liberated, recently liberated, unknown/grey, pre-2022 occupied). Point icons mark Russian units, airfields and HQs, and arrows show "directions of attack" [src:deepstate-api-history]. Ukrainian positions are never shown [src:kyivpost-2025-ashcroft-inside-deepstate].
- **ISW/CTP is the Western reference.** Its legend is epistemic rather than just territorial. It separates *assessed* (evidence-backed) from *claimed* (asserted, unverified) and, since December 2025, draws a dedicated *infiltration areas* layer [src:isw-arcgis-control-of-terrain]. Most Western outlets (e.g., the BBC) redraw ISW/CTP data [src:bbc-2022-ukraine-in-maps].
- **The front line has stopped being a line.** From 2025 on, drone "kill zones" and infiltration by small Russian groups turned the grey zone from a thin no-man's-land into a deep contact zone with overlapping positions. That forced DeepState (2026) and ISW (Dec 2025) to redefine their uncertainty categories [src:onlineua-2026-deepstate-legend] [src:kyivindependent-2025-farrell-front-line-mapping] [src:warontherocks-2026-maurin-front-line]. This is directly relevant to eras e8-drone-kill-zone and e9-counteroffensive-26.
- **Mapping is political.** DeepState has clashed publicly with Ukrainian commanders over encirclements and breakthroughs (Makarivka, Dec 2024; Dobropillia, Aug 2025). Flag-planting photo-ops by both sides are an information-war tactic that careful mappers refuse to map [src:devua-2024-deepstate-makarivka] [src:kyivindependent-2025-farrell-front-line-mapping].
- **Tactical UIs are a different world.** Delta (MoD situational awareness), Kropyva (Army SOS artillery/mapping tablet app), and the "Vezha" drone-stream module with Avengers AI are the Ukrainian military's own digital layers [src:wikipedia-delta] [src:militarnyi-2022-delta-unveiled] [src:forbes-2022-hambling-kropyva]. The Army of Drones Bonus "e-points" system turned video-verified strikes into a points economy with unit leaderboards and a marketplace [src:kyivpost-2026-korshak-epoints] [src:defensenews-2026-ruitenberg-epoints] [src:united24-2026-petriv-army-of-drones].
- **One consistent territory metric exists.** DeepState's undocumented history endpoint serves the full GeoJSON of every map version since 3 April 2022. Differencing month-end versions reproduces DeepState's own published monthly figures to within a few km² in most months, and gives Russian gains and Ukrainian recaptures separately (§2.7) [src:deepstate-api-history] [src:euromaidan-2026-tril-2025-4336].
- **Data rights are the main blocker.** DeepState has no documented API or open licence, although undocumented JSON endpoints exist and community scrapers use them. ISW's ArcGIS layers are public but carry "exclusive intellectual property… written consent" terms. ACLED requires a corporate licence for commercial use [src:deepstate-api-history] [src:isw-arcgis-control-of-terrain] [src:acled-eula]. GeoConfirmed's free API is scoped to "research, journalism, and analytical use", and Liveuamap allows reuse "with reference" but sells its API [src:geoconfirmed-openapi] [src:liveuamap-about-terms]. Only the symbology renderer milsymbol is permissively (MIT) licensed [src:github-milsymbol].
### e8-drone-kill-zone (Mar 2025–Jan 2026)
## 8. Media

- **HIMARS/GMLRS against bridges.** GMLRS reaches about 80 km [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons], with a CEP "less than a meter" [src:militarnyi-2023-kozatskyi-himars-year]. Ukraine fired small salvoes at the same aim point: 8 rockets on 20 Jul, 7 at Darivka and the dam about 22 Jul, and 8 + 2 on 26–27 Jul. This cratered the deck rather than dropping spans, and the strikes were repeated whenever repairs began [src:wavellroom-2022-miller-river-too-far] [src:isw-2022-07-27-roca] [src:isw-2022-08-25-roca]. TWZ reports that Ukraine deliberately hit only one small segment of the road bridge so that it could be repaired after liberation [src:twz-2022-newdick-antonivskyi-bridge]. Russian claims of interceptions (10 on 27 Jul, 44 on 30 Jul) are not borne out by footage [src:isw-2022-07-27-roca] [src:isw-2022-08-30-roca].
- **HIMARS against depots, HQs and trains.** Strikes hit the Kherson base on 10 Jul, the Nova Kakhovka depots, Radensk, the Brylivka train on 30 Jul, Chornobaivka, VDV regimental command posts on 1 Sep, and repair bases [src:isw-2022-07-12-roca] [src:wikipedia-2022-kherson-counteroffensive] [src:isw-2022-07-31-roca] [src:isw-2022-09-01-roca] [src:isw-2022-10-22-roca]. 8–12 launchers wrecked most Russian depots in the south and Donbas within weeks, and depots moved beyond about 85 km [src:kyivindependent-2022-ponomarenko-himars]. The US counted 400+ HIMARS targets by 8 Sep [src:defenseone-2022-tucker-milley-himars]. After the strikes Russia could no longer stockpile ammunition beside its guns [src:rusi-2023-watling-meatgrinder].
- **Supporting precision.** Ukraine reportedly also used Excalibur and possibly Vulcano 155 mm rounds against crossings and depots [src:wavellroom-2022-miller-river-too-far] [src:wavellroom-2023-miller-kherson-withdrawal], and HARM against air defence (Russia claimed HARMs shot down over the bridge on 1 Sep) [src:forbes-2022-axe-attacking-everywhere] [src:isw-2022-09-01-roca].
- **Russian counters to interdiction.**
  - Radar reflectors on the bridges [src:isw-2022-07-31-roca].
  - Rapid deck repair, which was struck again each time [src:isw-2022-08-25-roca].
  - Pontoon ferries manoeuvred by river boats at up to six sites [src:wavellroom-2022-miller-river-too-far].
  - Repaired barges, then a barge bridge, then civilian ferries and barges commandeered from Kherson port, which were hard to target [src:isw-2022-08-21-roca] [src:isw-2022-10-22-roca] [src:wavellroom-2023-miller-kherson-withdrawal].
  - A fuel pipeline along the rail bridge [src:wavellroom-2023-miller-kherson-withdrawal].
  - Moving logistics deeper, to repair yards at Kalanchak and a new base about 70 km southeast of Kherson [src:isw-2022-10-13-roca] [src:isw-2022-11-12-roca].
Drones went from being scarce and quickly lost to being the main killer on the battlefield.
### e4-bakhmut (Dec 2022 – May 2023)

Bakhmut was a salt-and-gypsum city of about 70–75,000 people on the Bakhmutka river. It lay at the junction of the roads from Sloviansk (M03), Siversk (T0513) and Kostiantynivka (T0504) [src:bbc-2022-bachega-zelensky-visits-bakhmut] [src:bbc-2023-landale-gozzi-bakhmut-deputy-mayor] [src:isw-2023-01-07-roca] [src:isw-2023-03-07-roca]. From early July 2022 Russia relied on the Wagner Group to carry the attack on it [src:isw-2023-01-31-roca] [src:isw-2023-02-15-roca].
### e7-kursk-pokrovsk (Aug 2024–Mar 2025)
## 9. Sources

- **Three phases with different player verbs.**
  - *Act 1 (one day):* a survival and morale scene with no tactical win. The scoring gate is "garrison refuses, survives the bombardment, is captured alive". Decision 2 (the *Sapfir*) is a classic trap event to script.
  - *Act 2 (one afternoon and night):* a detection, timing and launch puzzle.
  - *Coda (about 10 weeks, compressed):* an interdiction board where the player cuts supply rather than storms the island.
- **Act 2 mechanics.** All are sourced:
  - Neptune's radar horizon is about 18 km, but a weather modifier lets it reach about 120 km under low cloud [src:pravda-2022-romaniuk-moskva-neptune].
  - The salvo is two missiles with about 6 min flight [src:pravda-2022-romaniuk-moskva-neptune].
  - The cruiser's AD readiness is a hidden state [src:navalnews-2022-ozberk-moskva-negligence]. Cloud also blinds TB2s and optical satellites [src:pravda-2022-romaniuk-moskva-neptune].
  - The target can be confirmed by US/NATO input or not, and the debrief shows the dispute [src:nbc-2022-dilanian-us-intel-moskva].
  - The TB2 "decoy" should be an optional, contested modifier, not a requirement [src:forbes-2022-hambling-bayraktar-moskva].
- **Sinking model.** Two hits on a ship expected to need six or more [src:kyivpost-2023-tuzov-neptune-moskva]. The damage chain is fire, then AK-630 or Vulkan ammunition, then a tow in sea state 3, then a roll [src:intentpress-2025-neizhpapa-moskva-details] [src:guardian-2022-roth-moskva-photos]. Overnight pacing: about 11–13 h from launch (14:10 or about 16:00) to sinking (about 03:00) [src:pravda-2023-pohorilov-neptune-launch-video] [src:wikipedia-sinking-of-the-moskva].
- **Coda win band.** Russia abandons the island, with "no Ukrainian landing needed" and "assault fails" both historical.
  - Historical Russian attrition: about 4 Raptors, 1 Serna, multiple Tor/Pantsir/Strela-10, 1 Mi-8, 1 tug [src:navalnews-2022-sutton-tb2-ghost-snake-island] [src:navalnews-2022-ozberk-vasily-bekh] [src:ukrinform-2022-invaders-escape-snake-island].
  - Ukrainian costs: 1 Mi-14, about 10 assault troops and a boat, 1 Su-24MR [src:ppu-2024-bedzai] [src:pravda-2022-romaniuk-zmiinyi-battle] [src:wikipedia-snake-island-campaign].
  - Penalise holding the island with troops, which is not historical [src:pravda-2022-romaniuk-zmiinyi-battle].
- **Logistics as the target.** The island's supply should be a meter fed only by small craft and tugs. Each kill raises Russia's "cost to hold" until withdrawal triggers [src:zavhorodnii-2025-battles-snake-island] [src:dod-2022-vergun-snake-island-retreat]. After the *Moskva* is gone, Russian AD "umbrella" coverage drops to point defence only [src:navalnews-2022-sutton-curse-snake-island].
- **Artillery from the delta.** Guns at maximum range (40 km) move by pontoon at night (3–4 h each way). Metal decoys add radar noise, and the guns break down [src:militarnyi-2023-bohdana-snake-island].
- **Pacing.** Act 1 runs about 16 h of real events (03:00 to about 19:00); Act 2 about 11–13 h; the coda covers 15 Apr – 30 Jun with spikes on 2–8 May, 17 Jun and 20–30 Jun.

On 20 November 2025 Gerasimov told Putin that Kupiansk had been taken [src:isw-2025-11-21-roca]. By then Ukraine's counter-operation had already been running for weeks. Khartiia's search-and-destroy group and the Kupiansk Tactical Group cleared the forests and villages to the north, then pushed to the Oskil, cut the pipeline route and hunted the infiltrators building by building [src:ukrpravda-2026-kyrylenko-kupiansk-is-yours] [src:isw-2025-12-13-roca]. On 12 December Zelensky filmed himself at the town's entrance sign, and Khartiia announced that about 200 Russians were encircled inside [src:isw-2025-12-12-roca]. On 13 December the 429th "Achilles" regiment released video of the pipeline being blown with about three tonnes of explosives [src:defenseexpress-2025-achilles-pipeline-destroyed].
